1) Check the locomotor movements (walking, marching, fast walking, skipping, crab walking, etc.) given by music, screen and voice.
2) While the music plays, move freely around the space using the instructed movement.
3) When the whistle sounds with a "FREEZE" signal or voice, stop immediately and hold a frozen pose.
4) When a new instruction comes, switch to that movement and keep traveling to build body control.
디스 오어 댓 봄맞이 타바타 운동
This or That Spring Tabata Workout

1) Two spring-themed choices appear on screen (for example, flying a kite vs. going for a walk, or jump rope vs. jumping jacks).
2) Pick the one you like better, then check the exercise shown below that choice.
3) While the 30-second timer runs, do your chosen exercise with effort.
4) Choose again each round and keep going through a variety of full-body exercises.
디스 오어 댓 여름 에디션 타바타 활동
This or That Summer Edition Tabata Activity

1) Choose the one you like better from the two summer-activity options on each screen.
2) A moment later, see the exercise assigned under each choice (toe touches, running in place, push-ups, etc.).
3) Follow the countdown timer and do your chosen exercise for 30 seconds.
4) Go through the set rounds in order to build cardio endurance and full-body strength together.
별도의 교구 없이 화면(스크린)만 있으면 맨손으로 진행 가능

1) When a simple addition problem appears on screen, work out the answer in your head within the 10-second limit.
2) Each answer choice has a different character exercise next to it (stretching, jumping jacks, running, etc.).
3) Copy the exercise that matches the answer you calculated and keep moving during the countdown.
4) When time is up, the correct answer and a check mark appear so you can check it, then move on to the next problem.
No equipment needed; just a screen and bare hands
농구 테마 둘 중 하나 선택 타바타 준비운동
공 등의 도구 없이 맨손으로 참여 가능

1) Two basketball-related choices appear on screen (for example, left-hand dribble vs. right-hand dribble).
2) Check the exercise assigned next to the choice you prefer (squats, running in place, etc.).
3) Do that exercise energetically to the music for the set time.
4) When the screen changes, check the next question and exercise, and repeat in Tabata style to warm up.
No equipment needed; bare hands only
온라인 체육 수업 일일 준비운동 루틴
Daily Warm-Up Routine for Online PE Class

1) Follow the teacher's demonstration and the on-screen timer, doing each exercise in place for 30 seconds; warm up with cardio and step exercises such as jumping jacks, side leaps and boxer shuffles.
2) Loosen the upper-body joints with arm circles, the washing machine (knee-to-elbow twist), swimmer stretch and shoulder stretch.
3) Sit on the floor and build lower-body flexibility with a one-leg-extended forward fold, butterfly stretch and ankle circles.
4) Finish by strengthening major muscles with knee or toe push-ups, curl-ups and squats, 30 seconds each.
유치·저학년 줄넘기 기초 수업 (줄넘기 넘기 전 단계)
Basic Jump Rope Lesson for Kindergarten and Lower Grades (Pre-Jumping Stage)

1) Lay jump ropes out straight on the floor and practice jumping back and forth over the rope with feet together and with double bounces.
2) Straddle the rope and practice spin jumps, turning 180 degrees with each jump.
3) Without jumping, learn the rope-turning motion by swinging the arms slowly and widely behind the back so the rope lands on the floor in front of the feet.
4) Once the rope reliably lands in front of the feet, jump over it slowly, and when skilled, try continuous jumps or turning the rope backward.
Tissue Toss-and-Catch Agility and Reflex Challenge

1) Prepare one pull-out tissue (or 3 squares of toilet paper) and drop it from head height.
2) Try to snatch the falling tissue with the opposite hand below belly-button or knee height.
3) Take on variation missions such as tossing it high with one hand, spinning 360 degrees and catching it, or reaching between your legs to catch it.
4) Try harder challenges in a row, like catching it on the top of your foot or with your head without using hands, or doing a push-up after the toss and then catching it.
Box of tissues (or a roll of toilet paper), floor mat
팀 빌딩 협동 게임 강 건너기 (크로스 더 리버)
원마커(팀원 수만큼), 긴 폼 스텝/로그(또는 벤치), 섬 역할을 할 큰 매트
Team-Building Cooperation Game: Cross the River

1) Group members line up behind the start line and receive stepping stones (spot markers) and logs (step boards or boxes) matching the number of members.
2) By placing the spot markers and logs on the floor (the river) and stepping on them, every group member must reach the blue island at the midpoint or the far riverbank. The stones are very heavy, so they cannot be thrown or slid and must be placed by hand.
3) If any body part touches the floor (the radioactive river water), the whole team goes back to the start (the previous checkpoint) and begins again.
4) In later rounds, one stepping stone is removed, so teams use creative cooperative strategies such as carrying a teammate on the back or sharing one marker with both feet.
Spot markers (one per team member), long foam steps or logs (or benches), a big mat to serve as an island
신발 균형 유지하며 몸 뒤집기 챌린지

1) Lie on a floor mat, raise one leg straight up, and balance one shoe upside down on the sole of that foot.
2) Keep the sole level so the shoe does not fall, and slowly roll your torso over to a face-down position.
3) While face down, keep the shoe in place and roll the opposite way to return to the original lying position.
4) If the shoe falls, start again from the first lying position; the goal is to complete the full 360-degree roll within 1 minute.
초등 체육 훌라후프 트릭 챌린지 및 훌라 워
Elementary PE Hula Hoop Trick Challenge and Hula War

1) Each student receives a hula hoop and waits sitting inside it in an open space of the gym.
2) Practice the step-by-step challenges the teacher presents (waist spinning, spinning on the knees and standing up, neck spinning, arm spinning, jumping it like a jump rope, knee spinning, etc.) for 1 minute each; when the music stops or the signal sounds, stop without touching the hoop and listen to the explanation.
3) At the end of the lesson, choose a trick to keep practicing or play "Hula War" with a partner.
4) In Hula War, two students spin hoops at the same time and move toward each other so the hoops bump; whoever keeps their hoop going to the end without dropping it wins.
Hula hoops, cones for tidying up

1) Lay mats at both ends of the gym as swamps, split into two teams and start a dodgeball game.
2) A player hit by the other team's ball must go onto the opponent's mat (swamp); a trapped player who catches a ball thrown by a teammate without a bounce is rescued and returns to their own side.
3) If a player catches a ball thrown by an opponent directly, the thrower goes into the swamp.
4) The team that sends every opposing player into the mat swamp wins.

1) Split into two teams facing each other at opposite ends, give each member a number starting from 1, and place a scarf or towel as the "bacon" in the center of the gym.
2) When the teacher calls a number, the player with that number on each team sprints to the center.
3) A player who grabs the scarf first and returns to their own side without being tagged scores; if the grabber is tagged before reaching home, the defending team scores.
4) Call different numbers and repeat for more rounds.

1) Mark a pirate-ship defense zone in the center with cones, place beanbag "treasures" around it, and have each pirate team stand in a corner hoop.
2) One defending team stands inside the central ship while the other three teams infiltrate for 2 minutes, stealing one treasure at a time and carrying it back to their own hoop.
3) An attacker tagged by a defender inside the zone returns to the team hoop, does 5 jumping jacks, then rejoins, and any beanbag being carried goes back to its original spot.
4) When time is up, count each team's treasures, rotate the defending team and continue with the next round.

1) Each student takes off one shoe and puts it in a central circle or hoop, then lines up behind the team start line.
2) On the start signal, the first runner of each team sprints to the center, finds their own shoe and puts it on.
3) A runner who has fully put on the shoe returns to the team, high-fives the next runner and goes to the back of the line.
4) The first team whose members have all found and put on their shoes and returned wins; change the way of moving (hopping, skipping, galloping) each round.
Students' own shoes, a circle or hula hoop to mark the center

1) Place a long bench at each end of the gym; one player from each team climbs onto the bench at the back of the opposing court to start.
2) Instead of hitting opponents, each team passes the ball to their own teammate standing on the bench at the far end of the opposite court.
3) If the teammate on the bench catches the ball safely without dropping it, the passer also moves over and climbs onto the opposite bench.
4) The first team to get 5 teammates onto the bench wins the round.
2 long gym benches, foam balls or dodgeballs

1) Stand mats up to build a box (container) on the opposing court side, and lay a prison mat flat on the floor in each team's territory.
2) From their own side, students throw foam balls into the opponent's container, or cross into the opposing side to throw from close range.
3) A player tagged by an opposing defender holding a ball is trapped on the prison mat; a prisoner who catches a ball thrown by a teammate without a bounce escapes and may return, throw at a container, or shoot at a basketball hoop.
4) If the escaped player makes a basket, their team takes all the balls inside the opponent's container.
6 folding mats, foam balls or dodgeballs, basketball hoop

1) The swimmers line up on one end line while the shark (tagger) stands in the center circle zone of the court.
2) When the shark shouts "Shark Attack!", all swimmers sprint to the opposite end line, avoiding the shark.
3) A swimmer tagged on the way across sits down where they were caught and waves both arms while waiting.
4) On the next crossing, another surviving swimmer who high-fives a seated friend rescues them immediately, and they rejoin the game.
None (lines or a center line to mark the zones)

1) A thrower (it) stands in the center circle while everyone else runs clockwise around the edge of the gym dodging the ball; mats are placed in the corners as safe zones.
2) A student hit by the center thrower's ball is out, moves into the center circle and becomes another thrower.
3) The corner mats are safe zones where a hit does not count, but you may stay only 5-10 seconds and must then get out and keep running.
4) Throwers may fetch balls that roll away, but must return inside the center circle before throwing.

1) Everyone sits on the floor with eyes closed and head down while the teacher quietly walks around and taps heads to assign roles: one tap makes you a villain (tagger), two taps make you a secret agent who rescues citizens.
2) When the game starts on the signal, villains chase the fleeing citizens and tag them by hand.
3) A tagged player sits down on the spot immediately and can only get up when a secret agent comes and taps their shoulder.
4) The round ends when all the secret agents have been tagged and are sitting.

1) Place big exercise balls (power balls) in the center of the court and line up each team inside its own zone.
2) On the start signal, both teams throw foam balls (dodgeballs) at the center balls to push them over the opponent's goal line.
3) When a big ball fully crosses the opposing team's goal line, that team scores 1 point.
4) Students may step over the line briefly only to pick up a stopped dodgeball and must return to their own zone right away; balls must be released when thrown, and hitting a big ball while holding the ball is a foul.
Exercise ball (big playground ball), many dodgeballs (foam balls)

1) The kicking team waits in batting order, and the fielding team takes baseball positions such as pitcher, catcher, basemen and outfielders.
2) The pitcher rolls the ball along the ground, and the kicker kicks it and runs hard toward first base.
3) A runner is out if a fielder catches a fly ball before it touches the ground, throws to a base ahead of the runner, or tags the runner between bases by touching them with the ball held in hand.
4) A kicker who safely rounds all the bases and returns home scores 1 point; teams switch roles after 3 outs or when the batting order is finished.
Soft kickball (softball or foam ball), 4 rubber bases (or mats)

1) Set an end zone at each end of the field; the defending team starts in the middle of the field and the attacking team gathers in its own end zone.
2) Before starting, the attackers huddle and secretly pass a small eraser to one teammate, hiding it from the defenders.
3) On the signal, all attackers scatter and sprint toward the opposite end zone, dodging the defenders' tags; a tagged player sits down on the spot.
4) After the play ends, if any player who safely reached the far end zone is holding the real eraser, the attacking team scores 1 point.
1 pencil eraser (optional: tag belts or flags)

1) Make four helipads (landing zones) from 16 cones in four colors, 4 of each; two taggers holding pool noodles stand in the middle while everyone else waits at any helipad they choose.
2) When the teacher calls a move signal such as "Green helipad moves to orange," students in that zone must travel without being tagged.
3) A student tagged while traveling goes back to the helipad they just left.
4) The teacher keeps calling moves between zones one after another to continue the activity.
16 cones (4 each of 4 colors), 2 pool noodles
색상별 콩주머니(색상당 4개씩), 플라잉디스크(또는 덮개용 플라스틱 볼) 16개

1) Scatter colored beanbags on the floor, cover each with a flying disc or ball, and divide students into 4 teams by beanbag color, lined up in single file.
2) On the start signal, the first runner of each team runs out and lifts a cover to check whether it is a beanbag of their own team's color.
3) If it is their color, bring it back to the team; if not, cover it up again and return.
4) The next runner continues, and the first team to collect all the beanbags of its color wins.
Beanbags in four colors (4 per color), 16 flying discs (or plastic balls as covers)

1) Students scatter around the whole space, and each gets a unique number starting from 1.
2) The caller throws the ball up and shouts one number; that student runs to get the ball while everyone else runs far away.
3) When the student with the ball shouts "Stop," everyone freezes on the spot; the ball holder calls out S-P-U-D at a chosen player, takes 4 steps toward them, then throws to hit them.
4) After a hit or a miss, throw the ball up again and call a new number to continue the game.

1) Mark a jail zone with a line on one side of the court, place a freedom cone at a set distance, and scatter foam balls on the floor.
2) Choose 2-4 taggers; the other runners dash around the play area avoiding them.
3) A student tagged by a tagger is trapped in the jail zone.
4) A free student picks up a foam ball, goes to the freedom cone and throws a pass to a friend in jail; if the friend catches it safely without a bounce, they escape from jail.
Several foam balls, cones (for the freedom cone)

1) Set a start line and a finish line, and divide students into groups of about 5.
2) Each group member keeps one hand on a hula hoop, and the group runs together toward the finish line on the signal.
3) When the teacher shouts "Shipwreck!", the group drops the hoop on the floor and all members race to jump inside it; the first team with everyone inside scores 1 point.
4) Resume running and repeat the process; the team that crosses the finish line first earns bonus points.

1) Stand a mat up in a square in the center of the gym to make a goal target, and scatter spot markers around it.
2) One student goes inside the mat target to bounce the balls back out.
3) The other students pick up foam balls at the spot markers and shoot basketball shots into the standing mat.
4) The student inside pops each ball back out in all directions like popcorn, while the others move between markers, collect scattered balls and keep practicing shooting with correct form.
1 mat, spot markers, several foam balls
배구공 여러 개, 배구 네트(또는 라인)

1) Split into two teams on either side of the net, with team members waiting seated on the floor on the opposite side of the court.
2) Each team first chooses one server to stand on the serving line across the net.
3) The server serves toward a teammate seated on the floor across the net; if the seated teammate receives the ball accurately before it touches the ground, that student stands up, moves to the serving line and becomes a new server.
4) The team in which every member has received a serve and become a server wins.
Several volleyballs, volleyball net (or a line)
없음 (필요 시 코트 구획용 라인 또는 콘)

1) Runners scatter inside a set area (such as half a court) while everyone else lines up in single file at the start line.
2) On the whistle, the first student in line becomes the tagger and dashes into the area.
3) The tagger tags as many runners as possible during about 10 seconds; tagged students go to the back of the waiting line for their next turn.
4) When the whistle blows after 10 seconds, taggers switch quickly and the next student in line comes in as the new tagger.
None (lines or cones to mark the court area if needed)
훌라후프 8개, 콘(또는 깃발 등 열쇠 역할을 할 도구) 8개

1) Place 8 hula hoops in the play area as houses, with one student guarding a key (cone) in each house.
2) The other students are thieves who roam between the houses and try to steal the keys inside.
3) A thief tagged by a homeowner while trying to steal a key immediately moves on to another house and tries again.
4) A thief who steals a key without being tagged swaps roles with the homeowner; the new homeowner guards the key and the former homeowner becomes a thief.
8 hula hoops, 8 cones (or flags or other items to serve as keys)

1) Divide a basketball court in half so each team stays in its own territory and cannot leave it.
2) Players pass or move the ball by rolling it; once holding the ball, a player must pass or roll it within 10 seconds.
3) Rolling the ball across the opposing team's end line scores 1 point; as an option, set up cones behind the end line and award extra points for hitting or knocking them over.
4) When the ball goes out of the court, the first student to reach it raises a hand to claim possession and restarts by rolling it to a teammate.
테니스공 다수, 배구공 3개 이상, 라바콘 3개 이상

1) Split the gym in half with a team on each side, and make targets on the center boundary line by placing a volleyball on top of each cone.
2) Give every student one tennis ball and, on the start signal, throw at the targets in front of the opposing team.
3) The first team to knock off all the volleyballs on the cones by hitting them with balls wins.
4) When going to the center zone to retrieve scattered balls, avoid getting hit, and bring each retrieved ball back to your own throwing zone before throwing.
Many tennis balls, 3 or more volleyballs, 3 or more cones
사다리 타깃 1세트, 볼로볼 6개, 팀 조끼 2색상, 점수판 1개

1) Line up in teams, put on team pinnies, and set up the 3-tier ladder target at a designated throwing distance.
2) One player from each team steps up to the starting line and tosses 3 bolas toward the ladder target within 30 seconds.
3) Score 3 points for the top blue rung, 2 points for the middle red rung, and 1 point for the bottom white rung, earning 1 bonus point if all three land on the same rung or across all three distinct rungs, racing to reach exactly 21 points.
4) If a team exceeds 21 points their score drops back to 15 points, or modify the game for younger students by playing a simple highest-total-score format after everyone throws.
1 ladder target set, 6 bolas, 2 colors of team pinnies, 1 scoreboard
토스볼 타깃판 1개, 토스볼 6개, 팀 조끼 2색상, 점수판 1개

1) Line up in teams wearing pinnies and mark a throwing line 3 to 5 meters away from the target mat on the floor.
2) Decide the throwing order with rock-paper-scissors, and players take turns rolling or tossing the weighted toss balls toward the target.
3) Tally the points where the balls come to rest, counting borderline balls toward the closer area, to calculate the team total score.
4) Use an arithmetic math mat requiring 2 numbers and 1 operator symbol to calculate scores, or switch to a race to reach 50 points first.
1 toss ball target mat, 6 toss balls, 2 colors of team pinnies, 1 scoreboard
티볼 배트 2개, 티볼 공 3개, 배팅 티 1대, 본루 및 루 베이스 1세트(안전 1루 복식 베이스 포함), 팀 조끼 2색상, 점수판 1개

1) Set up home plate and bases on the field with a double safety base at first base, dividing students into two teams of 7 to 10 players.
2) Batters hit the ball off the batting tee within 10 seconds using a level, downward, or upper swing and run toward first base.
3) Whenever a hit lands in fair territory, base runners advance around the bases to score 1 point each time they safely cross home plate.
4) Switch offense and defense after all batters in the lineup have batted once through 3 innings, or adjust outfield fielders based on class size.
2 tee-ball bats, 3 tee-balls, 1 batting tee, 1 base set (with dual first base), 2 colors of team pinnies, 1 scoreboard
피구공(또는 4호 소프트 발리볼) 1개, 팀 조끼 2색상, 점수판 1개, 라인 테이프/콘

1) Divide the court into infield and outfield zones, send one starting outfielder to the opposing side, and put on team pinnies.
2) Start the match with a center jump ball, and the team gaining possession must throw or pass within 5 seconds to hit opposing infielders.
3) Players hit in the infield immediately move to the outfield to attack from behind, and the team with more infielders left after 5 minutes wins each set in a best-of-three match.
4) Restrict teams to a maximum of three consecutive passes before attacking, or adapt the game for younger students using size 4 soft foam balls.
1 official dodgeball (or size 4 soft volleyball), 2 colors of team pinnies, 1 scoreboard, boundary markers
키즈런 세트 1세트(스피드래더, 허들, 크로스홉 매트, 유소년 투창, 보텍스 공, 표적판, 바톤 링, 매트), 팀조끼

1) Set up stations for speed ladder, hurdle relay, cross hop, squat forward jump, javelin, and target throw across the gym.
2) Team members rotate through stations performing runs, jumps, and throws safely with foam equipment.
3) Teams accumulate points based on race times, jump counts, total distance, and target accuracy.
4) Conclude the session with the Formula One obstacle course relay combining tumbling, hurdles, and slalom sprinting.
1 Kids Run athletic set (speed ladder, mini hurdles, cross-hop mat, foam javelin, vortex balls, target mat, baton rings, gym mats), team pinnies
프리테니스 라켓 2~4개, 전용 고무공 1~2개, 미니 네트 1개, 점수판 1개, 팀조끼

1) Set up a 7m by 3m (4m for doubles) court with a 40cm net, rackets, and rubber balls.
2) Determine serve by rock-paper-scissors and serve diagonally behind the baseline after one bounce.
3) Players hit the ball on a single bounce alternately into the opponent's court to score in a best-of-three 11-point match.
4) If tied at 10-10, play continues until a 2-point lead, or adjust match targets to 15 or 21 points.
2 to 4 freetennis rackets, 1 to 2 soft rubber balls, 1 mini net (height 40cm), 1 scoreboard, team pinnies
스피드민턴 라켓 2~4개, 스피더(셔틀콕) 2~3개, 윈드링, 코트 라인 마커 8개, 점수판 1개, 팀조끼

1) Mark two 5.5m square courts separated by a 12.8m gap without any net in between.
2) Players serve from the 2.5m back service zone using an underhand or smash stroke toward the opposite square.
3) Serves alternate every 3 points regardless of score, scoring by landing the speeder inside the opposing square.
4) Play a best-of-three match to 16 points, utilizing wind rings for windy outdoors or speedlights for night play.
2 to 4 speedminton rackets, 2 to 3 speeder shuttles, wind rings, 8 court marker lines, 1 scoreboard, team pinnies
플라잉디스크 4개, 윷판 1대, 게임 말판 1개, 팀 조끼

1) Set a throwing line 3 meters from the Yut board, wear team bibs, and decide the throwing order via rock-paper-scissors.
2) Players take turns throwing a flying disc through the holes on the Yut board to determine how many spaces to advance their tokens on the game board.
3) Catching an opponent's token or hitting Yut/Mo grants a bonus throw up to three times, taken from 1 meter further back.
4) The team that successfully guides all four tokens around the game board back to start wins the match, with throwing distances adjustable by skill level.
4 flying discs, 1 Yut target board, 1 game board, team vests

1) Two holders pull both ends of a 40–50 meter rope baton taut, and runners wearing team bibs line up behind the starting line.
2) The first runner grips the sliding baton attached to the rope and sprints along the track around the cones.
3) The runner must firmly strike the plastic touch peg at the end to make an audible sound, officially passing the baton turn.
4) The relay can be modified into one-way sprint, shuttle run, or a 4-sided square track depending on space and group size.

1) Set up the Velcro target board, mark a throwing line 3 to 5 meters away based on skill level, and wear team bibs.
2) Players take turns throwing Velcro hook balls to stick them onto specific numbered target sections.
3) Teams score points through highest total score, hitting designated assigned numbers, or forming lines on a bingo sheet.
4) The game can be varied by adding physical challenges such as throwing on one foot, with the non-dominant hand, or backwards.
1 hook ball target board, 6 hook balls, 1 scoreboard, team vests
폼볼 1개, 오름판 1개, 스트라이크존 매트 1개, 베이스 4개, 팀 조끼, 점수판 1개

1) Set up the ramp, strike zone, and bases, then divide players into two teams to assign kicking and fielding.
2) The pitcher rolls the ball up the ramp in a bowling motion, and the kicker kicks the bouncing ball before it hits the ground.
3) Kickers advance around bases to score runs on safe hits, while the fielding team switches sides after making three outs.
4) Adjust the pitching distance according to skill level and use the center perfect strike zone rule for added challenge.
1 foam ball, 1 kicker ramp, 1 strike zone mat, 4 bases, team vests, 1 scoreboard
빅발리볼 공 1개, 배드민턴 네트 1개, 팀 조끼, 점수판 1개

1) Set up a net on a badminton doubles court and divide players into two teams of 4 to 6 wearing vests.
2) Start play from behind the service line using an underhand hit; players may use any body part including heads and feet.
3) Teams score by sending the ball into open spaces within a maximum of five touches, winning the best 2 out of 3 sets of 15 points.
4) Modify rules by prohibiting instant one-touch returns off serves or requiring minimum passes to encourage team cooperation.
1 big volleyball, 1 badminton net, team vests, 1 scoreboard

1) Stand a fun stick upright inside a stacking cup as a target, and mark a starting throw line at an appropriate distance.
2) Players hold another foam stick and throw it forward like a javelin to knock down the standing target stick.
3) A hit only counts if struck directly in the air; any hits resulting from a bounce off the floor are considered invalid.
4) Once mastered, players step further back to increase difficulty or set up multiple target sticks like bowling pins.
