Speed Stacks cup sets (12 cups each) 2 sets, StackMats with digital timers 2 units, Stacking table 1 unit
플로어볼 경기 및 전방 압박 골 넣기 게임
플로어볼 스틱 10~12개, 플로어볼 전용 공 2~3개, 플로어볼 골대 2대, 팀 조끼, 골키퍼 보호장비 2세트

1) Both teams place floorball nets at opposite ends of the gym and position a goalkeeper alongside field players.
2) The match begins with a face-off, and players use stick blades below knee level to pass and dribble the ball forward.
3) Teams score points by intercepting loose balls through aggressive defensive pressing and shooting accurately into the net.

1) Lay exercise mats across the floor and have students warm up while sitting in a comfortable, aligned posture.

초등 농구 지역방어 돌파 및 빠른 속공 게임
Elementary Basketball Zone Defense & Fast Break Game

1) Set up two basketball hoops at opposite ends of the court and divide players into two teams of 5 wearing pinnies.

3) Secure points by executing rapid fast breaks immediately after rebounds or turnovers to finish with layups and open jump shots.

공격형 외야수 연계 정식 규격 피구 게임
Standard Floor Dodgeball with Active Outfield Play

1) Mark a rectangular court divided by a center line, assign inner and outer field positions, and align players in their zones.
2) Commence the match with a jump ball, passing the dodgeball rhythmically between infielders and outfielders to find passing lanes.
3) Eliminate opponents by striking them with the ball on the fly (targeting lower extremities), sending eliminated players to the outfield.

1) Line up in groups and practice the basic steps of the Pivot Turn, Monterey Turn, Rolling Turn, and Rock Turn to the music.
2) Form pairs and perform a continuous relay where the second student immediately follows the partner's turning movements without breaking momentum.
3) Expand into a 4-person crew to execute all four turn cycles in rhythmic succession while maintaining formation spacing to earn points.
4) Freely recombine the four turn sequences and incorporate arm or upper-body gestures to create and present an original team routine.
JSPO アクティブチャイルドプログラム
저쪽으로 점프 뿅 (방향 일치 점프 게임)

1) Two players face each other and play rock-paper-scissors to decide who calls the jump command.
2) The winner chants the trigger phrase "Jump that way, hop!" right after winning the hand.
3) On the word "hop," both players synchronously jump in one of four directions: forward, backward, left, or right.
4) If both land in the same mirror direction, the caller wins; if directions differ, they return to the start and replay rock-paper-scissors.

3) The player must jump sequentially through 1, 2, and 3 without skipping any hoops along the route.
4) The fastest player to reach the finish line wins, and it can be expanded into team relays or odd/even selective jumping challenges.
12-15 mini hoops, floor chalk or boundary markers
JSPO アクティブチャイルドプログラム

1) Mark team zones A, B, and a center draw zone C on the ground, then divide players into three teams.
2) Teams A and B begin tugging on opposite sides of the rope while Team C observes from the side.
3) Team C runs in to assist whichever team is currently losing to balance out the rope.
4) When time expires, points/victory go to whichever team owns the active mark zone.
JSPO アクティブチャイルドプログラム
아침을 여는 전교생 색깔별 대항 릴레이 달리기

1) Students across all grades gather by colored teams on the athletic track wearing team vests.

발로 콘 잡기 스쿠터 릴레이 (콘 그랩)

1) Students pair up with one sitting on the scooter board and the other standing behind to push.
2) On the start signal, the pusher navigates the scooter forward toward a target cone.
3) The rider must grasp and lift the cone using only their feet without touching it with hands.
4) The team races back to the start holding the cone and tags the next pair to finish first.
초등 기초 피클볼 랠리 (더블 바운스 챌린지)
피클볼 라켓 4개, 피클볼 공 2개, 미니 네트 세트 1개

1) Players set up in doubles on opposite sides of a low portable net holding pickleball paddles.
2) The server executes an underhand serve striking the ball below the navel into the diagonal court.
3) Both the serve and the return must bounce once on each side before any volley is allowed (Double Bounce Rule).
4) Players continue the rally with flat paddle strikes, scoring points when opponents commit a fault.
4 pickleball paddles, 2 pickleballs, 1 mini net set
공중 9칸 배구 게임 (나인 스퀘어 인 디 에어)
9 Square in the Air Volleyball Game

1) Nine players enter the elevated 3x3 grid structure, each occupying a designated square numbered 1 to 9.
2) The player in the center square (#9/King) serves the ball up and over the top frame into another square.
3) Players use volleyball overhead sets or hits to keep the ball airborne and direct it out of their square on one touch.
4) When a player misses or hits out of bounds, they rotate to square 1 while others move up toward the center.

1) Each student takes up to three scarves and holds the center pinch to form a ghost shape.
2) With one scarf, lift gently upward and catch on the descent using a downward palm claw catch.
3) With two scarves, practice the criss-cross X-pattern calling out 'throw, throw, catch, catch' alternately.
4) Progress to three scarves, starting with the hand holding two, maintaining a rhythm with only one scarf in the air at a time.

1) Mark a 15m or 20m running course across the gym and pair up students into two-person teams.
2) The first runner jogs across to the opposite line in sync with the audio beeps, tags their partner's hand, and switches roles.
3) Partners alternate laps to manage fatigue, with stronger runners allowed to take consecutive turns to give their partner a rest.
4) The test ends when the team fails to cross the line before the beep twice, recording the total successful laps completed.

1) Fold and create three paper airplanes and place a laundry basket or bucket 5 to 10 feet away from the throwing line.
2) Start a 1-minute timer and throw the three paper airplanes one by one from behind the throwing line toward the basket.
3) Score 1 point if an airplane hits the outside of the basket and 2 points if it lands inside, quickly retrieving and re-throwing within the time limit.
4) Adjust the challenge by moving the basket further away or using a smaller target bucket to increase difficulty.
3 paper airplanes, 1 laundry basket (or bucket), timer
미니 농구공 여러 개, 농구 골대

1) Students line up at an appropriate distance around the basketball hoops with small arcade basketballs.
2) Review and practice the four core shooting cues of B.E.E.F. (Balance, Eyes, Elbow, Follow-through).
3) Follow the leader's demonstrated form and shoot toward the back of the basketball rim.
4) As a modification for more power, students bend their knees and jump during the shot instead of standing still.
매트 10장 이상, 미니 트램펄린 1개, 뜀틀 블록 매트 세트, 점프 박스 2~4개, 평균대 2개, 콩주머니 여러 개, 암벽장 및 로프, 번호 표시 콘 8개

1) Set up eight stations across the gym including traveling mat, vault, rock wall, rope swing, balance, jump boxes, balance beam, and partner balance.
2) Divide students into small groups at each numbered station and review the challenge task cards.
3) Practice each skill while music plays, and rotate along the gym lines to the next numbered station when music stops.
4) Modify difficulty by adjusting vault mat height, jumping tricks, or balancing with a bean bag on the head based on grade level.
10+ gymnastics mats, 1 mini trampoline, stacking vault mats, 2-4 jump boxes, 2 balance beams, bean bags, climbing wall, swing ropes, 8 numbered cones
앉아 윗몸 앞으로 굽히기(좌전굴) 유연성 측정
좌전굴 측정기 1대, 신장 체중계 1대, 대기용 벤치 의자

1) Students take off their shoes and line up in orderly fashion behind the sit and reach box.
2) Sit with one leg straight against the box, the other foot flat next to the knee, and fingertips aligned together.
3) Reach forward along the measuring scale as far as possible and hold the stretch for three seconds while the teacher records the score.
4) Switch legs to complete the second trial, then move over to the scale and stadiometer for private height and weight recording.
1 sit and reach box, 1 scale and stadiometer, waiting bench

1) Divide the gym into two courts, place a mat trashcan in each backcourt, and designate one student per team as Oscar inside the trashcan.
2) Scatter foam balls (trash) across the playing area and have students pick up only one ball at a time.
3) Players throw balls into the opposing team's mat using overhand or underhand throws, while Oscar continuously tosses balls out of the can.
4) If a player crosses the center line, they step aside to recite the ABCs before returning, and the team with the least trash in their can wins.

1) Select two taggers holding pool noodles while other students scatter across the open gym space.
2) When music plays, taggers chase runners and tag them gently with their noodles to freeze them.
3) Tagged runners, runners stepping out of bounds, or those falling must stay in place doing a fist pump dance without being unfrozen.
4) The round continues until the music stops, after which new taggers are chosen to begin a new round.

1) Assign one player to each of four marked squares (1-4) and have waiting students line up behind square one.
2) The server in square 4 bounces the ball once behind the service line and strikes it underhand into another player's square.
3) Players must allow the ball to bounce once before striking it into another square; hitting inside lines, double bounces, or hitting out results in an out.
4) The eliminated player moves to the end of the waiting line, players advance up a square number toward square 4, and the next challenger enters square 1.
썬더스틱(긴 줄과 공이 달린 막대) 1개, 훌라후프 5개

1) The turner stands at the center with a thunderstick while students form a circle or stand along court boundary lines.
2) The turner sweeps the thunderstick rope along the floor in a low circle around their feet.
3) Students jump over the incoming rope with timing; anyone whose foot gets struck by the rope is temporarily out.
4) Eliminated students move to an outside station to hula hoop or jog until a final winner remains to reset the game.
1 thunderstick (stick with cord and ball), 5 hula hoops

1) Position two rope turners while students line up single file facing the entry side of the long jump rope.
2) Turners rotate the rope outward from the runners, and students continuously enter the rope the moment the runner ahead leaps.
3) Each student performs exactly one jump and exits smoothly; touching the rope or letting the rope complete an empty turn results in elimination.
4) Eliminated students move to a secondary practice rope to keep active, while top finalists from multiple heats advance to a championship round.

1) Each student spreads out across the gymnasium with one soccer ball ready to dribble.
2) When designated bumpers approach playing light defense, students shield and protect the ball with their body.
3) If a student's ball is bumped out of bounds, they perform 5 push-ups before returning to play.
4) Bumpers pass the role to a quiet hand-raising student to rotate defenders while keeping defense intensity moderate.
Modified Pacer Test for Young Learners

1) Students line up spread out along the gym sideline and observe teacher demonstration laps.
2) On the starting signal, students run straight and slow across the modified short distance before the beep.
3) As test levels increase in speed, students keep pacing; making two consecutive mistakes ends their test.
4) Finished students sit down immediately to cheer silently for peers aiming for 25 to 30 total laps.

1) Adjust the jump rope length by stepping on its center so handles reach armpit height.
2) The teacher stands behind the student and guides their hands to make a big overhead circular turning motion.
3) The student waits for the rope to hit the floor in front of their feet before jumping over it.
4) Once single jumps are mastered, progress to backwards jumping and consecutive jumps of two to five reps.

1) Spread out into open space with safe personal boundaries across the room.
2) Perform four rounds of the 4-count chicken dance consisting of beaks, wings, tail feathers, and claps.
3) During the musical movement break, travel around the open area performing locomotor skills like skipping, sliding, and galloping.
4) Progress by having students square dance with partners or use ribbons and scarves during movement breaks.

1) Scatter a deck of 60 silly task cards face down inside the center circle of the gym.
2) On the start signal, students run in, grab one card, and complete the movement or social interaction challenge with peers.
3) Once completed, hand the card face up to the teacher and immediately grab another card to beat the target time.
4) When the central pile is empty, students without cards actively seek out and assist classmates still finishing tasks.
스텝 앤 푸시 농구 패스 기초 연습
Step and Push Basketball Passing Drills

1) For chest passes, stand 2 steps from a wall; for bounce passes, stand back-to-back with a partner, take 2 steps apart, and face each other.
2) Push the chest pass straight forward from chest level, and push the bounce pass toward the floor about three-quarters of the way to your partner.
3) Extend both arms with thumbs pointing down upon release, and catch incoming balls firmly using both hands.
4) Begin with individual chest passes against the gym wall, then transition into cooperative partner bounce passing practice.
초등 운동회 종목 순환 스테이션 활동
풀누들 12개, 긴줄 4개, 훌라후프 4개, 스태킹컵 4세트, 점핑 자루 4개, 라바콘 8개, 플라잉디스크 8개

1) Set up 18 diverse activity stations across the gym and field, including javelin throw, noodle tower, cup stack relay, and sack race.
2) Divide the class into squads to rotate through stations every 6 minutes upon hearing the air horn signal.
3) Teams score by throwing the farthest, building the tallest self-standing tower, or finishing relay races fastest.
4) Practice game rules with early grades first, then progress to competitive team challenges and championship throw-offs.
12 pool noodles, 4 jump ropes, 4 hula hoops, 4 cup stacking sets, 4 racing sacks, 8 cones, 8 flying discs

1) Pair students up in groups of two or three facing each other in front of a basketball hoop.
2) Both players simultaneously dribble 5 times (or slap the ball 5 times for early grades), then tap their balls together.
3) Immediately following the ball tap, both players sprint to shoot, continuing until someone successfully makes a basket.
4) The first player to score earns a point and resets to the starting mark; the first to reach 3 points wins the match.
Partner Jump Rope Tricks: Face to Face & Side by Side

1) Pair students up with one longer jump rope designated for two jumpers.
2) In 'Face to Face', one partner turns the rope while both jump together facing each other, or the second runner enters mid-turn.
3) In 'Side by Side', each partner holds one handle with their outside hand and coordinates a simultaneous swing and jump.
4) Progress from basic jumps to advanced challenges such as spinning, touching the floor, or jumping in and out of the turning rope.
빙고 학습지 학생당 1장, 마커 학생당 1개, 라바콘 1개

1) Students receive a bingo sheet and marker, then gather in the central square.
2) When music plays, ask a classmate about an adventure activity on the card (one question per person).
3) If they answer yes, have them initial the square, then run to tag the cone and jog one lap before asking another person.
4) Each classmate can sign only once, and players aim to complete 4 or 6 boxes in a row before time runs out.
Bingo sheet per student, marker per student, 1 cone
이것 아니면 저것? 균형 잡기 챌린지
개인용 매트 학급 인원수만큼, 스크린(TV 화면) 1대

1) Students sit on their mats in a pike position and view two balance options shown on screen.
2) On signal, try both balance poses within 30 seconds while engaging core muscles.
3) Hold each balance like a statue for at least 5 seconds to feel the required strength, flexibility, and stability.
4) Progress from basic balances to smaller bases of support and inverted poses, voting and discussing which was more challenging.
Gym mat per student, 1 display screen

1) Set up nine hula hoops in a 3x3 grid and place team cones with three colored scarves at the start line.
2) On go, the first runner takes one scarf, sprints forward, places it inside a hoop, and runs back.
3) The next runner can only leave the cone once tagged by the returning runner, placing another scarf strategically.
4) After all three scarves are played, subsequent runners sprint up to move one of their own scarves to an open hoop until one team aligns three in a row.
9 hula hoops, 6 scarves (3 per team), 2 cones

1) Stand at an appropriate distance facing a gym wall marked with a target area, holding a foam ball.
2) Point your non-throwing side toward the wall target and bring your throwing arm back into an uppercase L shape.
3) Step with the opposite foot, twist your torso, and throw the ball overhand at the target, catching the rebound.
4) Catch the ball off the wall three times in a row, then jog one full lap around the gym before returning for another round.
1 foam ball per student, marked wall target area

1) A small group of 3–5 students lines up facing a wall, and the first thrower hurls a tennis ball (or bouncy ball) against the wall so that it bounces back.
2) Another group member catches the rebounding ball, no matter how many times it has bounced on the floor, and immediately throws it back at the wall to keep play going.
3) A player who misses the catch must sprint and touch the wall before another player picks up the ball and hits the wall; if they get there first, they are safe.
4) Vary the difficulty and speed with underhand throws, no-bounce catches, or by adding more balls.

1) Divide players into Lion and Tiger teams and line them up facing each other along the center markers.
2) When the teacher calls out one team's name, that team turns and sprints toward their safe zone while the other team chases.
3) Players tagged before crossing the safe zone line switch to the opposing team for the next round.
4) Modify by pairing specific partners, playing touchless, or having students start from fitness positions like planks or animal crawls.

1) Divide players into two teams on a basketball court and determine initial possession with rock-paper-scissors at center court.
2) The offensive team advances by passing only without taking steps, scoring points by throwing the football into the opponent's hoop.
3) If a pass hits the floor or an airborne ball is swatted down by defenders, possession switches immediately to the opposing team.
4) Defenders must maintain a buffer of 1 to 2 feet without stripping balls from hands, with variations allowing adjusted team sizes or multiple half-courts.

1) All students start inside the basketball court boundaries while multiple dodgeballs are tossed into the playing area for a free-for-all match.
2) Players pick up balls and attempt to hit any opponent, and anyone struck by a ball must immediately exit to the outer boundary lines.
3) Out-of-bounds players remain active by retrieving balls rolling outside and throwing them at remaining players inside the court.
4) The game continues until only one survivor remains inside, with optional variations allowing outer throwers to re-enter upon scoring a hit.
엔드존 탈출 (태그 앤드 펀트 미식축구 게임)

1) Divide the court into two halves with end zones at each boundary, placing several teammates wearing flag belts into the opposite end zones.
2) Players throw football passes from their home court across to trapped teammates waiting in the opposing end zone.
3) Upon catching a pass in the end zone, that player chooses between punting the ball back for a teammate to catch or sprinting across the court without getting their flag pulled.
4) If a runner's flag is pulled they must return to the end zone, and the first team to successfully bring all end-zone teammates back wins.
Footballs 4-6, flag belts 8-10, cones 8, team pinnies

1) Divide into teams of four or five, with every player holding at least one hand on their team's hula hoop.
2) Scatter a large collection of foam balls in the center of the gym and wait for the starting whistle.
3) Move together as a unit holding the hoop and use only feet to kick and pass one ball back to your base at a time.
4) Count the collected balls or sum up point values assigned to different ball colors at the end to determine the winner.

1) Arrange four gym mats like baseball bases and divide runners so no more than three occupy a single mat.
2) Assign two taggers equipped with dodgeballs in the center while runners continuously circulate the bases forward.
3) Runners are safe while standing on a mat but can be hit by a thrown dodgeball whenever they move between mats.
4) Any runner hit becomes a tagger while the thrower becomes a runner, and an arriving runner forces the lead runner off the mat.

1) Place hula hoops with an equal number of bean bags at each corner and divide students into teams at their home bases.
2) On go, players run to steal one bean bag at a time from any opposing team's hoop and return it to their own hoop.
3) The team with the most bean bags inside their hoop at the end of the time limit wins.
4) As a variation, tag rules can be introduced so defenders can protect their hoops.

1) Divide the playing field into multiple distance zones and assign higher point values to zones further away.
2) The first player of each team stands as the thrower while the second player positions themselves in a chosen target zone to catch.
3) Successfully catching the thrown disc scores that zone's points, after which the thrower becomes the catcher and the catcher returns to the back of the line.
4) Variations include racing to a target score or switching the equipment to footballs or baseballs.
폼볼 3~4개, 볼링핀(또는 라바콘) 10~16개, 골키퍼 구역 표시용 접시콘 8개

1) Set up equal numbers of plastic pins as targets in each team's end and mark exclusive goalie zones.
2) Introduce multiple foam soccer balls for continuous passing and kicking action across the court.
3) Players shoot to knock down opposing pins; successfully downed pins are claimed and added to their own side until one team captures them all.
4) Expand to a four-corner team elimination format or vary ball counts to boost participation.
3-4 foam balls, 10-16 plastic pins (or cones), 8 marker cones

1) Divide students into teams behind the starting line and place a cone at the turning point for each team.
2) The first runner places a pool noodle between their knees without using hands and waddles around the cone.
3) Upon returning, they pass the noodle to the next teammate, and the team that finishes first wins.
4) For variations, returning runners can add teammates to hold the noodle together like a train, or try balancing it vertically on their palms while running.

1) Choose one student as the tagger (Tatanka) in the middle while the remaining players (buffaloes) line up along one end line.
2) When the center tagger shouts "Tatanka, Tatanka!", all runners sprint across to the opposite end without getting tagged.
3) Any runners tagged before reaching safety join the taggers in the middle for the subsequent rounds.
4) Continue playing as the tagger pack expands until everyone is caught, or reset with the last remaining runner as the new Tatanka.
축구공(또는 실내용 폼볼) 15~20개, 공 보관 바구니 1개

1) Scatter all students across the playing area, appoint 2–3 initial taggers with soccer balls, and place extra balls in a sideline bin.
2) Taggers dribble around and pass or gently kick their balls to tag fleeing runners strictly on their feet.
3) Any runner whose foot gets hit goes to the bin, grabs a new soccer ball, and becomes an additional tagger.
4) The game progresses as more players become taggers until everyone has been tagged, or plays as a timed survival challenge.
15–20 soccer balls (or safe foam balls), 1 ball bin

1) Students spread out across the gym as the teacher throws multiple foam balls into play.
2) Players pick up balls and throw or roll them to hit opponents strictly below the knee.
3) Any hit player must sit down immediately and can only re-enter when grabbing a different ball rolling toward them.
4) If hit while holding a ball, players must surrender it and sit, while teammates may roll balls to revive seated peers.

1) Students form a circle while objects ranging from large to small are lined up beside them.
2) Place the largest ball in the center, challenging all students to touch the object simultaneously without touching each other.
3) Once the group successfully touches the object without any body contact, replace it with the next smaller object.
4) As objects scale down to tennis balls and coins, students must strategize using single fingertips to complete the challenge.

1) Set up two goal nets facing backwards and divide students into two competing teams on the court.
2) Field players are not allowed to kick the ball and must strike or swat the ball strictly using their hands.
3) Goalies operate under reverse rules and cannot use their hands, defending the net solely with their feet and body.
4) Carrying the ball is prohibited, and teams score points by maneuvering the ball into the backward-facing nets.

1) The teacher announces a target alphabet letter and chooses one or two taggers.
2) Players scatter around the gym and taggers chase them to tag anyone they can reach.
3) Tagged players must sit down until they say aloud a word starting with the designated letter to rejoin.
4) Introduce a rule that students cannot repeat any word previously spoken to increase difficulty.

1) Place alphabet paper cards across the gym and line up teams behind the start line.
2) On start, the first runner sprints across, grabs one letter card, and returns to the team.
3) Teammates take turns running one at a time to retrieve additional letter cards for the group.
4) The first team to assemble a valid target word or score the highest point total wins.

1) Set up six cones to mark a large circle, place a bottle and rubber toys in the center, and seat groups between cones.
2) The teacher spins the bottle in the center, and the group pointed at by the bottle becomes the taggers.
3) Taggers grab rubber chickens while all other runners enter the circle area to avoid being tagged.
4) Tagged runners move to the circle perimeter to wait until all players are caught, then reset.
6 cones, 1 empty bottle, 4 rubber chickens (or foam sticks)

1) Divide the court with a volleyball net and place a hula hoop along each team's back boundary line.
2) Players pick up foam dodgeballs and continuously throw them over the net into the opponent's court.
3) If a player catches an incoming ball before it hits the ground, they store it directly into their hoop.
4) The team that collects the most caught balls into their hoop when time expires wins the round.
1 volleyball net, 10 foam balls, 2 hula hoops

1) Players line up along the end line facing away while the teacher scatters coins across the playing area.
2) On the go signal players run to locate a coin and stand directly on top of it.
3) Any players who fail to secure a coin must perform designated exercises such as push-ups or jumping jacks.
4) Remove one coin each round to gradually increase the number of students exercising until a champion remains.

1) Divide the court into two halves and set up a ball on a cone inside each three-point key with hula hoops as safe zones and corner jails.
2) Offensive players cross into the opponent's territory while evading defenders and resting safely inside the hula hoop zones.
3) Tagged players are sent to the opponent's jail and can be rescued when a teammate safely runs in and tags them.
4) Score a point by grabbing the ball and successfully carrying or passing it across the center line without being tagged.

1) Mark a throwing circle with cones in the gym center and place four folding mats standing upright along the perimeter.
2) One student starts as the thrower inside the central circle while all other runners jog in one direction around the mat course.
3) Runners can take cover behind the standing mats for up to 10 seconds before being forced to advance to the next mat.
4) Any runner hit below the waist must join the throwers in the center until all runners have been tagged out.
The Best Rock Paper Scissors Battle

1) Lay out a long line of hula hoops on the floor and designate the second-to-last hoop on each side as the scoring goal.
2) Two teams line up at opposite ends and the first runners bunny-hop forward through the hoops toward each other.
3) When runners meet in a hoop they play rock-paper-scissors, with the loser stepping out to the back of their team line.
4) The winner continues hopping forward while the losing team immediately sends their next runner, scoring a point upon reaching the opponent's goal hoop.

1) Students line up in a single file facing forward and give the lead runner a ball.
2) The entire line jogs together around the gymnasium perimeter maintaining a steady pace.
3) While moving each runner passes the ball overhead backward until it reaches the last player.
4) The last runner sprints past the line to become the new leader and teams can vary the pass between legs.

1) Divide the court into defense midfield and forward zones assigning players and goalies to each section.
2) Players must strictly stay inside their assigned zones and only play when the ball enters their area.
3) Teams score points by passing the ball through zones and kicking it into the opponent goal net.
4) Rotate players periodically between defense midfield and forward positions so everyone practices each role.

1) Designate two taggers as broken arrows and one cupid carrying mission cards while others are hearts.
2) Broken arrows chase and tag hearts turning them into frozen broken hearts standing on one foot.
3) Cupid delivers a card from the bucket to frozen players who rejoin after performing the listed exercise.
4) Taggers win if everyone is frozen or you can add extra cupids to increase game flow.

1) Pairs receive a basketball and 10 to 15 bowling pins to build custom pathways like an S pattern.
2) The first player dribbles the basketball smoothly through the obstacle pin pattern without knocking any down.
3) Partners count successful laps in a 30-second round or award points to the partner if pins fall.
4) Progress by enforcing weak-hand dribbling simultaneous pair dribbling or running it as a team relay.
폼볼 3개, 라바콘 5개, 학습 카드 80장, 정답 분류판 5개

1) Scatter 50 to 100 question cards in the center, assign one guardian team holding foam balls, and line up runners behind cones.
2) On go the lead runner sprints into the card field to grab one card while avoiding guardian tags.
3) Runners who safely return place the card onto the correct answer slot on their team board for points.
4) If tagged by a ball runners drop the card and return empty-handed, and guardians rotate each round.
3 foam balls, 5 cones, 80 question task cards, 5 team answer boards

1) Three taggers hold one hula hoop together as a jellyfish while the other runners spread out in the playing area.
2) Tagged runners freeze in place, and the jellyfish taggers lower the hula hoop over their head to the floor and lift it back up.
3) Eaten players move outside the perimeter, where they can tag any runners wandering too close to the boundary lines.
4) Every time three players are eliminated they form a new jellyfish team with a hoop until three survivors remain.

1) Two or three students start as pirates without a ball, while every other student dribbles a basketball around the gym.
2) Pirates move around the court trying to steal or knock away a basketball from any active dribbler.
3) When a player loses their ball, they immediately become a pirate and must pursue someone else's basketball.
4) Immediate takebacks from the player who just stole the ball are forbidden, and basketballs can be gradually removed to increase difficulty.
훌라후프 6~8개, 원마커(스팟) 20~30개, 펀스틱(스펀지봉) 4~6개, 물고기/미션 종이 카드 다수

1) Scatter hula hoops as fishing holes, placing paper fish and blank cards inside them covered up by poly spots.
2) Students form relay teams behind the starting line, with the first runner holding a pool noodle as a fishing rod.
3) On the whistle, one runner races out to flip over a single poly spot, retrieving the fish if found and flipping the spot back before returning.
4) Score by the total weight written on the fish, or add letter tiles, math equations, or movement penalties under the spots for creative variations.
6-8 Hula Hoops, 20-30 Poly Spots, 4-6 Pool Noodles, Paper Fish/Cards

1) Place four cones at the corners of the play area and designate four distinct locomotion movements for each boundary line.
2) All students begin traveling around the perimeter in the same designated direction (clockwise or counter-clockwise).
3) Runners perform actions like jogging and galloping along the long sides, and switch to crab walks and hopping on the short sides.
4) After several laps, reverse the running direction or swap in new locomotive movements such as side-stepping, skipping, or high knees.

1) Two teams wearing pinnies line up on opposite baselines, with one player from each team starting in the center as sharks.
2) A player rolls the foam ball to the opposite baseline who kicks it, triggering all minnows from both teams to sprint across to the other end.
3) Sharks attempt to catch the fly ball or throw the loose foam ball below the waist to eliminate fleeing minnows.
4) Minnows who are struck or hit a caught fly ball become sharks for the next round until one team's minnows are fully eliminated.
1 Foam Ball, 2 Sets of Pinnies (Team Vests)
맞불 작전 침투 구출 태그 놀이

1) Divide the play area in half, set up 2-point mats in corners and 1-point mats in the center rear, and scatter hula hoops as safe zones.
2) Players cross into the opponent's territory avoiding defenders, gaining temporary safety when inside hula hoops or point mats.
3) Tagged players must sit frozen on the spot until a teammate safely touches them, granting a free walk back to their half.
4) When the 3-5 minute round ends, everyone freezes and each team calculates total points based on players occupying the opponent's scoring mats.

1) Place numbered cones in a line across the center and have two teams line up facing each other behind their starting lines.
2) The teacher calls out a math equation, prompting the first runner from each team holding a baton to sprint toward the correct cone.
3) The runner taps the correct answer cone with the baton and races back to their team line, with the first returner scoring the win.
4) The losing team performs jumping jacks equal to the answer value, after which batons pass to the next pair for a new equation.

1) Arrange players into foosball-style rows (defenders, midfielders, forwards) with 2-4 players per row holding onto shared pool noodles.
2) Drop one or more soccer balls onto the court, requiring players in each row to slide together strictly side-to-side.
3) Teams pass the ball forward through rows and shoot into the opponent's goal using only their feet without letting go of noodles.
4) If a player lets go of the pool noodle or breaks formation to reach a ball, play halts to reattach and possession is given to the other team.

1) Mark two parallel team lines about 10 feet apart with goal lines at both back ends, having Team X and Team Y line up facing each other.
2) The teacher tosses a beanbag labeled 'X' on one side and 'Y' on the other high into the air like a coin toss.
3) Whichever letter faces up when it lands designates the chasing team, who immediately sprints to tag members of the opposing team.
4) The fleeing team tries to sprint across their back goal line to safety, and the chasing team earns one point for each runner tagged before crossing.

1) Establish safe lines at opposite ends, divide the class into two teams, and have each team secretly huddle to choose Gorilla, Man, or Gun.
2) Teams line up facing each other at the centerline, jumping into their designated pose when the teacher calls "Gorilla, Man, Gun, Shoot!".
3) According to the hierarchy (Gorilla beats Man, Gun beats Gorilla, Man beats Gun), the winning team chases the losing team.
4) Fleeing players dash toward their end safe line, and any player tagged before reaching it must join the opposing team for subsequent rounds.
등 대고 앉았다 일어서기 협동 챌린지

1) Students partner up and stand back-to-back without using their hands.
2) On the signal, partners push against each other and slowly lower themselves into a seated position without using their hands.
3) Once seated, they work together pushing back-to-back to stand completely upright again.
4) As they succeed, combine pairs into groups of four or more to attempt the same challenge together.

1) Place three hula hoops in the center as submarines with two foam balls and a captain in each, while the rest line up at one end.
2) On the go signal, runners sprint across to the other side avoiding balls rolled or thrown by the captains inside their hoops.
3) Hit runners lay down on their stomachs to become mines who can pivot in place to tag runners moving back and forth.
4) The last three surviving runners become the new captains for the next round, and the number of hoops can be varied.
패스 앤 스코어 구출 태그 놀이

1) Select two taggers with pool noodles and two freers holding foam balls, while other students scatter across the gym.
2) When tagged, a runner must freeze on the spot and raise a hand high to signal they need rescue.
3) Freers must stand stationary with the ball and throw accurate passes to frozen players; catching the pass earns 1 point for both players and frees the runner.
4) The catcher becomes the new freer, and variations include using bounce passes or switching to basketballs and footballs.
어라운드 더 월드 외곽 회전 피구

1) Four teams position in the four corners behind protective mats, while one team stands inside the center circle holding all dodgeballs.
2) On the whistle, runners from corner teams run in a set direction around the perimeter dodging balls thrown from the center.
3) Successfully completing a full loop back to the base scores one point for the team, while hit runners join the center throwers.
4) The round ends when time expires, the team with the most points wins, and the winning team rotates into the center for the next round.
8-10 foam balls, 4 exercise mats, 4 mini whiteboards
스쿠터보드 6~8대, 줄넘기 6~8줄, 플라스틱 볼링핀 6~8개, 폼볼 다수, 라바콘 4개

1) Attach skipping ropes to scooter boards, place a plastic bowling pin on each, and divide students into tugboats (pullers) and throwers.
2) Tugboats carefully pull their cargo across the gym while throwers roll or throw foam balls from side zones to knock the pins down.
3) Points are scored each time a cargo reaches the opposite wall, and players whose pins fall drop their ropes to become blockers for teammates.
4) The game can be varied by allowing throwers to kick the balls or use hockey sticks to shoot at the moving targets.
6-8 scooter boards, 6-8 jump ropes, 6-8 plastic bowling pins, foam balls, 4 cones

1) Place four exercise mats in the corners, position one tagger (the Chef) in the center, and have all other players (Gingerbread Men) lie down on the mats.
2) The Chef calls out the chant, which signals all players to get up quickly and sprint to a different mat.
3) Any runner tagged by the Chef before reaching another mat joins the tagging team as an extra Chef for subsequent rounds.
4) Modify the layout British Bulldog-style by placing mats along one end wall and having everyone sprint across to the other end.

1) Set up three cones in a line for each 3-player team, assigning roles as a thrower, a noodle holder, and a retriever.
2) The middle player shapes a pool noodle into a loop, and the thrower tosses the frisbee attempting to fly through the loop.
3) When successful, the team shouts their score, the retriever collects the disc, and all players rotate positions.
4) Footballs or foam balls can be substituted for frisbees to practice various throwing and targeting skills.
1 frisbee, 3 cones, 1 pool noodle (per group of 3)
준비물 없음(음악 재생 기기 활용 가능)

1) Divide the class into two equal teams, Bridges and Rivers, scattered freely across the gymnasium.
2) Students jog around to music; when the teacher shouts "Bridges!", the Bridge players form bridges while Rivers crawl underneath them.
3) When "Rivers!" is called, the River players lie flat on the floor and Bridge players leap over them.
4) The activity can be modified by having students roll balls under the bridges or bounce balls across the rivers.

1) All students disperse across the playing area, where every single player acts simultaneously as a tagger and a runner.
2) On signal, players run and tag others; any player who is tagged must sit down immediately on the spot.
3) A sitting player is freed and rejoins the game the moment the person who tagged them gets tagged by someone else.
4) If two players tag each other at the exact same moment, they play rock-paper-scissors to determine who sits down.

1) Divide the play area into three zones and place bowling pins in the middle zone separated into individual sections using skipping ropes.
2) Defenders stay inside their assigned middle section protecting one pin each, while attackers line up along the outside zones with balls.
3) Attackers kick balls simultaneously to knock down the pins, shouting out their cumulative score each time a pin falls while the teacher resets knocked pins.
4) After playing for a set time limit or reaching a target score, switch the roles of attackers and defenders.
10-15 foam balls, 6-8 jump ropes, 7 bowling pins

1) Place one hula hoop per student on the gym floor, have each student stand in a hoop, and let them practice communicating and switching spots.
2) Remove two hula hoops to begin the game, turning the two students without hoops into the 'Hunter Hawks'.
3) Students in hoops communicate using winks or gestures and attempt to sprint and swap places with each other.
4) The Hawks attempt to dive into an open hoop before the runners arrive, and the displaced runner becomes the new Hawk.

1) Divide players into two teams (green cars and red cars) lined up shoulder-to-shoulder along opposite sidelines facing each other.
2) Blow the whistle and count down from eight seconds as both teams run across toward the opposite team's starting line.
3) Any players who collide with anyone or fail to reach the other side before time expires must freeze on the spot as stationary 'roadblocks'.
4) Repeat the crossing rounds while progressively reducing the countdown time to 7, 6, and 5 seconds as more roadblocks clutter the court.

1) Have the entire class line up standing with their backs flat against the gymnasium wall and hand a ball to the first student.
2) Players pass the ball down the line, and immediately after passing, each player sprints to the far end of the line to become the new leader.
3) The team works together to maneuver the ball along all four gym walls until they return completely to their original starting point.
4) Increase difficulty by having players do a continuous wall-sit during passing, or lying on their backs using their feet against the wall to pass an exercise ball.
체육관 매트(또는 베이스) 6장, 킥볼(축구공) 1개, 대형 바구니(빨래바구니/플라스틱 상자) 1개

1) Set up six base mats in a wide perimeter with a collection basket in the center, dividing players into kickers and fielders.
2) The pitcher rolls the ball in, the kicker boots it into the field, and runners attempt to round all six bases sequentially to score.
3) With no foul balls, catch-outs, or tag-outs, the sole way to record an out is for fielders to toss the ball into the central container while runners are between bases.
4) For larger classes, allow multiple base-runners to stack safely on a single base, or switch sides after everyone has kicked once.
6 gym mats (or bases), 1 kickball, 1 large container/basket
여러 색상의 원마커(스팟) 20~30개 (또는 색상 훌라후프), 줄넘기 4~6줄

1) Scatter various colored spot markers or hula hoops randomly across the gym floor and split students into four groups.
2) The teacher calls out a specific color pattern sequence such as red, blue, yellow, blue, and green for students to memorize.
3) On the go signal, all students run simultaneously touching each designated color marker in that exact order and sprint back to their group base.
4) Vary movement locomotor skills using skipping, galloping, or hopping, or place jump ropes on the floor for students to leap over.
20-30 colored spot markers (or hula hoops), 4-6 jump ropes
팀 조끼(2개 색상 세트), 꼬리끈(플래그) 30~40개, 수납 상자(우유상자/바구니) 2개

1) Place two collection boxes about 50 meters apart and give every player wearing team pinnies a flag tucked into their waistband.
2) Players run into the open area to pull flags from opponents and safely carry them back into their team's collection box.
3) A player whose flag is pulled must return to their team box to retrieve a new flag; if the box is empty, they must wait until teammates bring flags.
4) If a player carrying stolen flags loses their own flag, they must forfeit all carried flags to the tagger, and a team wins by capturing all opposing flags.
Pinnies (2 colors), 30-40 flag belts or flags, 2 collection crates/boxes

1) Divide the class into two equal teams, placing one team as goalies along the wall and the other team as attackers throughout the court.
2) Set up a restriction line using cones or gym floor lines so attackers cannot get too close to the goalies along the wall.
3) During a 2-minute round, attackers shoot multiple foam balls toward the wall attempting to score as many goals as possible.
4) Whether a shot scores or is saved, goalies constantly kick and throw balls back into play, and teams switch roles after two minutes.
준비물 없음 (선택 사항: 신나는 배경 음악 및 스피커)

1) Students spread out across the entire open area while the teacher starts music or sets a 20 to 30 second timer.
2) Throughout the countdown, students continuously jog, skip, hop, or gallop around the area changing directions freely.
3) Once time is called, the teacher shouts a specific number (e.g., "Six!"), prompting students to instantly form groups matching that exact count.
4) Any leftover students who cannot complete a group perform quick exercises such as six jumping jacks or push-ups before restarting.
No equipment needed (Optional: upbeat music and speaker)

1) The teacher prepares a secret path key and arranges poly spots in a 6x6 grid.
2) The first student begins on the start spot and steps one spot forward, sideways, or diagonally.
3) If the step is correct they keep moving, but if incorrect they return to the back of the line.
4) The next teammate enters, recalling previous steps, and continues attempting to navigate all the way to the finish.

1) Students spread out on the gym court lines and one player is chosen as the starting Pac-Man.
2) On the go signal, all players and taggers must move exclusively along the lines.
3) The Pac-Man moves their arms like an opening mouth and tags runners, turning them into additional Pac-Mans.
4) Survivors must navigate intersections and dodge an increasing swarm of taggers to stay alive.

1) Mark a center zone using cones, scatter 50 beanbags as cheese, and select two cats to guard the middle.
2) Mice line up on one side and dash across to the opposite end, picking up exactly one beanbag along the way.
3) Any mouse tagged by a cat or crossing without a beanbag transforms into an extra cat for the next round.
4) Surviving mice must cross back each round accumulating more beanbags (two, then three) to determine winners.

1) Form groups of three, place cones to mark boundary lines, and assign the middle player to hold a skipping rope as the net.
2) Players on opposite sides start a rally by serving and passing a soft volleyball over the rope.
3) Teams score points through simple volleyball rules with no spiking allowed, rotating the net holder every 3 points.
4) Adapt rules according to skill level by allowing one bounce before passes to encourage longer rallies.
1 soft volleyball, 1 skipping rope, 4 cones per group

1) Set up boundaries with cones and assign dinosaur tagger roles such as T-Rex, throwers, and scooter-riding Triceratops.
2) Runners evade taggers across the gym while taggers use their specific tagging mechanics like tagging or rolling balls below the waist.
3) Tagged players freeze until freed by teammates or scooter rescues via a high-five tag.
4) Progress through the video's 10 featured tag game variations across rounds to sustain variety and engagement.
2 scooter boards, 4 foam dodgeballs, 8 cones, 2 pool noodles, 2 mats

1) Set up two goals with a goalie at each end and divide players into two teams with dodgeballs.
2) Players try to hit opponents, and anyone tagged by a ball is out and moves to the side.
3) When an active player throws the ball past the goalie into the net, all sidelined teammates revive back into the game.
4) A team wins by eliminating all opposing field players or holding the lead when time expires.

1) One player is chosen as the cat inside the circle while other students form a ring as little birds.
2) The birds rotate in a circle chanting a playful rhyme to tease the sleeping cat.
3) As soon as the chant finishes, the birds scatter away and the cat chases to tag them.
4) The first student caught by the cat becomes the new cat for the next round.

1) One student starts as the octopus in the center while all other runners line up at one baseline.
2) Runners chant the rhyme together and sprint across the gym toward the opposite safe line.
3) Anyone tagged must sit down right where they were caught, acting as seaweed/tentacles who can tag passing runners with their arms.
4) Rounds continue back and forth until everyone is tagged, and the last surviving runner wins.

1) Players line up single file behind the foul line, with the first two shooters holding basketballs.
2) Shooter one shoots, and as soon as it releases shooter two shoots, both racing to score their own rebounds.
3) If the trailing shooter scores before the lead shooter makes a basket, the lead shooter is eliminated.
4) Successful shooters pass their ball to the next player in line and rejoin the queue until the last survivor wins.

1) Scatter bean bags across the entire gym floor while all students spread out freely into open spaces.
2) With everyone playing simultaneously, students grab bean bags and slide them along the floor targeting others' feet.
3) Any runner struck on the foot by a slid bean bag must sit down immediately on that spot.
4) Seated players who collect sliding bags can shoot at standing runners' feet to revive back into the game.

1) Write warm-up tasks like laps or jumping jacks on the board using math equations.
2) Students enter the gym, check the board, and mentally solve each equation.
3) Each student completes the designated number of repetitions matching their calculated answers.
4) Vary the math level from simple addition to multi-step operations depending on student grade.

1) Form groups of three and assign players as pitcher, kicker, and catcher.
2) The pitcher rolls a foam ball along the floor toward the kicker.
3) The kicker kicks a high pop fly, and the team scores a point if the catcher catches it.
4) Rotate positions after each kick so everyone cycles through pitching, kicking, and catching.

1) Set up agility ladders and poly spots in an X shape with six perimeter stations.
2) Disperse students evenly across the fitness stations and agility paths to begin.
3) Perform designated exercises such as ten burpees then traverse the agility lines continuously for two minutes.
4) Rest for 30 to 60 seconds after each two-minute bout, then reverse running directions or switch activities.
2 agility ladders, 15 poly spots, 6 exercise mats

1) Divide players into two equal teams on either side of the court with dodgeballs.
2) Players throw foam dodgeballs across the center line to eliminate opponents.
3) Hit players step off to the sideline and remember the specific person who hit them.
4) When that particular opponent gets hit and eliminated, the waiting player instantly rejoins the game.
접시콘 5개, 훌라후프 5개, 보물 바구니 1개, 소형 교구 및 장난감 30개 이상

1) Dump various toy items on one side of the gym and set up starting cones and collection hula hoops for each team on the opposite side.
2) On the signal, the first runner sprints across, retrieves one treasure, places it inside their team hoop, and high-fives the next teammate.
3) The team that collects the three secret treasures pre-selected by the teacher, or gathers the highest total number of items, wins.
4) Vary the movement by requiring locomotor skills like skipping, galloping, or backpedaling instead of simple sprinting.
5 cones, 5 hula hoops, 1 storage bin, 30+ small toys/equipment

1) Divide the gym into Danger Land, Water, and Fun Land, placing mats as islands and providing each team with one scooter board and one rope.
2) Teams must transport all members across the water using only their scooter boat, mat islands, and rope without touching the gym floor.
3) If any student touches the floor, they must return to the starting area, and the team wins once all members safely reach Fun Land.
4) Increase difficulty by setting a time limit or restricting how many students can use the scooter at once.

1) Divide students into small teams of 2-3 facing their respective basketball hoops in a half-court setup.
2) On the go signal, the first player in each line dribbles toward the hoop and shoots from a comfortable distance.
3) Players must rebound and shoot continuously until making a basket, then shout out their score and dribble back to hand off.
4) The first team to reach a target score (e.g., 10 points) or the team with the most baskets when time expires wins.

1) Place 4 players (doubles) or 2 players (singles) on each court and line up extra students along the court sidelines.
2) Players rally or play mini-games continuously for 1 to 2 minutes upon the starting signal.
3) When the whistle blows and the teacher calls switch, all students rotate one spot clockwise so waiting players step onto the court.
4) Vary the activity by focusing on specific stroke drills or playing short competitive scoring matches each round.

1) Students pair up, spread out across the gymnasium, and receive one soft foam ball per pair.
2) While music plays, partners continuously toss and catch the ball back and forth at an appropriate distance.
3) The moment the music stops, the student holding the ball becomes the tagger and must chase and tag their partner with the ball.
4) Variations include tagging with the ball held in hand or gently tossing the ball below the waist to hit the partner.
도전 목록표 1장 (변형 시 폼볼, 줄넘기 등 추가 가능)

1) Divide the play area into four team zones and prepare a list of various physical challenges.
2) For each round, one representative from each team steps into the center circle to receive and compete in the announced challenge.
3) The player who completes or holds the challenge the longest earns a point for their team.
4) Challenges can be played equipment-free or modified to use balls, jump ropes, and beanbags based on available gear.
Challenge list sheet (optional: balls, jump ropes)

1) Pair up two teams at each available basketball hoop in the gym with one ball per team.
2) The first player shoots, retrieves their own rebound, passes to the next teammate in line, and goes to the back.
3) Whenever a basket is made, the entire team yells out the score, racing to reach five baskets first.
4) The winning team rotates to the next hoop clockwise, while the losing team stays to face a newly arriving opponent.

1) Half the class sits around a center circle as bouncers, the other half spreads out as rollers, and buckets are placed in the center and with the teacher.
2) The teacher scatters whiffle balls representing popcorn all over the gym floor, and rollers scramble to collect them.
3) Once a roller reaches a ball, they must stop and roll it to a bouncer, who bounces it once into the center bucket.
4) When all balls are gathered into the bucket, teams swap roles, and younger grades can directly toss into the bucket without bouncing.
20-30 whiffle balls (or small foam balls), 2 plastic buckets
팀 볼 태그 (팀 대항 폼볼 터치 구출 술래잡기)

1) Preparation: Divide students into three or four teams wearing colored pinnies and give every player one foam ball.
2) Progression: Players run with their ball in hand to tag opponents from other teams, causing tagged players to sit down immediately.
3) Scoring: Sitting teammates are rescued when a teammate touches their ball with another ball, and a team wins when all players on an opposing team are seated.
4) Modification: Set a specific chase order where each team only tags one target color or require tagged teams to do jumping jacks to return.
핀볼 (3가지 공격 경로 볼링핀 쓰러뜨리기 게임)

1) Preparation: Split the gym into two halves, placing about 20 bowling pins, a mini net guarded by 1-2 goalies, and a basketball hoop on each side.
2) Progression: Players roll or throw foam balls across the centerline to attack opponent pins, mini nets, and basketball hoops without crossing over.
3) Scoring: Direct hits down one pin, scoring into the net removes one opponent pin, making a basket removes two pins, and the team that clears all pins wins.
4) Modification: Allow kicking the ball for older grade levels or let each team strategically arrange their pins before the round begins.
20 foam balls, 40 bowling pins, 2 mini nets

1) Preparation: Set up running perimeters around the gym or field and pair up students standing across from each other.
2) Progression: One partner sprints along the outer perimeter toward the other while the second partner waits in place.
3) Scoring: Upon tagging up, the runner walks across the court width to rest while the waiting partner sprints along the perimeter in a continuous cycle.
4) Modification: Stagger running distances according to differing fitness levels so partners can complete their intervals comfortably.
파 어웨이 (음악 멈춤 공간 지각 거리두기 놀이)

1) Preparation: Gather students within a designated court boundary and prepare a special object such as a bean bag or trophy.
2) Progression: While music plays, students move around using various locomotor skills like running, skipping, or hopping while trying to stay as far from others as possible.
3) Scoring: When the music stops, everyone freezes, and the student found to be furthest from all other peers receives the special object to carry next round.
4) Modification: Vary the movement skills during music playback, such as galloping, crab walking, or moving at different tempo levels.

1) Divide the field into two zones with a center path and give teams 30 seconds to hide their flags visibly.
2) Infiltrate the opponent zone to find the flag, moving to the jail bench for 2 minutes if tagged by defenders.
3) Score and win the round by successfully carrying the opposing team's flag across the center line.
4) Introduce hidden immunity beanbags to grant tag immunity, or call a free-for-all mode if the round stalls.

1) Mount an exercise ball onto a laundry basket to stabilize it and form small groups of 4 to 6 players.
2) Throw a smaller ball so that it rebounds off the exercise ball and have teammates quickly catch it.
3) Score points by counting the total number of consecutive successful catches completed within one minute.
4) Adjust throw distance or switch the throwing object to different balls like foam balls to vary difficulty.
1 exercise ball, 1 laundry basket, 1 throwing ball
풀누들 다수, 대형 짐볼 1~2개, 체육 매트 2개

1) Set up mats against the walls as goals and have teams of three link together by holding pool noodles.
2) Move cooperatively while maintaining hold of the noodles and strike the large exercise ball with feet or bodies.
3) Score goals by kicking or hitting the exercise ball into the opponent mat goal without breaking the noodle link.
4) Adapt the game to pairs with one noodle or add multiple exercise balls to increase activity levels.
Multiple pool noodles, 1-2 exercise balls, 2 gym mats

1) Have all players disperse along gym floor lines and designate two taggers and two freers using colored pinnies.
2) Everyone must travel strictly on the floor lines, and anyone tagged must sit down immediately as a roadblock.
3) A sitting player is liberated and returns to active running once tagged by one of the designated freers.
4) Keep freers immune from tags and run short rounds so all students get frequent turns in special roles.
폼볼 다수, 의자 2개, 체육 매트 다수

1) Construct castles using mats with pillars holding balls, and send one knight from each team to the opposing side.
2) Teams race to complete objectives in order: throw 3 balls into opposing towers, then knock down 2 pillar balls.
3) Once pillars are cleared, the knight sits on the throne chair and must catch a thrown ball without standing up to win.
4) Integrate dodgeball elimination rules where hit players go to jail behind the wall until rescued by a catch.
Multiple foam balls, 2 chairs, multiple gym mats

1) Students line up at the baseline each with a ball, while the teacher stands at the opposite end of the gym.
2) On the teacher's 'green light' command, students advance forward while continuously dribbling the ball.
3) On the 'red light' command, players must halt their forward motion but keep dribbling in place; losing control sends them back to the start.
4) The game can be varied by using whistle counts, adding a slow-down yellow light, or racing competitively to the finish line.

1) Set up 6 to 8 exercise stations such as jump rope, sit-ups, and squats around the perimeter of a volleyball court.
2) Partners split up so that one runner performs laps or line sprints while the other performs the station exercise.
3) After a 45-second music interval, the teacher signals switch, and partners immediately swap their running and exercise roles.
4) Once both partners complete a station, pairs rotate to the next workout area until all stations are completed.

1) Form relay lines behind a starting line and place numbered posters 1 through 5 (or 10) at varying distances ahead.
2) The teacher calls out an age-appropriate arithmetic problem (for example, '2 plus 1') to the whole class.
3) The first runners in each line race to the correct answer poster (number 3), touch it, and run back to tag the next teammate.
4) Vary the movement by having students hop, gallop, skip, or dribble a ball to the correct answer.

1) Scatter hula hoops across the gym floor to serve as tree nests, placing each student inside their own individual hoop.
2) In part one, students practice verbal communication by making eye contact, asking to switch nests out loud, and trading spots.
3) In part two, talking is banned and students must use non-verbal cues like eye contact, hand gestures, and nodding to agree and swap nests.
4) In part three, remove several hoops to create Hunter Hawks who attempt to swoop in and occupy open nests during transitions.
코만도 다리 밑 터널 통과 릴레이
출발선 및 반대편 결승선 표시 라인

1) Teams line up in single file behind the starting line with all players standing with their feet spread wide apart.
2) The last player in each line crawls through the legs of all teammates until reaching the very front of the line.
3) Once at the front, that player stands up with feet spread and shouts 'Next!' to signal the next rear teammate.
4) Continue this caterpillar crawl sequence consecutively until the entire team crosses the designated finish line.

1) The tagger (wolf) faces the wall on one side, while all other players line up on the opposite starting side.
2) When players shout "Roll the dice!", the wolf rolls the foam die and counts out loud to that rolled number.
3) Players advance across the gym during the count and must freeze completely once the count ends; anyone caught moving is sent back to the start.
4) The first players to safely cross to the wolf's side win, and the game can be played for multiple rounds or time limits.

1) Each student spreads out across the basketball court with their own soccer ball (or basketball).
2) Players actively dribble within boundaries while trying to kick or knock away opponents' balls without losing control of their own.
3) If a player's ball crosses the boundary line or they lose possession, they are knocked out and move to the sideline.
4) Eliminated players stay along the perimeter lines trying to knock active balls out, while the teacher gradually shrinks the playing area to determine the final survivor.
1 soccer ball or basketball per student

1) Most players spread across the gym as butterflies, while two taggers designated as bees hold pool noodles, with a safe circle marked in the center.
2) When a bee tags a butterfly using the pool noodle, the tagged butterfly must instantly freeze in place.
3) To rescue a frozen butterfly, two other free butterflies must link arms with the teammate and escort them safely into the center circle.
4) Once inside the safe zone, the rescued butterfly counts to five before re-entering the game, and tagger roles can rotate periodically.

1) Have students form a large circle (or small teams) in the activity area and join hands with their neighbors.
2) Place a hula hoop over the arms of two students before they reconnect hands to form an unbroken circle chain.
3) Without breaking hand grips at any point, players must manipulate their bodies through the hoop to pass it along the entire circle.
4) Use a stopwatch to time how long it takes to complete a full circuit, then challenge the group to beat their record or compete against another circle.

1) Scatter hula hoops as lily pads across the court, mark caves and a belly area with cones, choose two gators, and line up the frogs on one side.
2) On start, frogs hop across toward the safe zone, and when the teacher calls "Go Gators!", gators hunt and tag frogs outside hoops for 30 seconds.
3) Tagged frogs enter the belly area, gators return to caves on "Freeze!", and frogs resume hopping for a total of three rounds.
4) Frogs remaining in hoops after round three are counted as caught, and successful frogs score a win before rotating new gators.

1) Divide students into four groups along the four boundary lines of the court, give each student a ball, and prepare a large foam dice.
2) The teacher rolls the dice, and if 1 through 4 is rolled, the corresponding side performs a full-court dribbling wave there and back.
3) When a 5 is rolled, all groups dribble and rotate clockwise to the next side, and when a 6 is rolled, they rotate counter-clockwise.
4) Vary the challenge during waves by requiring weak-hand dribbling, low dribbles, cross-overs at midcourt, or tricky dribbling moves.

1) Scatter all students across the gym, assign a blue tool to one tagger (freezer), and give a red tool to one rescuer (melter).
2) The blue tagger chases and tags runners, who must immediately freeze into frozen ice statues upon being touched.
3) The red melter moves around the gym to touch frozen statues to melt them, allowing rescued players to rejoin the game.
4) Challenge the freezer to catch everyone within a time limit, then rotate the blue and red roles among different students.
1 blue pool noodle, 1 red pool noodle (or dodgeballs)
필요 장비 없음 (정글짐/그물 놀이기구 등 야외 장애물 구역 활용)

1) Designate a jail area preferably near climbing structures, choose two players as cops, and assign all other players as robbers.
2) Robbers disperse and hide around the obstacle course while the cops count down aloud from thirty to zero in the jail.
3) Once the countdown ends, cops chase and tag robbers, immediately sending any tagged robbers into the designated jail.
4) Captured robbers stay active inside the jail structure, and after a few minutes, tally the arrests before rotating new cops.
None (outdoor playground structure or fitness park)

1) Students pair up facing each other around the room, while one extra player without a partner is designated as 'It'.
2) When 'It' calls out a physical prompt such as "Back-to-back!", each pair must immediately connect back-to-back.
3) When 'It' calls out a different prompt such as "Front-to-front!", partners quickly change their body positions accordingly.
4) When 'It' shouts "Switch!", everyone including 'It' must sprint to find a new partner, leaving the unpaired player as the next 'It'.

1) Prepare sticky notes numbered 1 to N, hand one to each student, and keep numbers strictly secret while spreading out.
2) The teacher calls out a specific number and starts a 1 to 2 minute timer, prompting that secret student to reveal themselves as the tagger.
3) The tagger chases and tags as many classmates as possible within the time limit to score tag points.
4) For variation, write called numbers on a whiteboard, recall previously used numbers, or call multiple numbers simultaneously.
폼볼 6~10개(특수 색상 공 포함), 라바콘 6개, 농구 골대 2개

1) Divide the gym into two halves, place three King's Cones targets on each side, and distribute multicolored foam balls across the court.
2) Players hit by a thrown dodgeball head to the sideline jail and wait in order of elimination.
3) A team wins the round instantly by knocking down all three enemy cones, sinking a designated special ball into the opposing basketball hoop, or eliminating all opponents.
4) Catching a flying ball frees the first player in jail, while sinking any shot into the basketball net instantly frees all jailed teammates.
Foam balls 6-10 (including special colored ball), Cones 6, Basketball hoops 2

1) Set up mats, benches, and obstacle tunnels on both halves of the court to create trenches and barricades, then distribute dodgeballs.
2) Players take positions behind barriers on their half and throw dodgeballs while ducking behind cover.
3) Any student hit by a dodgeball must exit to the gym sideline, remaining out until the round concludes when one team is completely eliminated.
4) Adapt the game into capture-the-flag paintball mode where teams dodge incoming throws while attempting to retrieve the enemy flag.

1) Form an energy charging station in the center using hula hoops and a side repair shop using cones, designating several students with dodgeballs as bad robots.
2) Good robots roam the playing area while bad robots attempt to tag them using the held dodgeballs.
3) Tagged robots become broken, moving to the repair shop to count out loud to 30 before re-entering play.
4) Good robots may take refuge in the center charging station for up to 10 seconds (counting to 10) where bad robots are not allowed to enter.

1) Set up goals at opposite gym ends using mats or nets, divide students into two teams, and assign starting goalkeepers.
2) Begin the match with an initial kickoff using the first soccer ball under standard no-hands soccer rules.
3) Toss a second and third soccer ball into the court unexpectedly after play gets underway to have all three balls active simultaneously.
4) Whenever a goal is conceded, that goalkeeper must immediately switch positions with an active field player.
Soccer balls 3, Gym mats or Mini goals 2 sets

1) Set up four cones with two teams facing each other across the middle where a target cone is placed.
2) On the signal, each team rolls their basketball back and forth trying to knock over the center target cone first.
3) The team that knocks over the cone immediately lines up to perform layup shots while the opposing team runs to the corner to complete 20 chest passes.
4) Once the 20 passes are finished, reset the target cone and tally the made layups before starting the next round.

1) Define the playing area, designate one or two taggers, and have the remaining players scatter across the gym.
2) When tagged, players must freeze in a banana pose with their arms raised overhead and bending sideways.
3) An untagged teammate can rescue them by gently pulling down their raised arm as if peeling a banana.
4) Switch taggers after a set time or increase difficulty by requiring both arms to be peeled to rejoin the game.

1) Set up mats as hospitals at each endline and designate two doctors equipped with scooter board ambulances per team.
2) Players throw dodgeballs across the center line, and anyone hit must sit down immediately where they were tagged.
3) The team doctor rides the scooter over to the downed player, transports them back to the hospital mat, and heals them.
4) Vary the game for older grades by allowing doctors to be hit and eliminated, ending the round when a team is wiped out.
4-6 foam dodgeballs, 4 scooter boards, 2 gym mats

1) Place beanbags as food on one end line, line up critters with flag tails on the opposite end, and place fox taggers in the middle.
2) Critters strategize to sprint across the playing area either individually or together while dodging the foxes.
3) Any critter reaching the food zone safely grabs one beanbag and brings it back to their home line without losing their tail.
4) If a player's tail is pulled by a fox, they must sit down at that spot and can only reach out to pull tails of passing critters until everyone is caught.

1) Set up cones in a large loop with one cone designated as a starting station for each player.
2) The teacher announces a running direction, the number of laps, and a target completion time such as one lap in exactly 40 seconds.
3) Players pace themselves by choosing when to walk, jog, or sprint around the perimeter cones.
4) The student who crosses back to their starting cone at the exact target time wins, and the challenge repeats with varied laps and times.

1) Designate two players as personal trainers wearing pinnies and scatter multiple soft dodgeballs throughout the gym.
2) Only the trainers are allowed to pick up and throw dodgeballs to tag the running classmates.
3) Any student hit by a thrown ball must step out to the perimeter fitness zone and perform predetermined exercises such as push-ups or jumping jacks.
4) Once the student finishes their prescribed repetitions, they immediately rejoin the active dodgeball game in the main area.

1) Students form a large circle or line up along the court boundary, with one leader starting in the center.
2) The leader performs a chosen physical movement (such as tuck jumps, push-ups, or silly dance stretches) for 20 seconds.
3) All surrounding classmates must follow along and mirror the leader's action for the entire 20-second duration.
4) Once the 20 seconds expire, that leader joins the perimeter and the next designated student steps in to lead a new movement.
스로 앤 고 (던지고 도망가는 짝 술래잡기)

1) Players pair up with one ball between them and stand facing each other approximately 10 to 15 feet apart.
2) Partners practice tossing and catching the ball back and forth using overhand or underhand throws.
3) The instant the teacher blows the whistle, the partner without the ball immediately turns into the tagger and chases the partner holding the ball.
4) The ball carrier flees using open space, and after a short chase period both reset to their distance to resume throwing and await the next whistle.
10–15 soft throwing balls (1 per pair), 1 whistle

1) Divide the gym into four corners, set up two stacked mats in each corner as skyscrapers, and split students into four teams.
2) Distribute dodgeballs to each team, and on the signal, players throw balls to knock down opposing skyscrapers.
3) Players may defend and block shots targeting their own skyscraper, and a team is eliminated when their mat tower falls.
4) Eliminated players disperse to join surviving teams, continuing the battle until only one standing skyscraper remains.

1) Split the class into two teams positioned behind their respective service lines on a full volleyball court.
2) One team receives volleyballs and all members serve simultaneously over the net aiming for in-bounds territory.
3) The team scores points equal to the total number of successful serves landing inside the boundaries.
4) The opposing team gathers all balls to take their turn serving, rotating between underhand and overhand serves until reaching 20 points.

1) Mark a large center circle in the gym or with jump ropes outside, and pair up students behind designated marker cones.
2) On the whistle, the first runner sprints to touch the perimeter of the center circle and sprints back.
3) Once the first runner returns and tags their partner, the second runner immediately takes off to repeat the cycle.
4) Modify the movement patterns from basic running to side-stepping, hopping, dribbling a ball, or performing five jumping jacks at the circle.

1) Line up all students along one baseline of the gym with sufficient safety spacing between peers.
2) Prompted by teacher guided questions, students suggest movement ideas and walk across to the opposite wall before jogging back.
3) Progressively advance movement patterns by having students perform running, single-leg hopping, skipping, and galloping across the gym.
4) Introduce imaginative movement variations such as animal walks, arm swing rhythms, and alternating lead feet during galloping.
Act It Out Creative Movement Charades

1) Organize students into small groups of 4 to 5 members and assign each team their own designated practice space.
2) Provide a dramatic scene prompt such as firefighters, medieval knights, or sporting events, or allow groups to choose their own topic.
3) Group members collaborate to choreograph physical movements and expressive poses where every individual plays an active role without words.
4) Groups perform their dynamic pantomime scene in front of the class while peer audiences guess the theme and evaluate creativity.

1) Students spread out in the classroom or gym and stand stationary at their spots.
2) Players toss a soft ball to each other silently without letting it bounce.
3) Any student who drops the ball, throws a bad pass, or speaks must perform an exercise like 5 jumping jacks to rejoin.
4) Increase the challenge by adding two or three balls into play simultaneously.
세 공 연속 킥 앤 런 트리플 볼
Triple Ball (Kick and Base Running Game)

1) Set up a hula hoop and two cones in a triangle, placing three balls inside the hoop.
2) One kicker kicks all three balls into the field one by one while three fielders prepare to retrieve them.
3) The kicker circles the two cones back to home as many times as possible, scoring one point per completed lap until all balls are returned.
4) Players rotate positions after each turn and teams can compare their accumulated points.
Tight Spaces Tag (Shrinking Arena Flag Steal)

1) Students start inside a designated large boundary, each wearing a flag tucked into their pocket or waistband.
2) On the signal, players run around trying to pull opponents' flags while protecting their own.
3) Players whose flags are stolen or who step out of bounds move to the sidelines, where they can swipe flags from nearby active runners.
4) Shrink the court boundary progressively as fewer players remain until the last survivor wins.

1) Players face the wall with eyes closed while the teacher secretly taps one student to be the Spy.
2) Everyone walks around making continuous eye contact while the Spy attempts to poison players by winking at them unseen.
3) Any player who is winked at must lie down or hold a fitness plank, and players try to deduce and accuse the Spy.
4) Incorrect accusations also result in holding a plank, and the game ends when the Spy is found or eliminates everyone.

1) Place six gym mats around the gym floor, naming each after a Mario world land.
2) Two taggers start in the middle while the remaining students distribute themselves across the six mats.
3) When taggers call out "Find a new land!", all runners must sprint to a different mat without getting tagged.
