4) Tagged players become the taggers in the center for the next round, and runners cannot return to their previous mat.

1) Designate a few attackers who start with hula hoops on the floor and spread the rest of the players as runners.
2) On the go signal, attackers kick their hoops across the gym floor aiming to hit the runners on their feet.
3) Any runner struck on the foot must exit and run a perimeter lap before re-entering or face elimination.
4) The game can be modified by using floor hockey sticks and pucks or by rolling foam balls toward feet.
신호 반응 컬러 라인과 볼 쟁탈전

1) Line up players along the designated start line and place cones topped with grab objects along the far wall.
2) The teacher calls out line colors, prompting all students to quickly sprint and relocate to that specific line.
3) When the teacher shouts out the target object command, players race to grab an available object from the cones.
4) The round can be varied by repeating colors as trick calls or removing one object each round.

1) Position one or two bakers in the gym center and divide runners into groups of holiday cookie names.
2) When the baker calls out a cookie name, those specific runners must cross to the far side without getting tagged.
3) Players tagged by the baker must enter the oven area along the side and wait inside while baking.
4) The baker can shout a rescue phrase to let all trapped cookies run over to the waiting table safely.

1) Drape bed sheets over the volleyball net so that both teams cannot see across to the opposing court.
2) Divide the class into two teams positioned on opposite sides without any view of opponents or setup.
3) Teams play standard volleyball rules, reacting quickly as the ball suddenly appears over the covered net.
4) Adapt play using lightweight beach balls, permitting one bounce, or adjusting the team size per side.

1) Divide the gym into four playing areas with a long runner zone down the center using pylons.
2) Teams in each corner area throw dodgeballs at opposing zones to hit other players.
3) A tagged player enters the middle zone and must run from one end to the other without being hit to get back in.
4) If hit inside the middle zone, the runner must keep attempting to cross safely to revive.

1) Mark hospital zones in opposite court corners with cones, and designate two taggers and two ambulance drivers.
2) Tagged players become sick patients and must lie down on the floor where they were caught.
3) Ambulance drivers push the scooter mat to collect up to two patients and transport them to the nearest hospital.
4) Patients complete a fitness task such as five push-ups at the hospital before returning to the game.

1) Scatter 50 to 100 beanbags (fish) in the lake center and place hula hoops (nests) at opposite sidelines.
2) The agile Seahawks receive a 5-second head start to dash in and collect fish into their nest.
3) The stronger Eagles enter to gather fish or tag Seahawks to force them to drop fish to steal.
4) Players carry only one fish at a time without throwing, and the team with the most fish wins.
머리 위 배터리 로봇 구출 놀이

1) All students act as robots with a beanbag placed on their head while two players are chosen as mechanics.
2) On the signal, robots walk around the gym maintaining their balance without using their hands.
3) If a beanbag falls off, that robot freezes in place until a mechanic arrives.
4) Mechanics pick up the fallen beanbags and place them back on heads to repair them, switching roles periodically.

1) Stand several folding mats upright in the gym center to form obstacles, set up start and finish lines, and choose one tagger.
2) The tagger yells face the wall and counts down from five to zero while hiding behind one of the mats.
3) Once zero is reached, runners dash toward the opposite finish line trying to avoid getting tagged.
4) Tagged runners, peekers, or anyone touching a mat become taggers for the next round until everyone is caught.

1) Scatter bingo chips, pennies, or small objects widely across a grassy field and organize students into teams of four or individuals.
2) On the start whistle, students sprint across the field to collect as many objects as possible within a 3 to 5-minute time limit.
3) Collected items are brought back to the designated team base continuously before the timer expires.
4) Teams count their collected items at the end to determine the highest score, and play again with different locomotor movements.
온몸으로 만드는 인간 알파벳 글자 맞추기

1) Students spread out across the gym moving in various directions using locomotor skills like running, hopping, or skipping to music.
2) The teacher stops the music and calls out an alphabet letter loudly.
3) Students quickly pair up with the nearest partner, lie down on the floor, and cooperate to form the shape of that letter.
4) Once confirmed, students stand up to resume moving, and variations can expand to 3–4 players spelling entire words.
스폿 샷 농구 릴레이 슈팅 배틀

1) Place poly spots around each basketball hoop with assigned point values (1 to 4 points) and divide players into small teams.
2) On the clock, the first shooter takes as many shots as possible within a one-minute time limit from any spot.
3) Teammates act as active rebounders under the hoop, catching misses and quickly passing the ball back to the shooter while tallying points.
4) After one minute, players rotate roles until every teammate completes their shooting round, crowning the highest cumulative team score.

1) Set up multiple holes across the gym or field using cones for tee-offs and targets, assigning groups of 2-3 to each hole.
2) The first player throws a disc from the tee cone toward the target cone and continues throwing from where it lands until hitting the cone.
3) Upon hitting the target, the player records the total number of throws and brings the disc back to the next teammate to compete for the lowest strokes.
4) Once all teammates finish the hole, groups rotate to the next hole simultaneously, with variations using soccer balls or hockey sticks.

1) Designate one student as Santa wearing a red pinnie while all other students scatter across the gym as reindeer.
2) Santa chases and tags the runaway reindeer while the reindeer dodge into open spaces to avoid being caught.
3) Once tagged, a reindeer must run to touch one wall of the gym and then sprint to touch the opposite wall before re-entering play.
4) Depending on group size and stamina, add helper elves as extra taggers or modify the wall-running movement to side-shuffles.

1) Scatter lily pad spot markers on the floor around basketball hoops and place a hula hoop collection chamber for each team.
2) Players from 2-4 teams dribble to an available spot marker and take a basketball shot from that exact position.
3) If made, the shooter retrieves that spot marker and brings it back to their team's hula hoop; if missed, they must attempt from a different spot before returning.
4) The first team to collect 10 spot markers or the team with the most markers within the time limit wins, with scoring weight adjustable by shooting distance.

1) Divide the activity space into two designated areas: Inner Space and Outer Space, assigning satellites (runners) and meteors (taggers).
2) Satellites must hop in Inner Space and jump in Outer Space, while meteors must do the opposite by jumping in Inner Space and hopping in Outer Space.
3) When a meteor tags a satellite while maintaining the required locomotion, they immediately switch roles and continue the game.
4) Locomotion rules can be modified to crab walks, backward walking, or skipping across zones to vary coordination challenge.

1) Line up 20-40 plastic pins along one side of the gym and establish a throwing line tailored to students' grade levels.
2) Place containers filled with various balls (foam balls, tennis balls) behind the line and have all throwers line up ready.
3) Players collaborate for 3 minutes to throw one ball at a time and knock down all pins before the ball bins run empty.
4) Students are strictly forbidden from crossing the throwing line to retrieve balls during play, and the activity can be modified into a team relay contest.
캐치 앤 스텝 (한 걸음 뒤로 던지기)

1) Pair students up facing each other and give each pair one ball to start.
2) When a player successfully catches a thrown ball without bouncing, that catcher takes one step backward.
3) If a catch is missed, the player who missed it must step forward to reduce the distance.
4) Switch throwing techniques between underhand and overhand, or use water balloons for advanced rounds.

1) Have all runners line up along one side of the gym and place one or two catchers in the middle.
2) When the catchers shout "British Bulldog!", runners must sprint across to the opposite end line.
3) Any runner tagged while crossing joins the center team as a catcher for the next round.
4) Continue until the last bulldog is caught, and the final survivor becomes the starting catcher next game.

1) Divide the gym into two halves, placing 7 bowling pins and one hula-hoop castle in each half.
2) Players throw foam balls to knock down enemy pins, with a maximum of one defender per pin.
3) Teams must knock down all 7 target pins before they are allowed to attack the hoop castle.
4) Accidentally knocking down the opponent's castle before eliminating all 7 pins results in an automatic loss.
8 foam balls, 12 hula hoops, 14 plastic bowling pins

1) Arrange the class in a grid (e.g., 5x5) and assign one student as a cat and another as a mouse.
2) When the caller shouts "Streets!" or "Alleys!", grid players pivot 90 degrees and join hands to alter paths.
3) The cat chases the mouse through open pathways strictly using fast power-walking without running.
4) If the cat tags the mouse or time runs out, switch roles; head-balancing items can be added as a handicap.

1) Choose three students to be bandits wearing pennies and scatter multiple foam balls inside the gym.
2) Regular players dribble and pass the balls to one another to keep possession away from the bandits.
3) Bandits steal balls and kick them against the perimeter wall to permanently eliminate them from play.
4) The game continues until all balls are eliminated, after which new bandits are selected for the next round.
Get Your Trash Off My Yard

1) Divide the court into two yards using a volleyball net and spread dodgeballs and beanbags evenly on both sides.
2) On the start signal, throw dodgeballs over the net and slide beanbags under the net across the floor into the opponent yard.
3) When time is called, count the items in each yard, and the team with fewer items wins the round.
4) Players may only handle one item at a time, and music can be played and paused to signal start and stop.
수집용 메쉬 주머니 4개, 콩주머니 20개, 폼볼 10개, 접시콘 20개

1) Students form lines by placing hands on shoulders to make snakes, with the last person holding a collection bag.
2) Scatter thirty to fifty small items such as beanbags, small balls, and cones all over the playing area.
3) On the whistle, snakes move together; only the head picks up items and passes each item down the line into the tail bag.
4) The team with the most collected items in their bag wins, and players can change snake lengths or head roles.
Mesh collection bags 4, beanbags 20, small foam balls 10, dome cones 20

1) Set up boundaries with cones; runners line up at one baseline while rollers position along the sidelines with dodgeballs.
2) Runners attempt to dash across to the opposite end while rollers roll soft balls across the floor aimed at runners' feet.
3) Any runner contacted on the foot joins the sideline rollers to roll balls during subsequent crossings.
4) Rounds continue back and forth until all runners are caught, with extra balls added to adjust challenge.

1) Teams line up behind starting cones with a turnaround marker set ahead, giving the first runner a beanbag.
2) On start, runners balance the beanbag on their head or arm, walk around the turning cone, and return without dropping it.
3) The runner passes the beanbag to the next teammate and sits at the back; the first team all seated wins.
4) Variations include balancing on shoulders, flipping and catching, or tossing the beanbag to the next runner from the marker.
실내용 풋볼 여러 개, 접시콘(또는 라바콘) 4개, 체육 매트 4개

1) Divide the gym into two halves, stand up mats at each end to form target areas, and place cones to create throwing lines.
2) When play starts, students throw footballs into the designated mat target area strictly from on or behind their throwing line.
3) Each quarter lasts two to three minutes, after which the balls inside each target area are counted to calculate team points.
4) In subsequent rounds, you can move the throwing line farther back or allow blockers to defend the target.
Multiple indoor footballs, 4 cones, 4 gymnastics mats
콩주머니 20개, 훌라후프 5개, 스쿠터보드 3대, 긴 벤치 2개, 체육 매트 2개

1) Set up benches, scooter boards, hula hoops, and standing mats across the gym, placing a hoop with bean bags at the far end.
2) Half the students become creatures (snakes on benches, crocodiles on scooters, frogs on hoops, lizards behind mats) while the other half are humans.
3) Humans attempt to cross the gym without getting tagged to collect one bean bag and safely return it to their team's stash.
4) If tagged, humans must return to the start and try again; teams switch creature and human roles after a set time.
20 bean bags, 5 hula hoops, 3 scooter boards, 2 benches, 2 gymnastics mats

1) Pair up or form small groups and place a cone in the center between players.
2) Follow the teacher's called-out movement commands such as toe touches or balancing.
3) Race to touch the cone when the teacher says 'Go', scoring one point for being first.
4) Vary the game by having students circle the cone to music and touch it when it stops.

1) Set up defensive zones in front of both goals using cones and assign attackers, defenders, and goalies.
2) Defenders must strictly remain inside their assigned defensive zone during play.
3) Attackers move the ball through zones via passing combinations to score into the opponent goal.
4) Modify the activity by using a basketball or handball with modified court rules.

1) Disperse students across the play area and designate a couple of players as taggers.
2) Tagged players must lie on their backs with arms and legs raised like a dead ant.
3) Four free players must each touch one limb simultaneously to revive the teammate.
4) For smaller groups, modify the revival rule so a single high-five frees the player.

1) Spread out all players across the playing area to move around freely.
2) When two players encounter each other, they stop and play rock-paper-scissors.
3) The loser must line up directly behind the winner and follow them as a train.
4) When trains meet, the lead champions battle until the entire class forms one long train.
접시콘 10개, 매트 4장, 훌라후프 4개, 스쿠터보드 1대, 줄넘기 1개, 원마커 8개

1) Set up gym stations using mats, hula hoops, scooters, skipping ropes, cones, and tunnels.
2) Have the next student in line start once the front student finishes the first few stages.
3) Complete each challenge sequentially including log rolls, single-foot hopping, scooter riding, and rope jumping.
4) Switch the running direction or have students design their own obstacle configurations.
10 cones, 4 mats, 4 hula hoops, 1 scooter board, 1 skipping rope, 8 spot markers

1) Set up gym mats in an octagon at waist height and place all students inside.
2) The teacher tosses in a soft bouncy ball and players strike the ball with their hands.
3) Any player hit below the knee is eliminated and steps outside the mat boundary.
4) Eliminated players re-enter when the teacher calls jailbreak or extra balls are added.

1) Place one exercise mat per team along the gym baseline and have all members stand on it.
2) On the go signal, teammates work together to move the mat without touching the floor.
3) The first team to navigate their mat across the gym to the opposite end line wins.
4) Scatter cones or beanbags as treasures on the floor to collect the most within a time limit.
축구공 15~20개, 폼볼 5개, 접시콘 20개, 볼링핀 10개, 팀 조끼 6벌

1) Divide the area into grids using cones and introduce 10 games including Bandits and Pinball Soccer.
2) Students rotate through stations practicing ball control, one-touch passing, and target shooting.
3) Teams score points by knocking down pins or kicking opponents' balls out of bounds.
4) Modify by introducing irregular balls like foam dice or adding active defenders in circles.

1) Form circles of 6-8 students with soccer balls and setup cones in designated areas.
2) Players call a teammate's name across the circle and deliver accurate inside-foot passes.
3) Score by knocking down target cones in the center or swap places when a defender intercepts.
4) Progress to all outer players holding balls and executing rapid one-touch passes with a center pivot.

1) Place one hula hoop per team opposite their relay line and scatter colored beanbags in the center.
2) On the go signal, the first runner dashes to grab one topping beanbag and places it in their hoop.
3) Runners return to high-five the next teammate who then sprints to deliver another topping.
4) Once all toppings are collected, teams sit down together to count and compare their ingredients.

1) Set up 10 plastic pins in a line along the center court line, placing goalkeepers in the middle, throwers and rollers on opposite sidelines, and ball retrievers on the endlines.
2) Throwers and rollers attempt to knock down the pins using foam dodgeballs while the goalkeepers block the balls from hitting the pins.
3) Teams score one point for each pin knocked down during a 3-minute round, and knocked-down pins are immediately stood back up by the goalkeepers.
4) Rotate positions after each round so every student experiences each role, or modify the game to end only when all pins are knocked over.

1) Mark a long lengthwise zone across the gym floor with cones, place 3-4 wolves holding scarves inside the den, and line up the rest of the players as bunnies along the sides.
2) Bunnies attempt to run across the den to the opposite side while wolves must stay within their designated zone and tag them with their free hand.
3) When a bunny is tagged inside the den, they retrieve a scarf from the crate and transform into a wolf for the next crossing.
4) Increase the width of the den or the starting number of wolves to scale the game difficulty for large groups up to 50+ students.

1) Designate opposite ends of the gymnasium as 'Army' and 'Navy' boundaries, and have all students begin by lining up along the center line.
2) When the caller shouts "Army!" or "Navy!", players run toward that designated side, immediately turning back if the opposite command is called mid-stride.
3) If "Hit the deck!" is called, every player must instantly drop flat on their stomach and remain completely still until the caller gives the command "At ease!".
4) Add an elimination or fun exercise challenge for players who react prematurely to trick commands or who are the last to reach the wall.

1) Students pair up, find an open space anywhere in the gym, and take one soft foam ball per pair.
2) The player without the ball gets a 5-second head start to sprint away and gain as much distance as possible.
3) Once the 5 seconds expire, the thrower chases their partner and attempts to tag them by throwing the foam ball at safe target areas like the feet or legs.
4) The thrower can retrieve and re-throw the ball until a hit is scored, after which the partners immediately swap roles and start a new 5-second countdown.

1) Students form a circle of 6 to 10 players, and one starting player holds a stuffed cow (or soft ball).
2) Players pass the stuffed cow around the circle from person to person without dropping it onto the floor.
3) Every time the toy successfully completes a full rotation around the circle, all players take one small step back to expand the circle.
4) If anyone drops the toy, everyone shouts "Moo-shake!" and performs a silly whole-body shaking wiggle dance before stepping back in to reset the circle.

1) The teacher starts as the leader and students spread out across the gym or classroom with enough personal space.
2) When the leader calls out an item good for the heart, students continuously perform an action like jumping on the spot.
3) When an item that is bad for the heart is called out, students must immediately freeze and stand completely still.
4) There is no elimination, and students discuss why an item is unhealthy while varying exercise movements such as high knees or jumping jacks.
어지르기 팀 대 치우기 팀 콘 뒤집기 축구

1) Scatter numerous cones across the area and divide the class into Messies who knock down cones and Cleanies who upright them.
2) Start with hands only, then progress to using feet only where players gently tip cones over or upright them without kicking.
3) In the soccer version, Messies dribble soccer balls and gently kick them into cones to knock them over while Cleanies fix them.
4) Progress into paired passing challenges against aligned cones or a slalom dribbling relay shooting at a final target cone.

1) Set up goals at opposite ends of the gym, divide the class into two teams, and have all players assume a crab walk position.
2) Players must maintain the crab walk stance throughout the entire match without standing up or using their hands and arms.
3) Teams pass and kick the beach ball toward the opposing net using only their feet, knees, or head to score goals.
4) Introduce multiple beach balls simultaneously onto the court to increase engagement and keep all participants active.

1) Section off a designated lane using cones or gym floor lines, placing half the students inside as targets and half outside as throwers.
2) Target players move continuously back and forth inside the gallery performing assigned locomotive skills like crab walking or hopping.
3) Throwers practice rolling, underhand, or overhand throwing soft foam balls at the moving target players from behind the line.
4) When a target is hit, they immediately swap roles with the thrower, or play with a rule where targets cannot dodge and must move at a steady pace.
Rock Paper Scissors Four Corners Warm-Up

1) Place four cones in the corners to form a rectangle, and have students divide themselves among the four corners facing clockwise.
2) Players at each corner pair up to play rock-paper-scissors, and the winner immediately sprints clockwise to the next cone.
3) The player who loses stays at the same cone and matches up with another waiting classmate to play again.
4) Players who lose three consecutive times advance automatically, and completing a full four-cone lap earns a scoring popsicle stick.

1) Runners gather in the center circle as horses while four taggers start outside holding hula hoops as lassos.
2) On the signal, runners gallop out of the center and spread out across the gym while cowboys attempt to tag them.
3) Tagged runners must return to the center circle and perform exercises such as jumping jacks.
4) To ensure safety, students gallop rather than sprint, or play with simple hand tags instead of hoops when running.

1) Set up five cones in a designated area and assign four defenders and one attacker to the group.
2) On the whistle, all players move around the play area looking for open angles and positions.
3) The attacker tries to capture a cone by placing a hand on top, while four defenders move quickly to touch and protect the cones.
4) A round immediately ends when the attacker successfully touches an open cone, after which a new attacker is rotated in.

1) Divide the court into two halves, line up team players along the end walls as goalkeepers, and start with three field players per side.
2) Throw a foam soccer ball into the center to begin the fast-paced three-on-three match.
3) Players attempt to kick the ball past defenders into the end wall below head height to score, with infractions penalized by free kicks.
4) Whistle blows every one to two minutes to rotate field players to the end wall line while three fresh players immediately sprint in.

1) Set up four corner bases using four colored cones representing Pokemon teams, and have students wear matching colored pinnies.
2) Designate one color team to be the taggers to start the round while all other students scatter across the gym floor.
3) Any tagged student must go to their team's home cone area and complete a designated movement skill before returning.
4) Once the movement challenge is finished, the student re-enters play, and tagger roles rotate to another color team after several minutes.
신체 모방 정글 동물 표현 놀이

1) Have students gather in the center of the gym while the teacher introduces a creative theme like a jungle or desert.
2) When signaled, students imagine an animal living in that habitat and spread out across the entire open space.
3) Each student travels around the room mimicking the unique movements and physical behaviors of their chosen animal.
4) The whistle blows for all students to return to the center circle, after which the class can explore a new theme.

1) Organize students into teams in straight lines and place 3-4 hula hoops in front of the lead jumper.
2) On the whistle, the first jumper (the frog) leaps forward into the hoops one by one.
3) Teammates behind quickly pick up the cleared hoops from the back and lay them down in front of the frog.
4) Stepping outside the hoop requires returning to the start, and upon reaching the far wall, a new jumper takes over for the return trip.

1) Disperse students across the gym and designate one or two players as taggers.
2) On the start signal, runners scatter while the taggers chase and tag them with a gentle touch.
3) Tagged runners must freeze and bend their backs forward with curved arms to form a candy cane shape.
4) Free runners unfreeze tagged players by ducking under the candy cane hoop, and roles switch after a set time.
Crabs and Lobsters Beach Ball Match

1) Set up goals with cones at each end, divide the class into two teams with assigned numbers, and place beach balls in the center.
2) The teacher calls out specific numbers, and the called players must enter the center playing area using a crab walk.
3) Called players (crabs) can only use their feet to kick the beach balls toward the opposing team's goal to score points.
4) Uncalled players (lobsters) guard the goal line using only their hands to push or punch the balls away without catching them.

1) From a standing position, bend your knees and place both hands on the floor.
2) Step back one foot at a time into a plank position without jumping.
3) Keep your hips and back from sagging, then step forward one foot at a time.
4) Straighten your back first and stand up using the strength of your legs.

1) Move only by passing without dribbling, taking no more than three steps while holding the ball.
2) Pass or shoot at the frame within three seconds of receiving the ball.
3) Complete a maximum of three consecutive passes within the team before attempting a shot.

1) Alternate 20 seconds of exercise and 10 seconds of rest.

Various Floating Methods and Breathing Practice

1) Float in the water using a comfortable posture such as shrimp float, star float, back float, or jellyfish float.
2) Press down on the water with your arms and lift your head above the surface to inhale when breathing is needed.
3) As the body sinks after breathing, resume the floating posture and wait to surface again.

1) Choose the most comfortable floating posture, such as shrimp float or prone star float, and enter the water.
2) Periodically push down on the water with both arms and raise head to breathe while floating.
3) Continuously check your surroundings and maintain the same spot to stay afloat for 5 minutes.

1) Perform a back float posture and gently move hands to maintain balance.
2) Without kicking legs, move arms like rowing oars to turn and move in the desired direction.

1) When holding a life buoy, lean chest against it and hook both arms over it rather than climbing on top.
2) Hug kickboards tightly against the chest and lie back to stay afloat.
3) If there is no immediate danger and land is far, look toward rescuers and wait in place.

1) Players from both teams take turns using long cues to slide disks into the scoring zones.

1) Warm up with 1 minute of light jogging in place on an exercise mat.

1) Place 2 storybooks side by side on the floor and stand upright facing them.

3) As step 2, alternate single touches over 16 beats, and as step 3, step both feet up and down alternately onto the books.

1) Rest hand on the floor and flick a bottle cap using thumb, index, or middle finger.
2) Place caps facing each other and take turns flicking to hit opponent caps or land within a hand span to capture them.

1) Players wear 3 wristbands chosen from 6 colors, and 6 to 12 players hold hands in a circle.

1) Observe picture cards of classroom items and select objects to represent.
2) Imitate shapes using bodily movements to highlight traits like big, small, sharp, round, wide, or narrow.
3) Express movements of functioning items like electric fans through variations in speed, curves, and straight lines.

1) Set starting and finishing lines and decide within groups how to move.
2) Move along the designated path using various steps such as walking, skipping, and galloping.

4) Students who need extra support can hold hands with peers or teachers while practicing.

1) Divide roles into throwers and target holders facing each other.
2) Target holders stand still without moving while holding a basket in front of their waist.
3) Throwers toss balls or objects into the basket from a set distance.
4) The player or group that lands the most objects into the fixed target at varying distances wins.

1) Mark the playing area and set up safety zones.

3) At the start signal, players chase each other and place stickers on friends' backs.
4) Players must not run out of the field while fleeing, and anyone with a sticker on their back moves to the waiting area.

1) Divide into teams and assign the fielding team to pitcher and fielders.
2) The kicker calls out the score zone where the ball will be kicked and kicks the ball.
3) If the ball lands in the designated zone, the team gets the points.
4) Landing elsewhere or being caught results in an out, and teams switch after three outs; the team with the most points after 3 innings wins.

1) Form fielding and batting teams.
2) When a batter steps up, the fielding team calls out a batting direction such as 1st base, 2nd base, or 3rd base.
3) If the batter hits toward the designated direction, they score 1 point; failing to do so awards no points.
4) Each student receives 3 batting chances.

1) Mark scoring zones from 1 to 3 points around the goal according to shooting locations.
2) Offensive players take turns dribbling from the starting line and shoot from their chosen zone.
3) Goalkeepers must stay within the goalkeeper area while defending.
4) The team with the highest total score at the end wins.
Table Tennis Paddle and Ball Activities

1) Hold a paddle in one hand and bounce a ball upward without letting it hit the floor.
2) Hold a paddle in each hand and alternate hitting the ball upward.
3) Two players sit facing each other and rally the ball without letting it drop.
4) From a designated distance, hit the ball with the paddle into a target box with or without a bounce.
2 table tennis paddles, 1 table tennis ball, box

1) Students sit in a circle in a cross-legged position with hands on their knees.

1) Set up a mini net by placing obstacles such as boxes or books in the center of the desk.

1) In pairs, one student stays outside the mat and rolls a die showing rolling movements and repetition counts.

1) Students pair up, and one person tosses a ball or shuttlecock toward the partner.

1) Team members get down on all fours to form a leg tunnel, keeping gaps between players within 10 cm.

1) Divide roles into balloon holders and balloon kickers.

3) Practice passing the ball, quickly moving along the sideline, receiving the return pass, and attacking.
4) Rotate defending and attacking partners sequentially by assigned numbers to repeat the drills.
Dodgeballs, 2 traffic cones, disc cones, team vests

1) Divide into a tagger at the front and two teams along the lockers
2) Play rock-paper-scissors with the tagger; winners split legs forward
3) Those who tie or lose must touch fingertips to the floor for 3 seconds
4) When a player reaches the target desk line, they score a point for their team and return to the back of the line

1) Arrange chairs equal to half the number of students in a circle with one team vest on each, dress one chair with a vest as a marker, and place a bell on a center desk.
2) Pairs play rock-paper-scissors where winners sit on chairs, one student sits at the desk as General Yi Sun-sin, and losers hold hands in front of the chairs.
3) Yi Sun-sin rings the bell once, players rotate singing Ganggangsullae, and when the bell rings again, they stop to face opponents aligned clockwise from the marked chair.
4) Facing pairs compete in three minigames using vests (sitting vest grab, standing vest grab, hand push game), and any student with 5 consecutive wins can challenge Yi Sun-sin.

1) Fold an old textbook in half and tuck it into the pages to form a curved track.
2) Divide into two teams and align textbooks end-to-end in a line from the start to a paper cup on a chair.
3) The front player rolls a ping-pong ball; once it passes, players sprint to the end of the line to extend the track.
4) If the ball drops, pick it up from that spot and continue; the team that deposits the ball into the cup first wins.
Old textbooks, 2 ping-pong balls, 2 paper cups, 2 chairs

1) Scatter team bibs (1 per person) widely across the area, and have teams of 6-8 sit in circles holding hands at the start line.
2) The first runner stands inside the circle; on the signal, the entire team moves together holding hands toward the bibs.
3) The first runner picks up one bib and weaves zigzag through the connected teammates for one full lap.
4) The next runner enters the center to repeat; the first team whose members all collect bibs and return seated at the start line shouting 'Success' wins.

1) Perform individual stretching from legs to upper body (short/long leg stretch, floor reach, arm and neck stretches) holding for at least 5 seconds.
2) Stand facing a partner, place hands on each other's shoulders, and lean upper bodies down to stretch shoulders and backs together.
3) Keep the lower body fixed and twist the torso to high-five the partner in sync with the teacher's whistle.
4) Start with feet together and play Rock-Paper-Scissors; the winner moves their front foot back, and the loser steps forward into a leg split.

1) The human number team (wearing numbered bibs) plans positions and scatters across the field.
2) Challenge teams (3 teams of 7 students) gather at the starting line to discuss running strategies.
3) On signal, each challenge team runs together in a single file, touching the palms of human numbers to check their hidden numbers.
4) Once identified, the team must touch the human numbers in exact order from 1 to 7, sprint back across the start line, and shout "Success."

3) Allow sufficient practice time before games to understand the rules.

1) Connect desks in a row down the center of the classroom to serve as nets, dividing every 4 desks into a court (3 courts total).
2) Divide 4 to 6 group members across each desk court facing each other.
3) The server tosses the table tennis ball over the desk net, and the receiving side hits the underside of the ball with their open palm after one bounce.
4) Count aloud each successful volley until the ball is missed, and record the highest consecutive count achieved within 5 minutes.

1) Form a circle of 6 students per team holding hands.
2) The first runner weaves zigzag in and out under the joined arms of teammates around the circle.
3) When the runner returns to their starting spot, the player to their right becomes the next runner.
4) The team whose members all finish running and sit down on the floor first wins.

1) Sit comfortably at desks and lightly warm up the body.
2) Play rock-paper-scissors simultaneously with the teacher on call.
3) Students who tie or lose must mimic the teacher's dance movements as accurately as possible.
4) Students who win do not have to copy the movements and may rest.

1) Divide into 4 teams of 5 to 7 students; 2 teams become challenge runners at the starting line, while 2 teams become human number teams seated on chairs in a circle.
2) The human number team secretly assigns numbers 1 through 6 among themselves.
3) On the start signal, challenge runners dash out and tag a seated student, who then displays their secret number using fingers.
4) Runners must find and tag the numbers in strict sequence from 1 to 6; incorrect numbers require running back to tag the next runner, and the team that brings all numbers 1-6 back hand-in-hand first wins.
Physical Education Sportsmanship and Consideration Orientation

1) Reflect on the purpose of physical education by viewing examples of Usain Bolt and Park Ji-sung.
2) Learn to show consideration and avoid alienating others with excessive competitiveness during familiar sports.
3) Pledge to give full effort without giving up even in challenging activities.
4) Promise to participate together harmoniously and enjoyably as a class.

1) Each student places 12 colored pencils on their desk and waits.
2) When the teacher rings the bell, students stand up one by one calling out consecutive numbers in order.
3) A student is eliminated if they stand up simultaneously with someone else, call the wrong number, or fail to stand before the end.
4) Eliminated students put one pencil into their pencil case, and the player with the most pencils left after multiple rounds wins.
12 colored pencils per student, desk bell

1) Prepare 10-14 long umbrellas found in the classroom.
2) Form teams of 5-7 players and stand in a circle holding an umbrella upright.
3) One teammate inside or leading the circle counts the beat (one, two, three).
4) Release your own umbrella so it stays balanced and quickly move sideways to catch the next umbrella on the beat.
5) Count successful catches without dropping an umbrella for 1 minute, and the team with the most wins takes the match.
Squat Number Calling and RPS Team Formation

1) Align front and side rows upon the teacher's call, then sit down in sequence while shouting numbers (jumping variation optional).
2) To form two teams with equal gender ratio, play rock-paper-scissors with same-gender peers and split into winners and losers.
3) To form four teams, play round 1 of rock-paper-scissors, then winners (raising hand) play each other and losers (hands on head) play each other.
4) Divide into 4 teams based on 2 wins, 1 win 1 loss, and 2 losses, line up, and verify team numbers with squat calling.

1) Divide into two teams with one team wearing vests, and determine each player's age by rock-paper-scissors: 1st (30 yrs/3 rubber bands), 2nd (20 yrs/2 bands), 3rd (10 yrs/1 band).
2) Teams start at opposite sides of the field and move to tag opponents upon the signal.
3) Teammates can join hands in groups of 1 to 3, combining their total ages.
4) When players tag each other, the side with lower total age surrenders 1 rubber band (10 yrs); reaching 0 bands requires 5 jumping jacks in the penalty zone to get 1 band back.
5) Sum the total number of outs for each team at the end; the team with fewer outs wins.

1) Set up five wrestling stations in the classroom (knee wrestling, arm wrestling, thumb wrestling, palm push wrestling, seated foot push wrestling) and a rock-paper-scissors area.
2) All students gather in the rock-paper-scissors area and play rock-paper-scissors with same-gender peers.
3) The winner chooses a wrestling station and takes the partner there to compete.
4) The winner receives 2 points and the loser receives 1 point, then both return to the rock-paper-scissors area to find new opponents until the highest scorer wins.

1) Form a team of 5 to 7 students standing in a circle with 1 ball.
2) One player tosses the ball into the center to bounce once, starting the rally.
3) Players hit the underside of the ball with their open palm so it bounces once inside the circle for teammates to hit.
4) Count the consecutive number of successful one-bounces until the ball bounces twice or hits an obstacle, aiming for the highest record.

1) Cluster desks into group islands ensuring clear walkways, and place 2 revival team vests on top of the desks.
2) Five throwers wear vests and roll 2 balls along the floor aiming at the runners' ankles.
3) A runner whose ankle is hit is out and must sit on a nearby desk.
4) Active runners hand a revival vest to an eliminated player; if that eliminated player throws the vest and hits an attacker, they revive, and teams count total outs over 5 minutes.

Bow, arrows, target board, ttakji paper tiles

1) Two partners stand side by side, each holding one handle of the jump rope with their outside hand.
2) Turn the rope together in sync and jump over the rope using a two-bounce jump.
3) Practice jumping while alternating feet to maintain a steady shared rhythm.
4) Progress into advanced variations such as one jumping, alternating every 4 jumps, continuous alternating jumps, and turns.

1) Grip the disc with the thumb on the labeled top surface, index finger on the rim, and remaining three fingers supporting underneath.
2) Stand sideways with feet shoulder-width apart and hold the disc at shoulder height.
3) Stand at the marker cone and throw towards the disc catcher on the count of one, two, three.

Foam discs, marker cones, disc catcher basket

2) Participants take turns taking 5 shots each toward the target.
3) Record and sum up the points based on which scoring ring the ball hits.
4) The player with the highest total score after 5 rounds wins.
Soccer balls, large target banner, score sheet

1) Two teams stand facing each other in parallel lines
2) The first runners of both teams sprint to the center and play rock-paper-scissors
3) The winner walks to the back of the line, while the loser runs a lap around their team line back to the front

1) Set up starting lines and mark zones 1 through 3 with cones for each team.
2) Runner 1 carries disc cones one at a time and places them at zones 1 through 3, completing 3 round trips.
3) Runner 2 runs out and collects the disc cones one by one back to the start, completing 3 round trips.
4) Subsequent runners alternate between placing and retrieving cones until the final runner finishes.

1) Set up nine cones in a 3-by-3 grid.
2) Both teams line up in single file, and the first three runners hold team vests at the starting line.
3) The first runner sprints out and places a team vest over one cone, then runs back.
4) From the fourth runner onward, players move an existing team vest to an empty cone, and the team that completes a straight line first wins.
9 cones, 6 team vests (3 each of two colors)

1) Students form a wide circle around a tagger in the center.
2) Outside players pass the ball with their feet to keep it away from the tagger.
3) The tagger must intercept the rolling ball using only their feet without using hands.
4) When the tagger intercepts the ball, the player who made the last pass becomes the new tagger.

1) Set up spot markers on the floor in a long U-shape path.
2) Both teams line up at opposite ends, and the first runners hop across the markers toward each other.
3) When they meet, they play rock-paper-scissors; the winner keeps moving forward while the loser's team sends the next runner.
4) The team whose runner successfully reaches the opponent's starting line wins the game.

1) The first runner of each team holds two fun sticks and places a ball on the floor.
2) At the starting signal, guide the ball between the two fun sticks around the cone and back to the starting line.
3) Hand over the fun sticks to the next runner upon returning.
4) The team whose final runner finishes first wins.

1) Crumple a sheet of A4 paper and unfold it onto your head like a hat.
2) Maintain balance while blowing to knock off opponents' paper hats.
3) Protect your own paper hat and do not stay in one spot for more than 3 seconds.
4) Players whose paper falls off must sit in place as obstacles; the last remaining player wins.

1) Form two teams facing each other behind starting lines.
2) Roll the dice, and when a team's color appears, that team chases to tag while the other team runs toward the cones.
3) Any player tagged before grabbing a cone is eliminated from the playing area.
4) The game can also be played with a rule variation where tagged opponents join the chasing team.

1) Divide into two teams and play rock-paper-scissors.
2) The winner sprints toward the ball while the loser sprints toward the cone.
3) The player with the ball scores by throwing and hitting the opponent before they return to the starting line.
4) The runner scores by dodging the ball or successfully carrying the cone back to the starting line.

1) Teams decide a playing order, designating riders to sit on rolling chairs and pushers.
2) From behind the baseline, pushers glide the seated teammate across the floor toward the target line.
3) The team stopping closest and most accurately to the target line wins the round.
4) Rotate roles each round so every student gets a chance to sit and push.

1) The fielding team disperses across the field while the kicking team kicks in order.

3) If a fly ball is caught directly, the kicker is out and runners cannot advance.

Tee-Ball: Basic Throwing Techniques and Step-by-Step Drills

1) Grip the ball with the index and middle fingers slightly spread on top, keeping it off the palm.
2) Practice wrist action by flicking the ball upward toward the target direction to feel finger release.
3) Kneel down, rotate the torso, raise the elbow, and release the ball with the fingers facing the target.
4) Stand up, step the front foot toward the target, and throw by sequentially transferring power from the torso, shoulder, elbow, wrist, and fingers.

1) Put the glove on the non-throwing hand and squeeze fingers to close the glove when the ball enters.
2) For ground balls, spread feet wider than shoulder-width, lower the body, catch in front of the toes, and cover with the right hand.
3) For fly balls, raise the glove and catch slightly to the left of the face, supporting the side of the glove with the right hand.
4) Practice playing catch with grounders and fly balls in pairs facing each other, or throw against a wall to catch rebounds.

1) Perform wrist stretching and ankle rotations alternately on both sides in place.
2) Place hands on hips and rotate neck and shoulders in sequence.
3) Perform torso/waist twists and knee rotations to loosen up the joints.
4) Do leg stretches (narrow/wide), arm and shoulder stretches, hip joint stretches, and finish with jumping jacks.

T-ball Equipment Exploration and Base-Running Basics

1) Set up the height-adjustable batting tee at home plate and place a T-ball on top.
2) Select an appropriately sized bat and wear the glove on the non-throwing hand.
3) Place rubber bases at 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and home plates.

batting tee, 3 bats, 3 T-balls, gloves, bases

1) The batter hits the ball off the tee and advances only one base; when the ball lands fair, all runners advance one base.
2) Fielders catch the ball and tag or step on the base while holding the ball before the runner arrives to record an out.
3) Three strikes (including three fouls or hitting the tee) results in an out; a runner crossing home plate scores 1 point.
4) Teams switch between offense and defense after every player bats once, and remaining base runners stay on base for the next inning.

Elementary Double-Base Limit Class-Match T-Ball Game

1) Batters hit inside the batting circle and run the bases, advancing up to a maximum of a double (except the final 10th batter who has no limit).
2) Runners must keep their foot on base until contact is made and cannot deviate beyond the 3-foot running lane.
3) Fielders get outs by stepping on the base while holding the ball, tagging the runner, or catching a fly ball (forcing runners to tag up).
4) Three strikes result in an out, and teams rotate through 10-player rosters balanced with boys and girls per half-inning.

1) Divide the class into two teams and designate a catcher with a basket on the head.
2) Start holding a rubber shoe and put it on at the shooting line.
3) Shoot the rubber shoe over the elastic cord obstacle into the catcher's basket.
4) The catcher catches it inside the defense line, and the shooter returns to high-five the next runner.
Rubber shoes, baskets, elastic cord, cones, team vests

1) Determine the player order through rock-paper-scissors with the last player becoming 'it'.
2) The first-place winner decides and gives a mission type such as Wangdaepo, Picnic, or Teacher Says.
3) The remaining players sequentially give commands of that type and 'it' follows them.
4) When 'it' completes all commanded actions, 'it' is freed and the next round begins.

1) Form groups of 4 and designate animal tiers using colored vests or paper.
2) Players only chase animals that are stronger than themselves.
3) After tagging, play rock-paper-scissors (muk-jji-ppa); if the weaker animal wins, they swap vests.
4) If the stronger animal wins, count to ten before pursuing again; the group with the tiger scores 1 point at round end.

1) Set up speed ladders, zigzag cones, and hurdles in order, and have the anchor wear a team vest.
2) On signal, all team members start in single file and navigate through the three obstacles.
3) Record the number of laps completed by the anchor in 3 minutes (1 point per lap, plus 0.5 points for over half a lap).
4) A 0.1-point penalty is given for each infraction such as stepping on ladder rungs or touching obstacles.
Speed ladders, dome cones, hurdles, team vests

1) Set up a rectangular playing area with cones and place hula hoops (energy refill station and star zone) at the end.
2) Divide players into offense and defense teams, placing offensive players along both sides outside the rectangle and defenders at the start line.
3) If hit by a ball (comet) rolled by the offense, defenders go to the refill station to recharge before returning to the start.
4) Defenders who cross the court collect a small marker and return to the start, switching roles after a set time.

1) Arrange hula hoops in a 3x3 or 5x5 grid on the floor.
2) Divide into two teams and line up behind the starting line.
3) Each runner carries a team vest, sprints to place it inside a hoop, and returns to tag the next runner.
4) Vests must be placed neatly without throwing, and players can move placed vests until one team completes a line to win.

1) Two players face each other, wrapping a thick rope around their waists in an S-shape to distribute force.
2) Hold the rope with one hand at the front of the abdomen and use the other hand behind the waist to grip firmly.
3) When the referee raises the flag, pull or release the rope; if an opponent's planted foot moves, score 1 point.
4) Switch sides and compete in a best-of-three match; if tied 1-1, continue in the same spots without switching.
Thick rope, team vests, referee flag

1) Draw a circular game court with marked paths and designated lanes on the playground ground.
2) Choose one tagger ("tiger") via rock-paper-scissors, who counts to 10 before chasing others.
3) All players must only move along the marked lines; if an evader enters the tiger's exclusive path, they become the tiger.
4) Both the tiger and evaders must stay strictly on their paths; tags made while the tiger is off-line do not count.

1) Set up only a home base on the field and divide players into kicking and fielding teams.
2) The kicker places the ball on home base, kicks it, and runs around their own team members for a set number of laps instead of running bases.
3) The fielding team lines up behind the player who caught the ball and passes it backward between their legs (tunnel).
4) The last fielder grabs the ball and sprints to touch home base; if they reach it before the runner finishes the laps, the kicker is out.
Ball, home base plate, team vests

1) Ready at center 0 of a cross hop mat (or line tape grid) with 50cm squares.
2) On signal, perform two-foot jumps in the sequence 0-1-0-2-0-3-0-4 to complete one cycle.
3) Jump for 20 seconds per person, scoring points for completed cycles and additional successful steps (1 point each).
4) A 1-point penalty is deducted each time a line is stepped on or the order is broken, and team scores are totaled.

1) Attach labels for Do, Gae, Geol, Yut, and Mo onto cones and space them out at a distance.
2) Prepare one set of large Yut sticks for each team.
3) Throw the Yut sticks upon the teacher's signal and check the resulting cast.
4) Run around the cone marker matching the cast result and return to the finish line first to win.

1) Form a circle around one central player, and assign numbers starting from 1 to all surrounding players.
2) The central player tosses the ball high into the air and calls out a number.
3) The player with the called number runs to the center to catch the ball.
4) If caught, that player moves to the center to toss next; if missed, the previous thrower tosses again and calls another number.

1) Select one tagger while the remaining players step inside a circle drawn appropriately according to the group size.
2) Players inside the circle push each other using their backs chanting "Yeongcha-yeongcha".
3) The tagger runs around the perimeter of the circle attempting to tag players in the center.
4) Anyone pushed out of the circle or tagged joins the tagger's team, continuing until only 1 final survivor remains.

1) Mark a spiral snail track on the ground with cones, and the defending team enters in single file.

3) Defenders dodge rolling balls along the track without overtaking teammates or stepping on boundary lines.

1) Divide into groups of 4 to 6 players and draw a circle approximately 6 meters in diameter on the floor.

1) Draw a segmented court on the field marking "Sky" (start), "Earth" (goal), and defense zones in between.

3) The attacking team starts from Sky, dodges defenders to reach Earth, and then runs back toward Sky.

1) Divide into two groups; two turners rotate a long jump rope while others sing and prepare.
2) One player from each group enters the turning rope and plays rock-paper-scissors while jumping.
3) The winner remains inside jumping, while the loser exits the rope.
4) The next player from the losing team enters to challenge the winner, and the team with the last surviving jumper wins.

1) Divide around 10 players into two equal teams across a net.

5) Play a best-of-3 sets match to 11 points, applying deuce rules at a 10-10 tie.

1) Form two co-ed teams with male and female students.

1) Form teams of 4 students each.
2) The first runner performs a standing long jump from the starting line.
3) The second teammate jumps forward from the exact landing mark of the previous jumper.
4) Continue in this relay format for all four teammates to measure the combined total distance.
5) Each team performs 2 attempts, and the better distance is recorded as the final result.

1) Divide all participating students into two teams.
2) Split the playing field in half with hula hoops placed in opponent territory, and cross the line to capture the opponent's ball upon the start signal.

4) If a player holding the ball is tagged out, the ball is left at that exact spot.
5) Win by successfully carrying the opponent's ball across into your own territory or by tagging out all opponents.

1) Divide students into two teams of 7 to 8 players lined up at the starting point.
