1) Three players set the ball or two players move while holding the ball to set up the attack.
2) After the referee's signal, call "Omnikin (team color)" and the designated hitter strikes the ball.
3) In fast-break tactics, run quickly to the landing spot to set up and have the fourth runner strike immediately.
4) Avoid moving more than 1.8 meters beyond the designated spot when hitting.
넷볼 교사팀 대 학생팀 실전 경기

1) Assign seven positions (GS, GA, WA, C, WD, GD, GK) and play within designated zones.
2) Advance the ball solely through passes without dribbling and score by shooting into the goal ring.
3) Rotate positions during the game so players can experience multiple roles.
Netball (or basketball), pinnies, netball goal posts

1) In 3v3 keep-away, complete 10 consecutive passes within a set space to score 1 point.
2) If the ball deflects off a defender out of bounds, subtract 1 from the pass count and continue.
3) In Netball Ultimate, start from your own end line and score by catching the ball in the opponent's end zone after at least 3 passes.
4) Possession switches upon turnovers, and standard netball fouls such as obstruction and contact apply.

1) A point is scored (Drop Ball) when the hit ball lands inside the court without being caught by the defending team.
2) All four teammates must touch the ball when hitting; touching another player's head or back causing a deflection results in a Contact Miss.
3) Call "Omnikin" followed by the opponent's color and hit the ball within 5 seconds after the referee's whistle.
4) Up to two players can move freely while holding the ball, but once a third player touches it, moving both feet is called a Walking foul.
플로어볼 경기 상황별 규칙 (페이스오프, 프리힛, 힛인)
플로어볼 스틱, 플로어볼 공, 골대, 링크(펜스), 골키퍼 보호장구(헬멧, 장갑, 무릎보호대)
Floorball Basic Rules: Face-off, Free Hit, Hit-in

1) Start play with a face-off at designated dots at the start of the match, after a goal, or after stoppages.
2) Hitting an opponent's stick, pushing, or raising the stick above knee level (high sticking) results in a free hit for the other team.
3) If the ball goes over the rink, restart with a hit-in placed 1 meter inside the rink from where it exited.
4) The player taking a hit-in or free hit cannot touch the ball twice in succession and must pass to a teammate.
Floorball sticks, floorball balls, goals, rink boards, goalkeeper gear (helmet, gloves, knee pads)
배드민턴 백핸드 서비스 및 릴레이 게임
Badminton Backhand Serve and Relay Drill

1) Grip the racket with a backhand grip and hold the shuttlecock feathers.
2) Place right foot forward with heel slightly raised and racket head below 1.15m.
3) Flick wrists outward to deliver the serve into the designated service court.
4) Conduct a 2-person relay game where pairs hit accurate serves into target zones.

1) Arrange 16 action hoops in a 4x4 grid on the floor.
2) Jump into two hoops with feet apart, move sideways to a 'one, two, one, two' beat, and return to center.
3) Jump forward one row and repeat the side-to-side movements with the two-beat rhythm.
4) Successfully complete all four rows and step out before the next student starts.

1) When the teacher calls out pirate-themed commands, students quickly perform the matching actions.
2) 'Port' runs left, 'Starboard' runs right, 'Captain' salutes, 'Scrub Deck' mops, and 'Seasick' runs back to pretend vomit.
3) 'Rowing' requires groups of 3 to sit and row, while 'Lunch Time' requires groups of 4 to pretend eating; unmatched students do star jumps.
4) The teacher inserts 'Captain' between commands to reset order, gradually speeding up commands.
솔방울 1개, 플라스틱컵 1개, 나무젓가락 2개, 끈 1개, 테이프, 글루건

1) Tape two wooden chopsticks together, tie a string 2 cm from the end, glue the chopsticks to a plastic cup, and secure a pinecone to the other end (about 60 cm) to make the equipment.
2) Practice swinging the pinecone to catch it in the cup twice in a row.
3) Play rock-paper-scissors with a partner; the winner attempts the challenge and wins by succeeding twice consecutively, while a miss passes the turn to the partner.
4) Compete to see who can achieve the highest consecutive catches with a partner as a witness, or try catching it using creative techniques.
1 pinecone, 1 plastic cup, 2 wooden chopsticks, 1 string, tape, hot glue gun

1) Set spot markers at the starting line and place hoops on the floor in a bowling pin or square layout.
2) Place numbered spot markers from 1 to 9 inside each hoop.
3) Roll a ball from the start line and score points indicated on the spot marker where it lands.
4) The first player of each team stands behind the hoops to collect balls and record scores.
Balls, hula hoops, numbered spot markers (1-9)

1) Step 1: Perform side steps moving left, right, behind, and in place.
2) Step 2: Slide forward with skating-like sliding steps.
3) Step 3: Tap left hand, right hand, hips, and clap hands to the rhythm.
4) Step 4: Walk backwards to the starting position and repeat along with the music.

1) The tagger holds a foam stick inside the designated area while other students stand around.
2) When the tagger calls out 'One Step', all students move exactly one step away.
3) The tagger also takes one step and tags nearby students with the foam stick.
4) Tagged students exit the area, complete 5 jumping jacks or 5 squats, and rejoin the game.
Table Tennis Ball Bounce Cup-Stacking Challenge

1) Pair up with one partner bouncing table tennis balls and the other holding Speed Stacks cups.
2) One teammate bounces a table tennis ball once on the floor toward the partner.
3) The other teammate catches the bounced ball directly inside their cup.
4) Each successfully caught cup is placed onto the table behind to stack 12 cups first to win.
12 Speed Stacks cups, table tennis balls, table
계란 포장하기 학습지, 스펀지 주사위, 색연필

1) Prepare a 36-egg grid worksheet and a sponge die, playing in pairs.
2) Take turns rolling the sponge die.
3) Group and circle the exact number of orthogonally adjacent eggs shown on the die.
4) The remaining eggs must match the die count exactly; the first player to package all 36 eggs wins.
Egg packaging worksheet, sponge die, colored pencils
Egg Carton Table Tennis Ball Tic-Tac-Toe

1) Place an egg carton on the floor or desk, and two players face each other at an equal distance.
2) Prepare table tennis balls of two different colors.
3) Bounce the ball with one or two bounces to land it inside an egg carton pocket.
4) The player who first aligns three of their balls horizontally, vertically, or diagonally wins.
Egg carton, table tennis balls, desk

1) Assign commands: 'Hand' for clapping, 'Desk' for tapping desk, and 'Foot' for stamping feet.
2) In stage 1, students repeat a 4-beat rhythm pattern demonstrated by the teacher.
3) Once comfortable, expand to an 8-beat two-measure rhythm pattern in stage 2.
4) Divide into two groups to play complementary beat patterns simultaneously to create harmony.
Egg Carton Table Tennis Ball Janggi Game

1) Place an egg carton between two players and line up 5 distinctively colored balls on each side.
2) Play rock-paper-scissors: Rock moves 1 space, Scissors 2 spaces, and Paper 3 spaces orthogonally.
3) Diagonal moves and jumping over other balls are strictly prohibited.
4) Land exactly on the opponent's space to capture their ball; capture all 5 opponent balls to win.

1) Practice pushing the puck with adjusted strength according to target distances on the board.
2) Slide pucks into four scoring compartments (1 to 4 points), noting that having pucks evenly in all four scores 10 bonus points.
3) Practice banking pucks off the side walls to understand rebound angles and force.
4) Aim and bank the puck off the side walls directly into desired scoring slots.

1) Set up a mini-net or rope across the classroom to divide the play area into two courts.
2) Start the game with a serve, keeping the balloon airborne using any body part (hands, feet, etc.) to hit it over the net.
3) Individual players are allowed to hit the balloon multiple consecutive times.
4) Players can block near the net during opponent attacks, and the rally ends in an out if the balloon touches the floor or outside objects.
Long Rope Jumping: Big Waves Small Waves and Little Kid

1) Two holders hold both ends of the long rope while the jumper moves into the center.
2) Sing 'Big wave, small wave, when the wind blows it turns, Monday through Sunday hurray' while jumping, then exit shouting hurray.
3) Turn the rope fully and perform actions according to 'Little kid, little kid, turn around, touch the ground, shout hurray, and goodbye'.
Ten Little Indians Long Rope Jumping

1) Two turners swing the long jump rope.
2) Players take turns jumping into the rotating rope one by one following the song lyrics.
3) After jumping on their number, players crouch down inside the rope to make room for the next jumper.
4) Continue until all ten jumpers are successfully inside the rope without stopping it.
넷볼 캐치와 패스 앤 무브 연습

1) In pairs, watch the incoming ball, execute a prep step, and land with a single step upon catching.
2) Keep one foot grounded, step forward with the other, and pass the ball like a basketball chest pass within 3 seconds.
3) Four players form a square and immediately step and pass to the next player without stopping upon catching.
4) Arrange six spots with one spot vacant for five players, where each player passes and immediately runs to the spot they passed to.

1) Stand tall with core engaged, interlace fingers behind the head, and gently stretch the neck downward for 10 seconds.
2) Place the right hand over the left ear to stretch the neck sideways, then repeat on the opposite side for 10 seconds.
3) Interlace fingers and use thumbs under the chin to gently stretch the neck upward for 10 seconds.
4) Interlace fingers, stretch overhead to the sides, and perform chest openers, back squeezes, and shoulder rolls sequentially.
Four-Step Bowling Approach and Swing Practice

1) Step 1 Push away: Push the ball forward.
2) Step 2 Down swing: Lower the swinging arm naturally downward.
3) Step 3 Back swing: Extend the arm backward and up.
4) Step 4 Forward swing: Swing forward smoothly to simulate ball release.
통합체육 보치아 축구공 사이즈 세트, 숫자 원형 마커, 점수판

1) Red and Blue teams sit facing each other on floor number spot markers with a white target ball placed in the center.
2) Determine the first team by rock-paper-scissors; player 3 throws the large ball toward the white target ball.
3) The opposing team's player 3 throws next, and subsequent throws are taken by the team whose ball is farther from the target.
4) Score points equal to the number of balls closer to the target ball than the opponent's closest ball; highest points win.
Inclusive boccia soccer-ball size set, number spot markers, scoreboard
골볼공(방울 소리 나는 공), 골볼체험 매트, 골볼 안대, 라인줄, 라인 테이프, 꼬깔콘

1) Set up goals using cones or mats on both ends, and mark the defender line, throw line, and high-ball line on the floor.
2) The thrower positions themselves without a blindfold, puts it on, and rolls the ball bouncing it before the high-ball line on the whistle.
3) Defenders feel the floor line to orient themselves, put on blindfolds, listen to the bell sound, and block using protective mats.
4) Each goal scored counts as 1 point, and each attacker gets one throwing attempt per turn.
Audible goalball ball, protective goalball mats, blindfolds, tactile boundary cord, floor tape, cones
골볼 전용 매트, 골볼 공, 시각스포츠 안대

1) Set up goalposts by spacing out goalball mats along the goal line.
2) Attackers wear eyeshades and roll the audible goalball from a close distance for lower grades or at least 7 meters away for upper grades.
3) Defenders wear eyeshades and listen carefully to track the trajectory of the rolling ball.
4) Defenders block the ball using their bodies or personal mats without sliding; a successful block concedes 0 points, while failing concedes 1 point.
쇼다운 전용 테이블, 소리 나는 구슬 공, 시각경기용 고글, 특수 장갑, 나무 라켓

1) Two players wear visual sports goggles and protective gloves, holding wooden bats.
2) Players strike the audible ball with the bat to rebound off the side walls or slide underneath the center board screen.
3) Scoring a ball into the opponent's goal pocket earns 2 points per goal.
4) The player who reaches 11 or more points with at least a 2-point lead wins.
Showdown table, audible ball, visual goggles, protective gloves, wooden bats
골볼체험 전용매트, 시각축구 체험 풍선공, 시각스포츠 안대, 시각러닝스트랩

1) Form 3-player teams where two sighted guides hold running straps on both sides and one blindfolded player stands in the middle.
2) At the goal kick line, the guided player identifies the ball's position with their hands assisted by guides.
3) One guide runs behind the mat goal and claps to indicate the target direction.
4) The blindfolded player listens to the clapping sound and kicks the ball toward the mat goal.
Goalball mat, balloon soccer ball, blindfold, running strap

1) In step 1, hold one ball, swing your arm downward, and toss it in an arc to catch it with the opposite hand, repeating smoothly.
2) Cushion the catch by lowering your hand slightly along with the ball's falling motion rather than stopping abruptly.
3) In step 2, hold a ball in each hand; toss the first ball, and when it reaches its peak, toss the second ball.
4) Catch each ball smoothly in sequence as they fall.
플라잉디스크 기초 및 경기 종목(윷놀이, 골프, 얼티미트)
Flying Disc Basics and Sports: Yutnori, Disc Golf, Ultimate

1) Learn basic throwing grips (backhand, forehand, upside-down) and catching techniques (two-hand, one-hand).
2) In Disc Yutnori, throw disc at target boards from a distance to move markers around the board to win.
3) In Disc Golf, groups of 4 throw discs into the disc catcher across 9 or 18 holes in the fewest throws.
4) In Ultimate, advance by passing without running while holding disc to score in the endzone, self-officiated by players.
Flying discs, disc catchers, target boards

1) Place a set number of marbles inside a drawn triangle.
2) Players throw a marble toward a line from the triangle; the closest to the line goes first, touching the line gets 1st, and going past makes you last.
3) Take turns rolling or throwing a marble to knock marbles out of the triangle; knock any marble out to keep going and claim it.
4) If your shooting marble stays inside the triangle or touches the line, you forfeit all collected marbles and are eliminated.
플로어볼 기초 기능 및 경기 방법
플로어볼 스틱, 플로어볼 볼, 미니 골대, 골키퍼 보호 장비

1) Practice fundamental skills including short dribble, long dribble, passing, and wrist/drag shooting.
2) Start play at the center mark with a face-off upon the referee's whistle.
3) Move the ball via passing and dribbling to shoot into the opponent's goal, with the team scoring more goals winning.
4) Resume with a hit-in if the ball leaves the rink, or a free hit with defenders 3m away upon fouls.
Floorball sticks, floorball balls, mini goals, goalkeeper protective gear
Futsal Passing Dribbling and Character Match

1) Pair up to practice inside foot passes, stepping toward the target and trapping with the sole, rotating partners counter-clockwise on signal.
2) Practice dribbling alternating between the outside and inside of the foot, stopping the ball with the sole if it rolls too far.
3) Organize small-sided futsal matches grouped by gender or skill level with team cheering and commentary.
Standing Long Jump Team Target Game

1) Balance players into Team A and Team B based on preliminary standing long jump records.
2) Establish a collective target distance for each team based on an achievable individual benchmark.
3) Establish a jumping order within each team and allow 10 to 15 minutes of structured team practice.
4) Take turns jumping by team while the waiting team observes for fouls and records; sum up all distances, and the team reaching closest to or exceeding the goal wins.

1) Form teams of 3 to 5 players of similar skill levels and have each player wear character bibs.
2) Before the match, teams discuss and decide on a group celebration, and select the opposing team's 'Daedani' (can only assist after 1 goal) and 'Deukjeomi' (scores 2 points per goal).
3) Begin and end the game by shaking hands and greeting each other at the center of the pitch.
4) Play for 5 to 10 minutes; after scoring, the entire team must gather and perform the predetermined celebration together for the goal to count.

1) Perform a 4-meter shuttle run, then sprint in to catch rolled or bounced dodgeballs and progress to full on-the-fly catches.
2) Designate 2 to 3 points and slide laterally using side steps to catch rolled and direct throws.
3) Move dynamically in multi-directional patterns (triangle or square) forward, backward, left, and right to catch incoming throws.
4) Navigate 10 zigzag points using backward steps while continuously receiving and catching dodgeball throws.

1) Students line up alongside, and each takes turns jumping in pairs alongside the instructor holding the jump rope.
2) Jump in sequence without tripping over the rope as turns pass down the line.
3) The student who trips the rope when time expires and the players on their immediate left and right receive the penalty.
4) The penalized group performs the designated penalty exercise (e.g., 5 repetitions).

1) Each player holds a sponge and prepares at their designated spot marker with their jump rope placed on the floor.
2) Walk around freely for 1 minute to play rock-paper-scissors with classmates, and the winner hands 1 sponge over to the loser.
3) When 1 minute ends, return to the spot and jump rope 10 times per accumulated sponge (e.g., 100 jumps for 10 sponges).
4) Complete the mission by flipping over 1 sponge every 10 jumps within the 1-minute time limit.

1) Run up at a moderate pace and take off by firmly stamping both feet slightly above the center of the springboard.
2) Place both hands firmly on the vaulting box at the two-thirds point or beyond the center.
3) Push off forcefully with hands while spreading legs wide apart to clear the box.
4) Land stably on both feet on the landing mat and raise both arms.
킨볼 기초 적응 놀이 및 릴레이

1) Practice popping and controlling the Kin-Ball upward by pulling it toward the body using hands and knees.
2) Do not grab the inflation valve and instead get underneath the ball to support it.
3) Conduct a Kin-Ball rolling relay where players round a cone, go around their teammates in line, and pass to the next runner.
4) Modify by having two players push from opposite sides or having all members move while supporting the ball with hands or heads.
킨볼 기초 경기 규칙과 서브 및 수비
Kin-Ball Basic Rules: Serve and Defense

1) Three teams of 4 players each (Pink, Grey, Black) compete on the court simultaneously.
2) When hitting (attacking), all 4 players must be touching the ball, and the hit must travel in a slight upward trajectory.
3) The 2nd and 3rd place teams must call the 1st place team, and the 1st place team must call the 2nd place team.
4) Receiving players may use any part of the body to keep the ball off the floor and must execute an attack within 10 seconds of initial contact.
체력 플랭크 자세 유지 기록 측정

1) Lie down in a plank position keeping head, shoulders, hips, knees, and ankles aligned, clasping hands with a 90-degree angle between hands, elbows, and shoulders.
2) Rest knees on the floor and start the plank with the audio signal.
3) Measure the duration until the posture breaks down.

1) Mark three shooting spots 90 cm away from the goalpost (height 3.05 m): left (A), center (B), and right (C).
2) Attempt the first shot from spot A using either a one-handed or two-handed shooting technique.
3) You may only advance to the next spot (A to B to C) upon making a shot; if you miss, you must shoot again from the same spot until successful.
4) Measure the total number of successful baskets scored within 1 minute while cycling through spots A, B, and C.

1) Face the wall, throw the ball against the wall, and begin with the rebound.
2) Alternate between underhand and overhand passes against the wall.
3) Count the number of successful consecutive passes completed in 1 minute.
4) If the ball is caught or drops to the floor, retrieve it and resume continuing from the previous count.

1) Prepare with a jump rope of any type and length.
2) On the starting signal, perform double unders continuously for 30 seconds.
3) If caught by the rope, resume jumping immediately.
4) Stop upon hearing the finish signal and count the total number of successful double unders within 30 seconds.
십자 구역 매트 또는 테이프(가로 50cm, 세로 50cm 칸 4개)

1) Stand at the center start area of a cross-shaped court with four 50cm x 50cm squares.
2) On the start signal, jump with both feet together in order: Start to 1, Start, 2, Start, 3, Start, 4.
3) Repeat the designated hopping sequence as many times as possible for 15 seconds.
4) Jumps where lines are stepped on or wrong orders are hopped will be excluded from the score count.
cross hop grid or tape (four 50cm x 50cm squares)

1) Fold a standard towel once, lay it on the floor, and stand behind it.
2) On the start signal, jump forward with both feet straddling the sides of the towel, land in front, and perform a burpee.
3) Jump back straddling the towel sides to the rear starting point to complete 1 repetition.
4) Measure the total time taken to complete 10 full repetitions through the final landing.

1) Place an eared pitch-pot in the center of an open yard or flat ground.
2) Divide players into two opposing teams.
3) Stand at a throwing distance approximately ten paces away from the pot.
4) Each player throws 12 red or blue arrows toward the pot, and the team that lands the most arrows in the jar or side ears wins.

1) Set up single, double, triple, and home run desks as well as home, 1st, 2nd, and 3rd bases in the classroom, then divide into three teams.
2) During offense, every student takes turns hitting a ball bounced off a desk to score points.
3) On a single, runners and batter advance 1 base; on a double, 2 bases; on a triple, 3 bases; on a home run, all score.
4) A batter is out if hitting before bouncing, failing to hit after bouncing, or missing the desk entirely.
SODA POP Easy Music Rope Skipping

1) Skip with side-to-side and front-back 2-count jumps followed by two-feet 1-count jumps during the intro.
2) Alternate left-right moving steps and front-back moving steps twice each during the verses.
3) Combine straddle jumps with lateral hops, followed by scissors jumps with front-back hops.
4) Transition through alternate foot jumps, ending with open-cross (SO, CO) step patterns.

1) Jump continuously to the music through the sequence: two-foot basic jump 1-bounce, 2-bounce, jogging step, side-straddle, front-and-back cross, and boxing step without tripping.
2) Begin the endurance jump challenge when announced at the song chorus.
3) Any participant who trips on the rope must immediately sit down in place.
4) Participants who continue jumping without tripping until the music finishes succeed in the mission.

1) Team members sit in a straight line in sequence.
2) On the starting signal, the first player grips the ball with both feet, lifts it, and passes it to the next teammate without dropping it.
3) The last teammate places the received ball into the hoop; if the ball is dropped midway, it goes back to the first player to restart.
4) The team that puts the most balls into the hoop within the set time wins.
콩주머니, 원마커, 후프, 바구니, 모둠 조끼

1) Form a team of four students and line up in a single file.
2) One player at a time hops on one foot while keeping balance to pick up a beanbag and hop back.
3) If any body part other than the hopping foot touches the ground or lands outside the spot marker, the turn passes to the next team and any collected beanbag must be returned.
4) The team that collects the most beanbags within the given time limit wins.
beanbags, spot markers, hoops, baskets, team pinnies
플로어볼 채, 플로어볼 공, 골대, 모둠 조끼

1) Dribble: Control and move the ball with the floorball stick, keeping it below waist height.
2) Pass: Send the ball to a teammate using the floorball stick.
3) Catch: Receive an incoming ball using the floorball stick.
4) Shoot: Strike the ball into the opponent's goal using the floorball stick.
floorball sticks, floorball balls, goals, team pinnies

1) Draw a large circle and everyone steps inside.
2) Everyone sits down and clasps their hands under their buttocks.
3) Push to knock down opponents at the teacher's start signal.
4) Anyone who falls or crosses the line goes outside the circle, and the team with the last remaining player wins.

1) Hand Wrestling: Stand with right feet facing each other, hold right hands, and push and pull to break the opponent's balance.
2) Pig Wrestling: Squat down, wrap arms under knees to clasp hands, and push with legs without lifting the buttocks off the floor.
3) Palm Wrestling: Face each other with palms raised and push or dodge palms to make the opponent lose balance.
4) Back/Foot/Rope Wrestling: Push back-to-back, push soles of feet together, or pull ropes behind the waist to break balance.

1) Draw a hopscotch court on the ground and toss a stone into square 1.
2) Skip the square with the stone, hopping on two feet for side-by-side squares and one foot for single squares up to square 8.
3) At square 8, jump with both feet to turn around and hop back in reverse.
4) Pick up the stone on the way back, return to start to throw into the next square; touching a line passes the turn.

1) Select about one tagger per five players and designate a base for the tagger to guard.
2) The tagger stays at the base while other players run far away from it.
3) Caught players must hold onto the base; multiple captured players hold hands in a chain waiting to be freed.
4) If a runner tags the base or chain while avoiding the tagger, they are rescued; the game ends when all are caught.

1) Divide into two teams with batons and line up facing each other along a single straight line.
2) The first runners hold their baton and walk along the line placing heel-to-toe.
3) When meeting an opponent, play body rock-paper-scissors; the loser returns to hand off the baton while the winner advances.
4) Reaching the opponent's starting cone scores a point before returning to hand off the baton; the team with the most points wins.

1) Eight students form a circle with hands on hips facing the center.
2) Facing pairs step forward to the beat, clap each other's hands, and return to their positions.
3) Other pairs take turns walking toward the center, clapping hands, and returning.
4) Join hands with partners and rotate in a circle before finishing the sequence.

1) Eight students form a circle holding hands.
2) Move around in a circle or move toward the center and back to music.
3) Face a partner, clap hands, and perform folk dance steps.

1) Choose two students to hold the limbo rope taut so it does not sag.
2) Lean back with the chest tilted and pass under the rope without letting the body touch it.
3) Start at shoulder height and gradually lower the rope; players who clear it line up again, while those who fail return to their seats.
4) The player who survives the longest wins.

1) Choose one tagger.
2) Place a beanbag on the back of the hand and dodge the tagger while keeping it balanced.
3) A player is eliminated if they drop the beanbag or are tagged by the tagger.
4) If the tagger drops their beanbag, the game ends and a new tagger is chosen; the last remaining runner becomes the tagger for the next game.

1) Hold the hula hoop with both hands at waist height.
2) Stand with feet about 10 cm apart and place one foot forward to keep balance.
3) Rest the hoop against one side of the torso and spin it firmly with the hands while rotating the hips and waist in a circular motion.
4) Place the right foot forward when spinning to the right, and the left foot forward when spinning to the left, practicing both directions or the preferred side.

1) Divide into teams, set up one mat per team, and line up behind the starting line.
2) The first runner hops on both feet like a rabbit from the starting line to the start of the mat.
3) Stretch arms and legs straight and log-roll sideways along the entire length of the mat.
4) Stand up at the end of the mat, sprint back to tag the next teammate's hand, and sit at the back; the team whose final runner finishes first wins.

1) Divide the class into two teams and select one tagger per team who wears sticker markers on chest and back.
2) Both teams enter their designated court areas and start playing upon the signal.
3) Throw the ball at opponents, aiming strictly below chest level.
4) Hit players move outside the court to attack from the perimeter, and the team that hits the opposing tagger first wins.

1) Divide the class into four teams, determine running order, and line up behind a cone for each team.
2) On the start signal, the first runner of each group carries a baton and runs one full lap back to the start.
3) When the first runner starts, the second runner steps up to the starting line and waits to receive the baton.
4) Pass the baton to the second runner and move to the back; the team whose members all finish a lap first wins.

1) Draw a foul line and target line 3 to 4 meters apart, divide into two teams, and decide offense/defense via rock-paper-scissors.
2) The defending team sets up blocks, and attackers throw or carry their block on their body to knock down target blocks.
3) Progression: One-foot hop, Standing throw, Chin clamp, Rice cake seller (forehead), Instep kick, Belly carry, Newspaper delivery (armpit).
4) Switch turns if failing to knock down all target blocks; advance to the next challenge upon knocking them all down.

1) Divide the class into two teams, decide throwing orders, and line up behind the starting line.
2) On signal, the first player holds a beanbag and balances on one foot.
3) Hop forward on one foot up to the line and toss the beanbag toward the cone.
4) Earn 1 point if the beanbag lands inside the hula hoop; the team with the higher score wins.

1) Divide into offense and defense teams, marking a large boundary line for students to fit inside.
2) Attackers stand outside the boundary and push a big ball with both hands from chest height toward defenders inside.
3) Defenders move only inside the area; stepping out or touching the ball eliminates them to become outside attackers.
4) Defense wins if anyone survives the time limit; offense wins if all defenders are eliminated.

1) Draw a ship shape on the floor and place spot markers (1/3 to 1/2 of the number of players) around the area.
2) One tagger becomes the shark, counts 5 seconds at the corner, and chases players who disperse from the center.
3) The ship and spot markers are safe islands where sharks cannot tag, but players must leave after 5 seconds without immediately re-entering.
4) Tagged players become taggers to continue the game, and sharks cannot camp outside safe zones.

1) Have students face away so they cannot see, spread disc cones across the area, and hide small snacks or candies underneath.
2) On signal, players flip disc cones one by one to find the hidden treasure.
3) The game ends when a player finds the treasure first or within the time limit.
4) For higher difficulty, players balance a disc cone on their head while searching, returning to the start if it drops.
Disc cones, candies or small snacks

1) Crumple the scarf with both hands, toss it high above the head, and catch it.
2) Toss the scarf high, clap hands or spin in a circle, and catch it before it lands.
3) Toss the scarf and catch it using different body parts such as the head, shoulder, knee, or foot.
4) Balance the scarf on a body part while walking around cones without dropping it, or play a tail-tag game.
Volleyball Fundamentals Step-by-Step Practice (Receive, Toss, Spike)

1) Tap a suspended volleyball with one or both hands to get familiar with ball contact.
2) Practice underhand passes (receives) with bent knees and overhand sets (tosses) forming a triangle above the forehead.
3) Swing arms back like skiing, jump, and practice hitting the suspended ball in a spike motion.
4) Across a net in pairs, practice throwing and catching, passing after one bounce, and playing mini rally games.
만보기 차고 하루 1000번 움직이기 실내 맨손운동

1) Fasten a pedometer to the arm or hold it in hand, and reset the counter to zero.
2) Swing both arms forward and backward 20 times, then march in place swinging opposite arms and legs 20 times.
3) Extend arms forward and pull inward 20 times, reach upward and pull down 20 times, and roll shoulders backward and forward 20 times each.
4) Lie on the floor to perform diagonal hand-to-foot touches 20 times and modified crunches 20 times to accumulate steps.
구슬이 든 스태킹 컵 핀, 바닥 표시 테이프

1) Mark a 1-meter line and a target circle on the floor with tape and set a starting line.
2) Decide turns via rock-paper-scissors and alternately slide cup pins containing marbles across the floor.
3) A cup is out if it crosses the 1-meter line or goes off course; players may bump opponent pins away.
4) The team that lands a cup inside the target circle or closest to the line wins.
Stacking cup pins with marbles, floor marking tape
One, Two, Three, Shoot! Football Game

1) Draw a rectangular pitch and a starting line on the court facing a goal.
2) Form teams of 4 to 6 players into offense and defense, designating one goalkeeper on defense.
3) The attacking team starts from the starting line, dribbles and passes the ball, while defenders try to block them.
4) Every attacking player must touch and pass the ball at least once before scoring a goal for 1 point; if intercepted, attack restarts from the starting line.

1) Choose 2 or more taggers as spiders depending on the group size.
2) At the signal, one spider guards home while other spiders chase and catch bees to bring them home.
3) The first caught bee touches home base, and subsequent caught bees hold hands in a chain.
4) If a free bee breaks the linked hands, bees on the outside of the break run away.

1) Form groups of three and stand in a straight line between cones from the start to finish line.
2) On signal, the first player throws the disc to the second, who catches and throws it to the third player.
3) If a disc is dropped, it is returned to the thrower who must throw it again.
4) The group whose final player successfully catches the disc first wins.

1) Form teams of 4 runners and stand at designated positions.
2) On the starting signal, the first runner of each team starts running.
3) Run one lap around the oval course and hand off the baton to the next runner.
4) The team whose anchor finishes first wins.
Spot markers, disc cones, relay batons, team pinnies
원마커, 츄크볼, 츄크볼 골대, 모둠 조끼

1) Form two teams of 3 players each and line up outside the goal line.
2) The offense dribbles and completes 3 passes among teammates before shooting at the rebound frame.
3) If the defenders fail to catch the rebound off the net, the attacking team scores 1 point.
4) If the defense catches the rebound or the shot misses the frame entirely, possession switches.
Spot markers, tchoukball, tchoukball rebound frames, team pinnies

1) Kneel on one knee in a large circle.
2) One 'it' player stands in the center of the circle.
3) On the start signal, players in the circle roll the big ball to hit the center player.
4) The player who hits the center player switches roles to become the new 'it'.

1) Divide into two teams and line up in order in front of the mats.
2) On the signal, perform a log roll sideways across the mat until reaching the end.
3) The player who reaches the end and grabs the cone first scores 1 point for their team.
4) The team with the most points within the allotted time wins.

1) Form teams of 5 players to shoot into the opponent's basket while defending their own.
2) Move by dribbling the ball and do not take three or more steps while holding the ball with both hands.
3) Score 3 points outside the arc, 2 points inside, and 1 point for each successful free throw.
4) Comply with violation rules including the 24-second shot clock, 8-second backcourt, 5-second inbound, and 3-second key restriction.

1) Divide into two teams, determine the first turn with rock-paper-scissors, and throw stones toward the house from a set distance.
2) Kneel on one knee or cross legs, rolling the stone with all bottom wheels contacting the floor.
3) Stones that fail to cross the hog line or are released over the throw line are removed as fouls.
4) The end concludes when all stones are thrown; the team with the stone closest to the house center wins the end and throws first next.
농구 드리블 조끼 뺏기 및 공 뺏기 게임
Basketball Dribble Pinny Steal and Ball Knockout Game

1) Mark the boundary area with cones, give each student a basketball, and tuck a team pinny into each waist.
2) Move around inside the designated area while maintaining a continuous dribble.
3) Dribble while attempting to pull other players' pinnies and throw them outside the area.
4) Any student who loses their pinny or has their ball pushed outside must leave the boundary until one player remains.

1) Place 3 sets of 3-stack cups on the floor at 3-meter intervals.
2) At the starting signal, run toward the turning point, up-stacking all 3 sets of 3-stacks sequentially.
3) Round the turning point and return to the starting line while down-stacking all 3 sets of 3-stacks.
4) The team whose runners complete the relay and return to the finish line first wins.
3 sets of stacking cups (9 cups total), 2 cones

1) Set up 12 stacking cups on a table opposite the starting line.
2) At the signal, run to the table and perform the complete Cycle Stacking sequence (3-6-3 up-stack/down-stack → 6-6 up-stack/down-stack → 1-10-1 up-stack/down-stack ending in 3-6-3).
3) After finishing the down-stack and organizing into a 3-6-3 setup, sprint back to the starting line to tag the next runner.
4) The team whose runners complete the cycle relay with fewer mistakes first wins.

1) Set up a portable net in the center of a rectangular court and form two teams of three players each.
2) Start the game by hitting a balloon over the net using small implements within the designated court area.
3) All team members must hit the balloon once before sending it over the net.
4) If a team fails to receive the balloon or return it to the opponent's area, the opposing team scores 1 point, and the first team to reach 10 points wins.

1) Step onto the balance beam sideways with one foot first, spreading arms to balance.
2) Check the landing spot and dismount lightly with both feet while keeping arms extended.
3) Hold single-leg balance and try various balance poses on the beam.
4) Face a partner and hold hands to balance together.

1) Players take turns serving by tossing the ball with their hands into the opponent's court.
2) The incoming ball can be played either in the air or off one bounce, using any part of the body.
3) Every player on the team must touch the ball at least once before returning it.
4) The final shot over the net must be made using only the feet or head; the first team to reach 15 points wins.
피클볼 기초 기술 및 간이 게임

1) Serve underhand below the waist from behind the baseline diagonally into the opponent's service court.
2) Apply the two-bounce rule where both the serve and the return must bounce once before being hit.
3) Volleys are allowed from the fourth shot onward, and no volleys are permitted inside the non-volley zone (kitchen).
4) The game is won by the team that reaches 11 or 15 points first.
Hula Hoop Ball Bounce Pass Challenge

1) Two players face each other in pairs, each holding one side of a hula hoop.
2) On the start signal, one player bounces a volleyball on the floor through the hoop.
3) The opposite player catches the bounced ball and bounces it back through the hoop.
4) Count the number of successful passes fully cleared through the hoop within the time limit.

1) Four players form a team and two teams play against each other.
2) The game starts with a serve from outside the court, and the ball must be sent over the net within three touches.
3) Only feet and head can be used to send the ball, hands are not allowed, and the ball cannot bounce more than once on the floor.
4) A team scores 1 point if the opposing team fails to return the ball, the scoring team serves next, and the first team to win 3 sets of 15 points wins.

1) In Flying Disc Passing, 3 players form a team and line up to pass the disc sequentially, earning 1 point when the last player throws it into the disc catcher, with the highest score winning within the set time.
2) In Flying Disc Putting, 4 players form a team and take turns throwing the flying disc, scoring the points indicated where the disc lands, with the highest score winning.

1) Five players form a group, dividing into offense and defense groups.
2) Offensive players dribble and step on red, yellow, and green circular markers in order before heading to the scoring area.
3) Defenders can steal the ball only when it leaves the offensive player's hands, and tagged-out attackers are eliminated.
4) Teams switch roles, and the team with more players reaching the scoring zone wins.
Basketballs, red, yellow, and green spot markers

1) Divide players into a ball-rolling group and a ball-dodging group.
2) The rolling group pairs up in teams of four to roll big balls along the boundary lines.
3) The dodging group waits at the starting line and runs to the finish line avoiding the big balls; players touched by a ball must exit the court.
4) Teams switch roles, and the team with the most members successfully reaching the finish line wins.

1) Choose a vault height suitable for your skill level and select vaulting movements you can perform.
2) Decide the order of the chosen movements and practice them.
3) Present the practiced routine in front of your classmates.
4) Identify and compliment the classmate who performed the best vaulting routine.
하키 스틱(채), 공, 간이 골대, 보호 헬멧

1) Six players form a group to play a match against another group, with each team designating one goalkeeper.
2) The offensive team passes or dribbles the ball with sticks into the opponent's area.
3) Attackers cannot enter the semi-circle in front of the goal and must shoot from outside; possession switches upon scoring or a turnover.
4) The team scoring more goals within the designated time wins.
Hockey sticks, hockey balls, mini goals, protective helmets

1) Divide the class into 4 groups and set the jumping order for each group.
2) The first jumper runs up, steps on the spot marker at the start line with one foot, jumps, and places a marker at the landing spot.
3) The next jumper runs up, steps on that marker with one foot, jumps forward, and marks their landing spot.
4) All group members take turns jumping in relay fashion, and the group that reaches the furthest distance wins.

1) Check the springboard position and perform a controlled approach run
2) Look toward the hand placement spot, reach forward, and take off forcefully so the hips rise above head level
3) Place hands on the front section of the box, tuck the head deeply between arms, and roll in order: hands, back of head, back, waist, buttocks
4) Bend knees slightly upon landing on the mat to absorb shock, extending both arms sideways to maintain balance

1) Squat facing away on the mat with feet together, hands above shoulders palms facing up.
2) Shift weight back, push feet, and bring knees close to chest when back touches mat.
3) Tuck chin, keep body rounded, and push the mat forcefully with both hands to stand.
4) For straddle backward roll, straighten and spread legs sideways while rolling, then push mat to stand.

1) Five players per team; the batting team decides the batting order and designated spot markers.
2) The batter hits the ball with a fist and scores 1 point by retrieving their chosen marker home.
3) The batter is out if defense catches the fly ball or throws the ball home first.
4) Teams switch sides after all batters finish, and the team with more points wins.
앞, 뒤, 콩, 콩, 콩, 기차놀이
Front, Back, Hop, Hop, Hop Train Game

1) Four players form a line, placing hands on the shoulders of the player in front.
2) Jump forward or backward with both feet together following the rhythm call.
3) When meeting another train, the front players play rock-paper-scissors.
4) The losing leader moves to the back of the winning train; the longest train wins.

1) Divide the class into two teams, with each team standing at opposite ends of the balance beam.
2) Set the order, and the first players step onto the beam to play rock-paper-scissors.
3) The winner stays on the beam, while the loser jumps off the beam.
4) The winner continues playing against the next opponent; the last surviving team wins.

1) Five players per team play against each other.
2) Move into the opponent's court by dribbling or passing the ball.
3) Score 1 point by shooting into the hoop, and 2 points if every teammate passed before scoring.
4) Turnovers occur when losing possession or out of bounds; the team with more points wins.

1) Prepare behind the hoops in a bending posture.
2) On the start signal, move the beanbags from your hoop into the opponent's hoop.
3) Both feet touching the ground must not lift off, and players must bend their bodies to move the beanbags.
4) Play continues for a set time, and the player with the fewest beanbags in their hoop wins.

1) Players move into the opponent's territory while controlling the ball with the stick.
2) The stick must not touch an opponent's body, and the blade of the stick must not be raised above knee level.
3) A team scores a point by putting the ball into the opponent's goal.
4) The goalkeeper can block the ball using their entire body.

1) The whole class is divided into two teams, and each team decides the throwing order for the flying disc.
2) Players take turns throwing the flying disc toward the target board.
3) Move the game pieces according to the target square hit by the disc; if the disc misses the target board, pieces cannot be moved.
4) The team whose game pieces all reach the finish line first wins.
Flying disc, target board, game pieces

1) Seven players form a team and two teams play against each other.
2) Players pass the flying disc to teammates to move forward, scoring 1 point when receiving the disc inside the scoring zones at either end of the field.
3) Players cannot move while holding the flying disc, and defenders can intercept or catch the disc to take possession.
4) Possession switches to the opposing team if the disc is dropped after touching the hand or after a score, and the team with the higher score within the set time wins.

1) The batter tosses the ball up, hits it with a fist, and runs bases.
2) If the defense catches the hit ball before it touches the ground, the batter is out.
3) If the thrown ball reaches the base before the runner arrives, the runner is out.
4) Teams switch between offense and defense when three outs are made.

1) Score points by dropping the ball into empty spaces on the opposing team's court.
2) The ball must be sent to the opposing court within three touches.
3) One player must not touch the ball twice in a row.
4) The body must not touch the net.

1) Four players form a team, two teams play, and each team sets the order of rolling.
2) The team that wins rock-paper-scissors rolls first toward the center circle, alternating turns.
3) Players can push away the opponent's balls by rolling their ball.
4) After everyone has rolled, the team with more balls closest to the center wins.
다리 벌려 뜀틀 뛰어넘기 기본 기능 익히기

1) Take a running approach from 5-10m away, adjusting stride 3-4 steps before takeoff.
2) Maintain approach speed and take off powerfully with both feet using elasticity.
3) Lean slightly forward, place hands on roughly 2/3 of the vault, and lift your head.
4) Spread legs wide, pull your body forward, release hands, and land with knees bent.

1) Stand with feet together, place hands shoulder-width apart on the mat, and tuck chin looking back.
2) Push the mat with both feet, keep chin tucked so back of head touches mat, rolling rounded.
3) Hug legs, bring knees close to chest, and stand up keeping balance.
4) For straddle roll, extend and spread legs when back touches mat, then push the mat to stand.

1) Divide the class into two teams and tuck scarves behind waists to form tails.
2) On the start signal, grab the other team's tails; tagged players step off the court.
3) Captured tails can be given to eliminated teammates so they can rejoin the game.
4) The team that captures all of the opposing team's scarves wins.

1) Warm up with neutral stances, bent-over stretches, and squats.
2) Learn the opening arm lifts, ch-ap steps, and bouncing steps to the tempo of 'To You'.
3) Practice the chorus section with high arm extensions and rotating steps.
4) Stand in a straight line and execute ripple wave timing and left-right formation changes.

1) Prepare 3 cups nested together in the center.
2) Up-stack by taking one cup with the right hand and placing another cup on top with the left hand.
3) Down-stack by bringing the top cup down with the right hand and placing the remaining cup with the left hand.
4) Start the spacebar timer, complete 3-cup stacking as quickly as possible, and stop the timer.

1) Hold one ball in each hand positioned at shoulder level.
2) Toss vertically with the dominant hand and catch, then toss vertically with the non-dominant hand and catch.
3) Once comfortable, toss inside and outside shoulder width, shifting gaze to the next ball at its peak to throw simultaneously upon catching.
4) Perform 8 rounds every minute on the minute transitioning through shoulder, inner, and outer widths.

1) Prepare 12 cups, set 1 cup on each side (one flipped), and grab 5 with the right hand and 4 with the left from the center 10 cups.
2) Up-stack into a 4-3-2-1 pyramid using alternating hands starting from the center cup.
3) Down-stack into a 3-6-3 formation using the side cups by sliding diagonally to the right, then gripping all right cups and 1 left cup diagonally to the left.
4) Collect all cups into a single column after down-stacking and repeat 10 times to measure total time.

1) Prepare 6 cups stacked in a single column in the center.
2) Pick up 3 cups with the right hand and 2 cups with the left hand, leaving 1 cup on the surface.
3) Alternate right and left hands to up-stack into a 3-2-1 pyramid.
4) Down-stack by gripping the top cup with the right hand and the cup below it with the left hand, sliding them downward in a V-shape, then nesting the remaining cups.
저글링 양손 번갈아 반박자 대각띄우기 도전
Juggling Alternating Half-Beat Diagonal Toss Challenge

1) Start with the dominant hand to toss both balls diagonally on a half-beat rhythm and let them drop to learn the tempo.
2) Toss on a half-beat starting with the right hand and practice catching with only the opposite hand.
3) For right-handers, toss and catch with both hands in a strict 'right-left-left-right' half-beat sequence.
4) Perform 8 rounds every minute on the minute progressing from dominant hand first to alternating starts.

1) Prepare 9 cups by dividing them into 3 stacks of 3 cups each.
2) Choose a direction (left or right) and perform up-stacking sequentially.
3) Down-stack in the same direction that up-stacking was performed.
4) Practice 3-3-3 stacking in your preferred direction and record your completion time.

1) Prepare a juggling ball of palm size using socks or beanbags.
2) Toss a ball vertically above head level using the dominant hand and catch it 5 times.
3) Perform the same vertical toss with the non-dominant hand 5 times.
4) Perform 4 rounds of every-minute-on-the-minute vertical tosses alternating hands each round.

1) Divide into two teams; the attacking team consecutively passes the ball among teammates while avoiding defenders.
2) The teacher counts the consecutive completed passes aloud starting from one.
3) If the defending team intercepts the ball, the accumulated count resets to zero and possession switches.
4) Traveling with the ball is prohibited (pivoting only), and the first team to reach the target number (15 passes) wins.

1) Prepare one official dodgeball and one big volleyball, then divide students into two teams.
2) Assign 3 outfield defenders per team before starting the game.
3) Team representatives play rock-paper-scissors to decide offense and defense, then start play.
4) When only 3 infielders remain on either team, the initial 3 outfielders return to the infield, and the game ends when all are out.

1) Teams play on a designated court and are free to attack either bounce frame at both ends.
2) Players must not hold the ball over 3 seconds, take more than 3 steps, or exceed 3 passes before shooting.
3) Players shoot toward the bounce frame without stepping on or inside the 3m forbidden zone.
4) The attacking team scores 1 point if the rebounded ball hits the ground before the defense catches it.
Home Full Body Tabata Workout Round 1

1) Check the surroundings and clear away any hazards to ensure a safe space.
2) Perform four full-body exercises (jumping jacks, elbow-to-knee touches, slow burpees, and planks) for 20 seconds each with 10 seconds of rest.
3) Complete two full cycles of the four exercises (2 minutes per set) for a total 4-minute workout.

1) Place one half-cut sheet of paper on the floor and step on it with one foot.
2) Balance on that single foot while placing the other paper strip on top of your head.
3) Bend your head forward to let the paper slip and fall.
4) Catch the falling paper with your hand before it touches the ground: Level 1 standing, Level 2 bent knee, Level 3 leg extended backward.
소형 골대 2개, 폼볼 1개, 팀 조끼, 원마커

1) Divide into two teams, wear team pinnies, and sit on the gymnasium floor with bottoms touching the ground
2) Move by sliding without lifting bottoms off the floor while executing passes and dribbles between teammates
3) Advance into the opposing half and shoot the ball into the small goal to score points
4) Defenders remain seated and extend arms to intercept passes or tag attackers to disrupt offensive plays
2 mini goals, 1 foam ball, team pinnies, spot markers

1) Explore the ball's properties by throwing, catching, and bouncing 1-2 fleece balls off various body parts
2) Hold one ball in each hand and practice throwing one upward while quickly transferring the other across
3) Once comfortable, use three fleece balls to create continuous alternating arcs in the air
4) Set specific goals (such as 2 or 3 consecutive catches) and practice without dropping the balls
Forward Roll with Propulsion Using Obstacles and Vaulting Box

1) Set up obstacles on the mat and practice shifting center of gravity and pushing off with feet while placing hands
2) Connect a jump directly into a forward roll to build forward momentum
3) Once confident on high jump mats, practice rolling on top of a narrow vaulting box
4) After a run-up, place hands as far forward as possible and focus on controlled landing
mats, high jump mat, vaulting box, obstacles

1) Divide into two teams and position players on opposite sides of the volleyball net
2) In stage 1, catch and pass the ball so it crosses over the net on exactly the second contact
3) In stage 2, return the ball on the third contact, allowing a player to catch a set, jump, and spike or throw it downward
4) Once familiar, transition from catching to continuous underhand and overhand rallies without holding the ball
volleyball net, net posts, foam balls

1) Hold the top of the stick with one hand and lower down with the other to ensure proper control.
2) Use both sides of the stick blade to dribble the ball with short touches.
3) Shift body weight with feet apart to pass and receive the ball with a partner.
4) Shift weight forward to execute an accurate shot at a stationary ball.

1) Practice the basic motion on the floor by placing hands and spreading legs as wide as possible upon landing.
2) Place the vaulting box horizontally and jump over it while reaching hands as far forward as possible.
3) Set up obstacles like cones or mini-hurdles to maintain running momentum without stopping before the box.
4) Place the vaulting box vertically, gradually increase the height, and jump over by placing hands at the far end.
고무밴드와 판자를 활용한 배구 언더패스 기초 연습
Volleyball Underhand Pass Basics with Elastic Bands and Boards

1) Put elastic bands around feet and lower body center while maintaining shoulder-width stance.
2) Move only one foot to adjust to ball drop position and bump the ball using a wooden board.
3) Squeeze a small ball between elbows to keep arms straight and perform underhand passes.
4) Once accustomed, connect the pass by catching the dropped elbow ball after a single bounce.
Volleyballs, large soft balls, elastic bands, wooden boards
츄크볼 리바운더를 활용한 티볼 수비 송구 연습
티볼 공, 야구 글러브, 츄크볼 리바운더 2개, 베이스, 득점판
T-Ball Fielding and Throwing Practice Using Tchoukball Rebounders

1) Divide into two teams and line up behind two tchoukball rebounders.
2) Catch the rebounded ball with two hands and quickly take the ball out of the glove.
3) Shift direction sideways and rotate hips to throw accurately toward the home net target.
4) Score 1 point each time the thrown ball hits inside the net.
T-balls, baseball gloves, tchoukball rebounders, bases, scoreboard
세워진 배드민턴 라켓 통과 셔틀콕 던지기
Badminton Shuttlecock Throwing Through Upright Rackets

1) Place badminton rackets upright in a row across the floor.
2) Students sit or kneel in a line behind the throwing boundary.
3) Throw shuttlecocks through the head frame opening of the upright rackets focusing on wrist snap.
4) Collect thrown shuttlecocks into baskets and repeat the throwing practice.
막대 협동 공 나르기와 배구 리시브 연결 놀이
Cooperative Stick Ball Carry and Volleyball Cushioning Drill

1) Pairs hold two long sticks in parallel, balance a ball on top, and run around the cone marker.
2) If the ball drops, pick it up using only the sticks without touching it with hands.
3) Face each other holding the sticks and cooperatively catch an incoming ball on the sticks after one bounce.
4) Lower center of gravity and bend knees upon ball contact to absorb the impact.

1) Form two teams of 4 players on opposite sides of a lowered badminton/volleyball net.
2) After receiving a bounced serve, connect the play in order (catch/bump, set, spike) to return within 3 touches.
3) Spikers step back and approach with rhythmic footwork (left-gather-jump-hit) to spike over the net.
4) Rally back and forth using the receive-set-spike combination to score points.

Cooperative Bomb Relay with Rugby Balls

1) Two teams stand facing each other while the teacher kicks or throws rugby balls into the center.
2) Students sprint to where the ball lands; the first person to secure the ball becomes the team leader.
3) Remaining teammates quickly form a single-file line behind their leader.
4) Pass the rugby ball backwards through the line; players sit immediately after passing, and the last player brings the ball forward.

1) Set up low badminton nets and divide students into two large teams seated on the gymnasium floor.
2) Start the rally by tossing a large light ball from near the service line.
3) Keep seats on the floor and hit the ball over the net (boundary players can stand to assist balls back into court).

1) Seven players from each team line up in end zones, and play begins with the defense pulling the disc.
2) The offensive team advances by passing the disc, and the thrower must stop moving and pass within 10 seconds.
3) If the defense intercepts the disc or it touches the ground, possession switches immediately.
4) A point is scored when a player catches a pass in the opponent's end zone.

1) Groups identify the 5 color-coded holes (yellow, green, purple, orange, pink) and head to the starting tee.
2) After tee shots, players advance to their discs and throw subsequent shots in order of furthest distance from the basket.
3) Count each throw until the disc lands inside the target basket (traveler), and the group leader records the score.
4) Rotate through all 5 holes in sequence under the leader's directions, competing for the lowest total throw count.
Flying discs (1 per student), 5 disc golf target baskets (travelers), scorecards

1) Form teams of 5-6 players and assign a sequential number to each teammate.
2) Each player touches the balloon only once in numerical order, and only the last player can send it over the net to attack.
3) Players take turns serving in order, and the player who wins a point continues to serve.
4) If a number is skipped, someone other than the last player hits it over, or the balloon touches the floor, the opponent scores, and the first team to reach 10-15 points wins.

1) Divide the classroom into 4 zones using desks with students seated on the floor
2) Keeping bottoms on the floor, hit balloons crossing into your zone to other zones
3) Start a 30 to 50-second timer and call out a specific balloon color
4) When the timer sounds, the team holding or touching that colored balloon loses a point

1) Set up 2 balance beams on opposite sides with 10 hula hoops between them and safety mats on both sides.
2) Players start from opposite ends, hopping with feet together through the hula hoops.
3) When meeting an opponent, play rock-paper-scissors; the winner advances and the loser returns to their line.
4) Falling off the beam counts as out, and the player who reaches the opponent's starting end wins.
2 balance beams, 10 hula hoops, 4 or more safety mats
Bounce Ping Pong Ball Bucket Catch

1) Prepare 20 ping pong balls per team, and position one player holding a bucket opposite the thrower.
2) The thrower bounces the ping pong ball on the floor toward the teammate holding the bucket.
3) A player who successfully scores into the bucket swaps places with the bucket holder.
4) If missed, the thrower retrieves the ball and goes to the back; the team that finishes all balls first wins.
20 ping pong balls per team, buckets

1) Create a 4x4 grid on the floor using hoops or floor tape.
2) The teacher keeps time with rhythm sticks while students clap along to the beat.
3) Students jump to the rhythm through the hoops, mastering steps 1 through 5 in sequence.
4) As the lead runner moves forward, the next student enters in sync with the beat without interruption.

1) Place 5 hoops in a row and set a cone 10m ahead.
2) Pass through the hoops using two-foot hops, single-foot hops, sideways jumps, and straddle jumps, then round the cone.
3) In hoop relay, teammates stand inside individual hoops and the last runner picks up their hoop to move forward.
4) The next runner starts only after the moving runner puts their hoop down, racing around the turning cone.

1) Mark the play area with cones and place hoops equal to one-third of the total player count inside.
2) Select 4 taggers wearing vests while runners avoid them outside the hoops.
3) Entering a hoop puts a player in a frozen state unable to leave until an outside player tags them to unfreeze.
4) Tagged players are eliminated to a designated area outside, and the game ends when all are tagged or time expires.

Follow Me Circle Rock-Paper-Scissors Chair Game

1) Arrange chairs in a circle with one less than the number of players, placing a spot marker in the center.
2) The tagger stands on the center marker and calls out Rock-Paper-Scissors; matching the tagger (Stage 1) or beating the tagger (Stage
2) forces players to switch seats.
3) If the tagger jumps, all players must switch seats (Stage 3), and the person left standing becomes the new tagger.
4) In the Follow Me phase, players must mimic the tagger's movement or dance while rushing to find an open chair.

1) Divide the classroom court with line tape, give each student a spot marker, and have them place it on their chosen spot.
2) Players cannot move their spots or take their feet off their markers during play.
3) If hit by the balloon, the player is out and moves to the outfield with their marker to continue attacking.
4) Catching the balloon directly or catching it before it hits the floor after bouncing off a teammate counts as safe.

1) Arrange desks in rows and place a spot marker at the front of each row.
2) The captain on the marker tosses the ball to teammates seated in the row one by one.
3) After catching and tossing back to the captain, students put their heads down; once complete, the captain rotates to the back.
4) In the class mission, each row takes turns attempting the relay, and the entire class succeeds when all rows finish within their allotted tries.

1) Connect classroom desks lengthwise to create a track course.
2) Balance a ping-pong ball on a plastic spoon and walk around the desk track back to the start.
3) Transfer the ball spoon-to-spoon to the next runner without letting it fall.
4) For an upgraded variation, space desks apart and weave through them in a zigzag pattern.

1) [Game 1] Hold hands in a circle and pass the hoop around through each person's body without letting go of hands.
2) [Game 2] Stand in a straight line with hands on the shoulders ahead, passing the hoop backward without breaking contact.
3) [Game 3] Line up hoops (players-1); each runner runs to stand a hoop up to build a tunnel, and the final runner crawls through all hoops to grab the cone.
4) [Game 4] Two players hold a jump rope taut while runners lift hoops from one end, passing them over bodies and rope to the other side.

1) Place numbered cones (1-6) on one side of the gym, place a large die on the far side, and mark the center line with a spot marker.
2) The tagger stands on the spot marker, sprints to fetch the large die upon signal, and returns to the center spot marker.
3) While the tagger fetches the die, all other students sprint to the opposite side and choose any numbered cone (1-6) to stand behind.
4) Anyone who fails to reach a cone before the tagger steps on the spot marker is out, after which the tagger rolls the die.
5) Players at the cone matching the rolled die number instantly become taggers and chase others; tagged runners sit behind their cone.
6) The round ends after 2-3 minutes or when no survivors remain; survivors become taggers next round, or taggers play rock-paper-scissors if none survive.
1 giant die, 6 numbered cones (1-6), 1 spot marker

1) One tagger faces the wall while the remaining players place a scarf flat on their heads and line up along the starting line.
2) While the tagger faces the wall chanting "The scarf flower has bloomed", players carefully walk forward without dropping their scarves.
3) If a player drops the scarf or touches it with their hands at any point, they are caught by the tagger.
4) Anyone seen moving when the tagger turns around is also caught, joining a chain holding hands or pinkies with the tagger in order.
5) When an active runner tags the tagger's body or breaks the hand chain, everyone grabs their scarf and sprints back to the baseline.
6) The tagger chases to tag runners before they cross the baseline; runners who drop their scarf must pick it up before reaching safety.

1) Tip desks on their sides to form an enclosed square arena, seat a blindfolded tagger at the open side, and place 5 balls nearby.
2) 6-8 dodging students enter the arena and roam freely inside.
3) The blindfolded tagger listens to footsteps and calls "Stop!", upon which all dodgers must freeze immediately in place.
4) The tagger rolls a ball along the floor like a bowling ball; dodgers must freeze and cannot move their feet until the ball stops completely.
5) Players are out if hit directly, hit by rebounds off desks or peers, move feet before the ball stops, or touch stationary balls on the floor.
6) Dodgers who avoid all 5 rolled balls survive, while eliminated players watch or assist by retrieving balls for the tagger.
12 desks, 5 balls (bouncy balls, volleyballs, etc.), 1 blindfold

1) Stand one block in the center of each desk, divide the class into 4 teams at the classroom corners, and give each team one beanbag.
2) The first runner carries the beanbag on the back of the hand and drops it to knock over a block on a desk.
3) If knocked down, the runner brings the block to their team and hands off the beanbag; if missed or dropped, hand it over to the next runner.
4) Advance through stages (under the chin, on top of the head), and the team collecting the most blocks wins.
1 block per student, 1 beanbag per team

1) Place spot markers one fewer than the number of students; students on markers freeze in unique creative body poses.
2) The tagger runs to a frozen player and imitates their exact posture.
3) Once successfully copied, that player is unfrozen, leaves the marker, and roams to unfreeze other classmates by copying them.
4) When everyone is unfrozen, all students join hands to form a circle and walk around.
Spot markers (one fewer than the total number of students)
Flying Disc Class (Pass, Distance Throw & Cone Hunting)

1) 'Catch & Throw': Face partners and practice basic disc throws back and forth on signal.
2) 'Distance Throw': The first player throws far and moves to the back; on signal after discs land, the next player retrieves and throws.
3) 'Cone Hunting': Split into 2-3 teams and throw discs toward cones set up in the court.
4) Hit a cone to claim it for your team; the team collecting the most cones when time expires wins.

1) Place an egg carton on top of a cone at an appropriate distance and distribute 12 ping pong balls to each group.
2) Players take turns bouncing a ping pong ball once on the floor to land it inside the egg carton.
3) If a ball misses, the player must retrieve it and move to the end of the line.
4) The group that successfully places all ping pong balls into the egg carton first wins.
Ping pong balls, 4 egg cartons, 4 cones
Look at the Cone & Tap-Tap Tag

1) 'Look at the Cone': Partners face each other; the student indicated by the tossed cone runs away while the partner chases to tag.
2) 'Tap-Tap Tag': The tagger approaches a partner facing away, taps their shoulder, and flees; the tapped partner turns and chases.
3) Switch roles after each round and repeat the chase.

1) Two players hold both ends of a stick and place it low on the floor in front of the runner.
2) The runner jumps over the stick with both feet, and the stick holders lift it over the runner's head to place it ahead again.
3) When reaching the turning point, the runner and the stick holders all run around the marker back to the start line.
4) Repeat the process for the next runners until the final runner crosses first to win.

1) Place spot markers two fewer than the number of players; all players stand on a marker except for the cat and the first mouse.
2) The cat holding a fun stick chases the mouse, who must tag a teammate on a spot marker before getting caught.
3) The tagged teammate becomes the new mouse and runs, while the tagging mouse sits down on that marker.
4) The mice succeed if all mice sit on spot markers without being caught and the last mouse high-fives the teacher.

1) Taggers and runners position themselves at opposite ends of the area to start.
2) Taggers carry a fun stick and must move while keeping one foot inside a hula hoop; if the foot slips out, they must put it back in before moving.
3) Runners tagged by the tagger's fun stick are out and move to a designated area.
4) Runners who survive until the time limit ends win the game.

1) Students choose one of four menu items (tteokbokki, sundae, fried food, fish cake) to form teams of 4-8 players, each selecting one owner to sit on a chair.
2) The owner receives 30-40 shuffled receipt cards, and once the game starts, the owner hands one receipt to each team employee.
3) Employees walk around the classroom to meet employees from other shops and play rock-paper-scissors, where the winner guesses the opponent's receipt menu.
4) A correct guess wins the opponent's receipt to return to their owner; an incorrect guess passes the turn, and if both fail they find new opponents.
5) Players who lose their receipt get a new one from their owner, and when time is up, the shop whose owner collected the most receipts wins.

1) Students line up facing each other from opposite sides of the gym, placing one cone in front of each student's feet.
2) Students face their matched opponent and play rock-paper-scissors; the winner moves one step forward toward the opponent's cone while the loser stays.
3) As players repeat rock-paper-scissors and advance closer, the teacher blows a whistle at an unannounced moment.
4) When the whistle blows, players sprint to grab their opponent's cone, and the player who grabs it first wins before rotating lines to face a new partner.

1) Each student takes one juggling scarf, tosses it upward from their spot, spins a full turn, and catches it.
2) Toss the scarf overhead, clap hands, and catch it, progressively increasing the challenge from one clap up to eight or more claps.
3) Toss the scarf and catch it on top of a raised foot or leg, holding balance for 3 seconds without letting it drop.
4) Catch the falling scarf on the head or shoulder, or pair up with a partner to toss simultaneously and catch each other's scarf.
5) Choose one of the practiced skills as a row-by-row team mission where every member in the row must succeed.

1) Divide the class into 4 teams lined up behind cones, and place one chair per team on the opposite side of the baseline.
2) One student from each team sits on an opposing chair to serve as the challenger, while teammates line up at the start.
3) On start, the first runner sprints to the chair and plays rock-paper-scissors; if they win, they sprint back and high-five the next runner.
4) If the runner loses, they must sprint back to touch the team cone and return to the chair to challenge again until winning.
5) When applying tie rules, tying requires doing a full spin in place before replaying, and the team whose final runner crosses first wins.

1) Arrange desks in 3 parallel columns of 5 to create two narrow lanes between the rows.
2) Place throwers at both ends of each lane and place 3-4 dodging students inside each lane.
3) Throwers must strictly roll bouncy balls along the floor between desks and are forbidden from throwing through the air.
4) Dodging students hold onto the desks on both sides and jump to avoid balls rolling across the floor.
5) Any student hit by the ball is eliminated to observe from outside or serve as a referee, and the round ends when all dodgers are out.

3) Face a partner and connect each other by pressing only the tips of your index fingers against each end of the wand.
4) Move creatively to music without dropping the wand, stepping back when pushed or turning in sync.

3) If a throw misses the hoop, the player must hop back to the start line before attempting another throw.

Soft Volleyball Catch and Throw Game

1) Divide into two teams positioned on opposite sides of a net.
2) The server tosses the ball over the net in an arc so the opponent can catch it easily.
3) Players cannot move while holding the ball and must pass in place or throw into empty spaces.
4) A point is scored when the ball touches the opponent's floor; touching or shaking the net is a fault.

1) Face each other across a net using a soft volleyball.

1) Place two hoops in a straight line on the floor for each group.

3) If the ball stops inside a hoop, move the rear hoop forward to advance the track toward the finish line.

1) Draw a game court on the ground with numbered squares from 1 to 8 and a semi-circle sky at the top.
