Pre-Workout Full Body Stretching and Support Hold

1) Clap and rotate wrists, ankles, and knees to warm up the joints.
 2) Make large circles with shoulders and arms forward and backward, then spread legs wide and press down on knees.
 3) Lie face down, place hands firmly on the floor, extend legs, and hold the body straight 5 times.
 4) Catch your breath after each round and repeat for a total of 3 sets.

1) Jump rhythmically with feet together, heels lifted, upper body slightly leaned forward, and eyes looking straight ahead.
 2) Hold the rope in one hand at waist height and rotate it using the wrist while jumping, alternating hands.
 3) Hold the rope with both hands, rotate it from waist height, and practice 100 jumps per day.
 4) Once mastered, challenge single-foot jumps or alternating side-straddle jumps.
Flying Disc Curling, Bowling, and Shooting Games

1) Grip the disc with the thumb on top and four fingers underneath, then practice throwing from inside to outside.
 2) Set up a scoring target on the floor and throw discs to score points or knock away opponent discs.
 3) Throw discs toward pins set on a table to see who can knock down the most pins.
 4) Run from the start line, pick up a disc, check the written number, and hit the matching target.
Flying discs, target mat, pins, table

1) Draw a starting line, set obstacles in pairs at equal intervals, and line up two teams of 3 to 5 players behind the start line.
 2) The first runner dribbles the ball zigzag through the obstacles and returns.
 3) If an obstacle is knocked over upon returning to the line, reset it before the next runner starts.
 4) The team whose final runner finishes dribbling and returns first wins.

1) Form 4 teams of 3; two teams wait at the start line and two teams position one player per tag grid.
 2) Runners attempt to cross from the start line to the finish line avoiding taggers.
 3) Taggers catch runners only within their designated grids, and reaching the finish line scores 1 point.
 4) Tagged runners and those reaching the finish return to start over, then teams switch roles.

1) Mark the starting zone, ocean, and safe zone on the ground, then divide roles into fish and sharks.
 2) Fish start in the starting zone and sharks wait in the ocean, with only 3 fish allowed in the ocean at the same time.
 3) Fish try to reach the safe zone without getting tagged; tagged fish must return to the start and try again.
 4) A shark scores 1 point for tagging a fish, and a fish scores 2 points for reaching the safe zone safely; the team with more points wins.

1) Form groups of 4 to 6 students and decide the order.
 2) The first player performs a chosen basic movement learned earlier.
 3) The second player repeats the first movement and then adds their own movement.
 4) Subsequent players repeat all previous movements in sequence and add a new one, applauding anyone who remembers the full sequence without mistakes.

1) Draw a playing area on the floor and set up goals on both sides.
 2) Divide into two teams of 5 players each.
 3) Dribble or pass the ball to advance into the opponent's area.
 4) Stealing the attacker's ball switches offense and defense.
 5) The goalkeeper can block shots using any part of the body, including hands, in front of the goal.
 6) Scoring a goal earns 1 point, and the team with more points within the set time wins.

1) Form two teams of two and set up cones at 5m, 7m, and 9m from the starting line for each team.
 2) At the start signal sounding every 10 seconds, the first runner sprints to a chosen cone.
 3) Returning before the next signal awards points based on distance (5m: 1 pt, 7m: 2 pts, 9m: 3 pts); failing to return yields no points.
 4) When the next signal sounds, the next runner must depart regardless of the previous runner's return, and points are totaled over the set time.

1) Divide into two teams of 5 players each on a basketball court.
 2) The team with the ball dribbles or passes into the opponent's area; if the opponent intercepts the ball, offense and defense switch.
 3) Scoring inside the semi-circle area yields 1 point, while scoring from outside gives 2 points.
 4) The team with more points at the end of the designated time wins.

1) In a circular running course, divide two teams in half to prepare at the starting point and opposite side.
 2) At the starting signal, the team on the inside runs as close as possible to the curve, while the team on the outside runs far away from the curve.
 3) Record each team's time.
 4) Swap the positions of both teams, run again, and record the times.

1) Draw a deserted island and three islands on the ground, placing 4 treasures on each island.
 2) Form groups of 4 students, assigning 1 guardian and 3 explorers per group.
 3) Guardians protect treasures while explorers take one treasure at a time from other islands; tagged explorers leave the treasure and go to the deserted island.
 4) Trapped players return when high-fived by a teammate; after time expires, treasures on the island score 2 points each and carried treasures score 1 point, highest score wins.

1) Draw a court with cones in the middle, and pairs of two hold blankets to get ready inside their zone.
 2) Partners bounce the ball using the blanket to send it to the opponent's area or pass among teammates before sending it over.
 3) Score 1 point if the opponents fail to catch the ball or if it lands on the center cones.
 4) Score 1 point if the same pair on the opponent team catches it twice in a row or passes 5 or more times.

1) Lower your body posture and bend your knees slightly into ready position.
 2) Bounce the ball against the floor using wrist snap and fingertips.
 3) Keep your eyes up toward the moving direction and opponents rather than down at the ball.
 4) Move forward smoothly while continuing the rhythmic dribble.

1) Set up goals and plastic bottles at one end of each team lane and place a ball at the opposite end, with team members lined up in front of the goal.
 2) Both teams start simultaneously, passing the ball in sequence with their feet to the next teammate.
 3) The last teammate receives the ball in front of the bottles and kicks it from that spot to knock them down.
 4) Once knocked down, pass the ball back to the start, reset the bottles, repeat for the set time, and score 1 point per fallen bottle.
Finding Space and Passing the Ball

1) Draw a circular court, divide into two teams of 4, with 3 players per team standing alternately around the outer circle and 1 player inside.
 2) Outer players pass the ball to each other avoiding the opposing player in the center.
 3) The center player tries to intercept the opponents' pass and connect it to their own outer teammates.
 4) When all 3 outer players successfully pass the ball once each, they earn 1 point, and the team with more points after rotating roles wins.

1) One player stands in each hula hoop while other students line up at the starting line.
 2) Players take turns running to perform a forward roll on a wide mat and then play rock-paper-scissors with the first hoop player.
 3) The loser stays in the hoop while the winner performs a forward roll over a 2-tier vaulting box and advances to the second hoop.
 4) The winner does a forward roll over a 3-tier vaulting box and returns to start, or spins the hoop 10 times if too difficult, scoring 1 point per lap to reach 5 points.

1) Take a light approach run from 5-6 steps back and take off with both feet from the springboard.
 2) Spring up with enough height to lift the body while reaching hands toward the vault.
 3) Place hands on the near side of the vault box and support weight with arms to keep balance.
 4) Tuck the body rounded to roll, lower legs when hips touch the top, and land with knees bent.

1) On the command 'On your mark', approach the starting block and place hands shoulder-width apart behind the starting line.
 2) On 'Set', raise the hips higher than the head and shift body weight onto the arms and front foot.
 3) At the start signal, drive forward keeping the body low while pumping arms forcefully and pushing off the front foot.
 4) During full sprint, keep the torso upright, pump arms back and forth, raise knees high, and sprint through the finish line.

1) Only the first person of each team faces the demo group while others look away.
 2) The demonstration group performs their custom gymnastics move for 8 counts.
 3) From front to back, teammates relay the demonstrated movement one by one.
 4) If the last person performs the exact correct movement, the team earns points.

1) Each student holds a hula hoop around their body as a protective bubble.
 2) Everyone moves one step together following the tagger's chant of 'One Step'.
 3) If the hula hoops of fleeing players touch each other, they are caught by the tagger.
 4) Switch roles when tagged, using the strategy of gathering together and scattering quickly.

1) Divide into teams, set a running order, and line up behind the starting line.
 2) On the signal, the first runner sprints to the desk where the cups are set up.
 3) Unstack the three stacks of three cups from left to right (or vice versa) into 3-3-3 pyramids.
 4) Immediately downstack the cups in the same direction into three stacks and sprint back to tag the next player.

1) Pair up in twos and face each other.
 2) Toss and catch a beanbag back and forth.
 3) On the signal, the student holding the beanbag becomes the tagger and chases the partner who flees.
 4) Tagged runners perform a physical activity task before continuing the game.

1) Draw a starting line and place multiple colored markers across from it, then divide players into two groups of 3 to 5 and line up in order.
 2) Each group gets one ball, bounces/dribbles the ball toward the colored markers in the exact color sequence called by the teacher.
 3) Upon reaching the colored marker, bounce the ball 3 times, pass through the designated markers, and return to the start line for the next runner.
 4) The team whose last player completes the course and returns across the starting line first wins.

1) Draw a court with a starting line and target area, then divide into offense and defense teams.
 2) The offense moves toward the target by dribbling and passing, with every member holding the ball at least once.
 3) The defense tries to steal the ball; if stolen, the offense restarts from the beginning.
 4) Offense gets 1 point upon reaching the target, and defense gets 1 point per steal, taking turns within a set time.

1) Form a group of 5 to 10 players and draw a figure-8 line on the ground.
 2) All team members hold a long rope in their right hands and stand in a single file on the figure-8 line.
 3) On the start signal, the team jogs along the line; the front runner releases the rope, sprints forward, and chases the last runner.
 4) After tagging the last runner, shout 'Go' for the next runner to sprint; anyone failing to tag within three laps rests inside the loop, and the last two remaining runners win.
Mat and Vaulting Box Chick-to-Rooster Game

1) The first runner from each group rolls forward like an egg on the mat and plays rock-paper-scissors.
 2) The winner becomes a chick, steps onto the first vaulting box tier, and chirps; the loser rolls backward to the back of their line.
 3) The next teammate rolls forward to face the player standing on the first tier.
 4) If the chick wins again, they become a rooster, step onto the second tier, crow, and jump down; the first group whose members all become roosters wins.

1) Set up the play area, divide into two teams, and have all students attach three different colored tails to their sides and back.
 2) On start signal, steal tails from the opposing team, but you cannot steal a color you already captured.
 3) Once a player collects all three colors, they cannot steal more tails and must protect their own.
 4) Score 1 point per tail at the end; the team with the higher sum of captured and remaining tails wins.

1) Set up a court with a goal, starting line, and score zones (1-pt and 2-pt zones).
 2) Divide into two teams of 3-5 players for offense and defense, with one defender as goalkeeper.
 3) The offense dribbles or passes to score into the goal; if defense steals the ball, offense restarts at the start line.
 4) A goal from the 1-point zone scores 1 point and from the 2-point zone scores 2 points; the team with more points wins.

1) Draw the playing field boundaries and scoring zones on the floor, using a single ball.
 2) Each group starts in their area, running with or passing the ball toward the opponent scoring zone.
 3) The ball can only be passed backward to teammates positioned behind.
 4) Scoring 1 point occurs when reaching the scoring zone, while defense can intercept and forward passing or pushing results in a turnover.
Passing the Ball While Evading Defenders

1) Draw starting lines, finishing lines, and designated defensive zones on the floor.
 2) Divide into two teams of three players each, placing the attacking team at the start line and defenders in their assigned zones.
 3) The attacking team dribbles and passes the ball toward the finish while the first zone defender keeps one foot in a circle and the free zone defender moves freely.
 4) If the ball is intercepted or reaches the destination, restart from the beginning, and the team that brings more balls across within the time limit wins.

1) Lie on a mat, raise your legs with momentum, and practice lifting your upper body to a sit-up position.
 2) Start from a standing position and roll forward, spreading both legs as wide as possible when they are airborne.
 3) Place both hands deeply between the legs and use the rolling momentum to lift the waist and upper body.

1) Form two teams of 5 players on a field with two soccer goals.
 2) Dribble and pass the ball toward the opponent's area, switching possession upon a turnover.
 3) The goalkeeper can use any part of the body, including hands, in front of the goal.
 4) Scoring into the opponent's goal awards 1 point, and the team with the most points when time expires wins.

1) Prepare a Kin-Ball and boundary markers.
 2) One tagger gets ready with the Kin-Ball to tag other players.
 3) The tagger rolls the Kin-Ball to tag fleeing players.
 4) A tagged player switches roles with the tagger, continuing the game for the set time.
Catch and Throw Volleyball Net Game

1) Two teams face each other across a net placed in the center of the court.
 2) Players strike or throw the ball over the net into the opponent court.
 3) Players can catch the ball with their hands and either return it directly or pass to teammates before returning.
 4) A point is scored if opponents fail to catch hit the net touch twice consecutively or pass five or more times.
Egg, Chick, Chicken Game on Vaulting Box

1) The first player of each team rolls forward like an egg and plays rock-paper-scissors with the opponent.
 2) The winner becomes a chick, steps onto the 1st tier of the vaulting box, and chirps.
 3) The loser backward-rolls back to the start line, and the next player rolls out to challenge the chick.
 4) If the chick wins again, they become a chicken, climb to the 2nd tier, shout, and jump down; the first team where all members become chickens wins.

1) Form two parallel lines facing each other, designating one line as Tigers and the other as Rabbits.
 2) When the leader calls out 'Tigers', the tigers chase the rabbits directly in front of them, while the rabbits sprint toward their safe white line (roles reverse if 'Rabbits' is called).
 3) If a runner crosses the white line safely, the runner scores 1 point; if tagged beforehand, the chaser scores 1 point (first to 3 points wins).
 4) As a variation, facing pairs play rock-paper-scissors where the winner chases the loser toward the boundary line.

1) Divide into two teams, with each team placing a different colored scarf in their pockets.
 2) On the start signal, the first runner vaults over the box, places a scarf inside a hula hoop, and returns.
 3) If a runner fails to vault over the box, they must return to the starting line and try again.
 4) Block the opposing team from completing a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line; the first team to complete a line wins.

1) Divide the area on the floor to draw two playing courts, form two groups of 6 players each, and assign 4 attackers and 2 defenders per group.
 2) In each zone, 4 attackers and 2 opposing defenders enter together to prepare for the game.
 3) Attackers pass the ball within the designated area while defenders try to intercept the ball.
 4) Attackers score 1 point after completing 4 passes, defenders score 2 points upon intercepting the ball, and the first team to reach 10 points wins.

1) Form two teams of 5 and stand in a line at the starting line holding one volleyball.
 2) On signal, the 1st person twists right to pass to the 2nd, the 2nd twists left, the 3rd arches back over the head, and the 4th bends over to pass between legs.
 3) Repeat passing the ball far twice, and the team that moves further wins.

1) Squat on the mat, place palms facing upward beside the ears, and tuck the chin slightly downward.
 2) Shift body weight backward so the hips, back, shoulders, back of the head, and palms contact the mat in order.
 3) When palms touch the mat, push firmly against the mat with both hands while driving the legs backward.
 4) As feet touch the mat, push against the mat with palms to stand up and regain balance.

Home Item Arm Exercises and Stair Climbing

1) Stand straight holding two water bottles of suitable weight.
 2) Keep elbows close to the torso, curl the bottles upward, then lower them back down.
 3) Press the bottles straight overhead and return to the starting position without swaying.
 4) Perform stair climbing by single steps, multiple steps, or stepping up and down.

1) Mark a court with a start line and a target area, then divide into offense and defense teams.
 2) Offense moves toward the target by dribbling or passing, ensuring each member holds the ball at least once.
 3) Defense tries to steal the ball; if stolen, offense restarts from the start line.
 4) Offense scores 1 point upon reaching the goal, defense scores 1 point if they steal the ball, and the team with the most points wins.

1) Perform wrist and ankle exercises to the count, then repeat with the opposite foot.
 2) Perform neck and side stretches in sequence.
 3) Perform thigh, waist, and back stretching exercises.
 4) Finish with shoulder dance movement and deep breathing exercises opening both arms wide.
스포츠 리듬 트레이닝 원 레그 투 점프

1) Clap along to the rhythm of the music.
 2) Step on one foot and jump twice, alternating feet and hands in opposite directions.
 3) Once familiar with the movement, expand the motion by opening and lowering the arms.

1) Gently rotate your wrists and ankles.
 2) Place both hands on your knees and repeat sitting and standing up.
 3) Bend one leg while extending the other and gently press the knee, repeat on the other side, sit down to stretch one extended leg, and stand sideways to stretch both legs thoroughly.
 4) Place hands on waist and rotate hips, rotate shoulders with loose fists and straight arms, and rotate neck with hands on waist.
손짚고 옆돌기 기초 연습(다리와 엉덩이 들어올리기, 매트 짚고 다리 넘기기, 원둘레 돌며 다리 넘기기)
Cartwheel Lead-up Drills (Leg and Hip Raise, Mat Hop-over, Circle Line Transfer)

1) Place both hands shoulder-width apart on the mat, bend knees, kick off the mat to hop, and raise legs and hips.
 2) Lean forward, place hands on the mat, shift center of gravity to arms, kick both feet up, and transfer them to the opposite side.
 3) Follow a circle drawn on the floor, placing hands and feet one by one (for a left turn: left hand, right hand, right foot, left foot).

1) Run while kicking the buttocks with the heel of each alternate foot.
 2) Alternately lift each leg high and clap hands beneath the thigh while moving forward.
 3) Step forward into deep lunges with the front knee bent at 90 degrees and the rear knee near the ground.
 4) Drive the knee upward until the thigh is parallel to the ground and flex the ankle while stepping forward.
Vaulting Board Run-Up and Takeoff Practice

1) Take a light approach run from three to five steps back.
 2) Step firmly on the front part of the springboard with both feet together using the whole sole.
 3) After jumping high off the springboard, slightly bend knees and spread both arms to land with balance.
 4) Repeat the sequence to become proficient.
Vaulting Box Dismount with Various Movements

1) Stand on the vaulting box facing the landing mat in a ready position.
 2) Attempt dismounting while clapping hands once or twice.
 3) Attempt dismounting while turning the body backwards in mid-air.
 4) Lift legs high and land safely onto the mat.
스포츠 리듬 트레이닝 (포워드 점프 & 백워드 점프)
Sports Rhythm Training: Forward & Backward Jump

1) Move to the 120 BPM tempo by flexing the ankles, knees, and hips to absorb the rhythm.
 2) Perform forward jumps while swinging arms in sync with the beat.
 3) Perform backward jumps while maintaining the rhythm.

1) Take a light approach run from 3 to 5 steps back and jump off the springboard with both feet together.
 2) Place both hands on the near side of the vault and leap upward to elevate the body.
 3) Tuck the body as round as possible to perform a forward roll.
 4) Once the hips touch the vault, lower the legs and land with knees softly bent.

1) Perform basic jump by jumping once per rope turn with both feet together.
 2) Perform alternate-foot jumps by alternating feet lightly as if jogging in place.
 3) Perform side-to-side double jumps without lifting feet too high.
 4) Perform cross jumps by crossing arms in an X shape for one jump and uncrossing for the next jump.

1) Jump down from the vaulting box while clapping once or twice.
 2) Jump down from the box while turning the body backward before landing.
 3) Raise both arms high like wings before landing on the ground.
 4) Choose and try your own creative action to challenge dismounting the vaulting box.

1) Squat on the mat and place hands near the ears with palms facing up toward the ceiling.
 2) Shift center of gravity backward and roll so the back touches the mat.
 3) As hands touch the mat and legs go over, spread both legs straight apart to the sides.
 4) Once feet touch the ground, push the mat with hands and raise upper body to stand.

1) Step on the middle of the rope and adjust its length so the handles reach your armpits or chest.
 2) Stand in place holding the rope in one hand, swing it slowly, and jump lightly as it taps the floor.
 3) Once comfortable, switch hands or spin the rope faster to practice jumping.
 4) Sit in place, hold the rope in one hand, swing it horizontally along the ground, and hop over it.
Forward Roll Practice Using an Inclined Mat

1) Crouch on the mat, place hands shoulder-width apart, tuck the chin down, lift the hips, and look at the sky between the legs.
 2) Prepare with palms facing upward beside the face, lean forward to place palms on the mat lifting hips slightly, and push back to reset.
 3) Practice raising the hips higher with chin tucked until the back of the head touches the mat.
 4) Stand on an inclined mat, crouch and place hands down, roll sequentially across the back of the head, back, hips, and feet, then tuck chin and grab knees to stand up.

1) Pair up in twos and play rock-paper-scissors.
 2) The winner flees and the loser becomes the tagger to chase their partner.
 3) When the reversal signal sounds, roles switch and the runner becomes the tagger.
 4) A tagged player performs a designated exercise 3 times and becomes the tagger; the player who is not the tagger when time expires wins.

1) On the command "On your mark," place feet in the starting blocks and place hands shoulder-width apart behind the starting line with fingers together except the thumb.
 2) On the command "Set," look ahead of hands, raise hips higher than the head, and shift weight forward.
 3) At the start signal, accelerate staying low, pump arms vigorously, push off the ground firmly, and gradually raise the torso while lengthening strides.
 4) During the sprint, run tall with high knees and maintain full speed through the finish line without slowing down.
Forward Roll on Mat and Vaulting Box

1) On the mat, bend knees, place both hands on the mat, tuck the chin, and roll forward contacting the back of the head, shoulders, back, waist, and hips in order.
 2) If the mat is long, practice two consecutive forward rolls.
 3) On a low vaulting box, place hands from the springboard, tuck the head, round the body, and roll forward in a straight line.
 4) Take 3 to 5 running steps, jump off both feet on the springboard, place hands on the vault, and connect smoothly into a forward roll.

1) Run up from 3 to 5 steps away, step firmly on the springboard, and jump upward.
 2) Look at where your hands will land and lean forward with arms extended.
 3) Place both hands on the vaulting box while spreading both legs wide.

공 12개(모둠별 서로 다른 색 6개씩), 흰색 공 1개, 의자

1) Two teams prepare 6 balls each in different colors.
 2) Throw a white ball from the throw line, then one player from each team throws 1 ball.
 3) The team farther from the white ball sits on a chair and throws the rest, followed by the opposing team throwing their remaining 5 balls.
 4) Compare each team's balls closest to the white ball and score 1 point for each ball closer than the opponent's closest ball.

Exercise Along the Card Path Board Game

1) Prepare different-colored balls for each player and arrange all cards facedown to form a walking path.
 2) Take turns rolling the die and advance personal balls according to the rolled number.
 3) Flip the card at the landing space and perform the listed exercise; if already flipped, perform half the repetitions.
 4) The player who returns to the start/finish space first wins.
Heart and Mind United (Spot Marker Jump)

1) Each student takes one differently colored spot marker and stands on it forming a large circle.
 2) Stand with both feet together on the spot marker and hold hands with neighboring classmates.
 3) On the count of 'one, two, three', jump simultaneously to the right onto the next spot marker.
 4) If someone falls or fails to land inside the spot marker, everyone performs squats together, and advanced rounds involve hopping on one foot or jumping to the left.
책상, 콩주머니 3개, 숫자 원 마커, 모둠 조끼

1) Form groups of 4 and decide the throwing order.
 2) Throw 3 beanbags one by one onto the numbered spot markers on the desk.
 3) Score points if the beanbag lands inside or touches the target marker.
 4) Combine scores of all group members, and the group with the highest score wins.
Desk, 3 beanbags, numbered spot markers, team vests

1) Mark the starting line on the floor using line tape.
 2) Team members lock arms in a line and sit down back-to-back with the opposing team.
 3) On signal, keep arms firmly interlocked and push the opposing team using back strength.
 4) The team that pushes the opposing team further from the starting line wins.
탁구공, 패드민턴 채, 책상, 모둠 조끼

1) Form two teams of 2 players, decide the hitting order, and face each other across the desk.
 2) Take turns hitting the ball with paddle bats so it bounces on the desk toward the opposing team.
 3) If a team fails to bounce the ball onto the desk or miss a return, the opposing team scores 1 point.
 4) The first team to reach 10 points wins the game.
table tennis balls, paddle bats, desks, team vests

1) Four students form a team wearing pinnies and line up at the starting line.
 2) On signal, runner 1 goes to the first desk, stacks 3 cups, loops around the desk, and returns.
 3) Runner 2 stacks 6 cups on the second desk and returns, and runner 3 stacks 3 cups on the third desk and returns.
 4) The final runner collapses all cups back together and returns; the first team to finish wins.
Desks, Speed Stacks cups, team pinnies

1) Divide into teams wearing pinnies, with each player holding a soccer ball.
 2) On the signal, dribble inside the designated area while protecting your own ball.
 3) While dribbling, kick opponents' balls outside the boundary area.
 4) If your ball goes out, carry it to the scoreboard, add 1 point to your team, and rejoin; the team with the lowest score at the end wins.
Cones, Soccer balls, Scoreboard, Team pinnies

1) Divide into two groups and place one dish cone on every student's head.
 2) On signal, hit the balloon using hands and feet.
 3) A player is eliminated if the cone drops, touches another player, or if the balloon touches body parts other than hands and feet.
 4) The group with more players remaining after the set time wins.

1) Stand in a circle, hook individual jump ropes onto a center ring, and hold the ropes with both hands.
 2) When the signal sounds, place an object on top of the ring and pull the ropes to transport it to the designated area.
 3) The team that transports more objects within the given time wins.
Jump ropes, ring, spot markers, team vests, objects (books)

1) Place the baskets of each group in the center and place spot markers 3m away from the baskets.
 2) Each person takes 3 beanbags and lines up at the spot marker.
 3) When the signal sounds, take turns throwing the beanbags underhand one by one per group.
 4) If a beanbag thrown by another group lands in our basket, it becomes ours, and the group with the most beanbags in their basket wins.
Beanbags, baskets, spot markers, team vests

1) Designate 3 attackers and 1 defender within each group.
 2) Mark a circle; the defender holding a hoop stands inside the circle, while 3 attackers from the other team stand outside in a triangle.
 3) On signal, attackers pass the ball avoiding the defender's hoop, while the defender tries to pass the ball through the hoop.
 4) The team whose defender passes the ball through the hoop the most times within the time limit wins.

1) Divide the class into an offensive team and a defensive team.
 2) The kicker kicks the rolling ball using the instep or inside of the foot and runs around cones back to home base.
 3) Fielders catch and throw the ball to knock down the hoop towers, then carry the ball into the defensive home base.

 3) When pulling an opponent's tail, place it into the team tail box and move one beanbag to the score box to score 1 point.
 4) Players who lose all tails must step out of bounds, and the team that transfers more beanbags within the time limit wins.

1) Form two teams of 4 players each and set up a net in the center of the court.
 2) Start the game by throwing the ball with two hands over the net from outside the court boundary.
 3) Catch the incoming ball with two hands and pass it so every teammate touches it before throwing it back.
 4) If a team drops the ball or throws it out of bounds, the opposing team scores 1 point; first to 15 points wins.

1) Form 2 teams of 2 players each, set up a net in the center of a rectangular court, and mark 4 pink zones in the corners.
 2) Hit the shuttlecock back and forth over the net.
 3) Score 1 point if the shuttlecock lands in the opponent's court or if the opponent hits it out of bounds.
 4) Score 3 points if the shuttlecock lands in the opponent's pink corner zone; the first team to reach 21 points wins.

1) Set up a net in the center of a rectangular court and form groups of four.
 2) Prepare four baskets, badminton rackets, and ten shuttlecocks per person.
 3) Hit shuttlecocks over the net into all four baskets to score 1 point.
 4) The group with the highest score after everyone hits all shuttlecocks wins.
4 baskets, badminton rackets, 10 shuttlecocks per person

1) Choose jump rope movements with a friend and set a target number of repetitions.
 2) For the two-foot jump, swing the rope forward and jump over it with feet together when the rope reaches your feet.
 3) For the criss-cross jump, cross your arms into an X shape to jump over the rope, then uncross your arms and jump again.
 4) Practice various moves such as straddle jumps and backward jumps daily.

1) Run up toward the vaulting box and perform a two-footed jump off the springboard.
 2) Place hands on the front of the vaulting box, straddle sit on top, then jump down bending knees on landing.
 3) Shift forward on the box while supporting weight on hands, push off the edge, and dismount safely.
 4) Jump off the board, place hands, and swing legs sideways over the vaulting box to land softly on the mat.
긴 줄 연속 8자 마주 건너기 게임
Continuous Figure-8 Long Rope Jumping Game

1) Two turners hold and swing both ends of a long rope.
 2) Set the timer for 2 minutes, and upon the start signal, teammates enter the rope one by one.
 3) Just before a runner exits, the next person immediately enters to jump and exit continuously.
 4) Runners loop in a figure-8 pattern around the turners, and the team with the most successful jumps in 2 minutes wins.

1) Stand in front of the mat and attempt the forward roll one by one.
 2) Place both hands shoulder-width apart on the mat and tuck the head down as much as possible.
 3) Pull the chin in, bring knees together close to the chest, curl the body round, and roll forward with power.
 4) Once comfortable rolling with legs together, try straddle roll by opening both legs the moment the lower back touches the mat.

1) Set up the field with bases about 15m apart, prepare spot markers, and divide into two teams of 9 players each.
 2) Fielders place their spot markers where they want to defend while the kicker prepares to kick.
 3) The kicking team kicks the ball rolled by the fielding team and runs around the bases toward home plate.
 4) A kicker is out if a fielder catches the kicked ball while stepping on their spot marker, catches a fly ball directly, or throws the ball to the base before the runner arrives; 1 point is scored when a runner touches home.
뜀틀과 놀기 (뜀틀 잡고 점프하기, 손 짚고 뜀틀 건너가기, 뜀틀에 걸터앉기, 뜀틀 밟고 뛰어내리기)

1) Run up, place hands on the vaulting box, stomp the springboard, and jump.
 2) Place hands on two vaulting boxes spaced about 50 cm apart and cross over.
 3) Run, stomp feet, and straddle-sit on the vaulting box with hands placed.
 4) Step up onto the vaulting box with one foot and jump down.

1) Form two teams of 9 players each, with the defense pairing up by twos in pre-designated zones.
 2) The kicking team kicks the pitched ball and runs the bases to reach home plate.
 3) A batter is out if a fly ball is caught directly or if the ball reaches the base before the runner.
 4) Teams switch sides after 3 outs, playing 3 innings to determine the winner by total score.

1) Divide into two teams of 6 players each, and set up the field with cones placing a near cone and a far cone.
 2) The kicking team kicks the ball toward empty space using inside, toe, or instep, then runs around their chosen cone.
 3) Returning around the near cone scores 1 point, while returning around the far cone scores 2 points.
 4) The runner is out if defense catches the ball and steps on the defensive home base first; teams switch after all members kick, playing 3 innings.

1) Slowly exhale while holding each stretching movement for 10 to 15 seconds and repeat.
 2) Bend one knee and pull the instep toward the buttocks to stretch the thighs.
 3) Interlock fingers overhead to stretch sides, then cross one arm and press the elbow with the other arm to stretch shoulders.
 4) Face a partner, bend forward to press each other's shoulders, or hold hands with legs positioned to stretch the sides together.

1) Set up a portable net in the center of a rectangular court and form 2 teams of 4 players each.
 2) Start the game by serving the ball from outside the court boundary.
 3) The ball must bounce once on the floor before being played, must be touched by every teammate, and is then sent over the net.
 4) If a team fails to receive the ball or hits it out of the opponent's boundary, the opposing team scores 1 point; the first team to reach 15 points wins.
Call and Pass Big Ball Game

1) Draw a 2-meter diameter circle on the floor and have a group of six students stand around it with even spacing.
 2) A player calls a teammate's name and passes the large ball toward them.
 3) The called student lets the ball bounce once on the floor and passes it along to another named teammate.
 4) When the ball successfully passes through all six team members, the team scores 1 point, and the team with the most points within the set time wins.

1) Set up a cone and a hoop with distance between two teams, and have players line up behind each cone.
 2) On the signal, one runner from each team runs toward each other.
 3) When they meet, they shake hands, take one step back, and play rock-paper-scissors.
 4) The winner continues running while the loser returns to the back of the line; the losing team's next runner dashes out to block them, and stepping into the opponent's hoop scores 1 point toward a 3-point victory.
1 hoop per team, 1 cone per team
피구공 1개, 모둠 조끼, 콘 또는 줄 긋는 기구

1) Form two teams, where dodging teams create trains of 3-4 players inside the court, and the throwing team stands outside the opposite side of the court.
 2) The throwing team throws the ball to eliminate players starting from the train's tail in sequence.
 3) Hit players are out and move outside the opposite court to throw balls.
 4) The game continues until all players on the dodging team are out.
1 dodgeball, team pinnies, cones or line-marking equipment

1) Place thumb on the disc top and rest fingers against the rim underneath.
 2) Throw disc horizontally from chest level using brisk wrist snap.
 3) Each player throws the disc 3 times toward 5 upright cones placed ahead.
 4) Earn points matching the number of knocked-down cones to decide the winner.

1) Divide the field into three zones (attack, midfield, defense), set up goals, and form two teams.
 2) Assign player roles and positions to designated zones before starting.
 3) The attacking team passes or dribbles the ball through the zones toward the front, while defenders anticipate passes to intercept.
 4) The attacking team shoots into the goal from zone A to score.
Elephant and Rhino Coco Running Tag

1) Divide into an elephant team and a rhino team with four players each standing back-to-back at the starting line.
 2) The team whose animal is called runs away while the other team chases and tags them.
 3) Score points by tagging fleeing opponents or by crossing the 10m finish line uncaught.
 4) Modify by chanting coco-co before calling out an animal name.

1) Observe videos of nature movements (schools of fish, thunder/lightning, raindrops) to identify rhythms.
 2) Move the hoop up and down or swing it back and forth to express a school of fish.
 3) Toss and catch the hoop high or pass vertically through it to express thunder and lightning.
 4) Connect multiple hoops together and wave them up and down sequentially to depict splashing raindrops.

1) Set up a 1.5m net at the center of a rectangular court and form two teams of 4 players each.
 2) Hit the ball coming over the net overhead either directly in the air or after a single bounce.
 3) If a team fails to return the ball within 3 hits or sends it out of bounds, the opposing team scores 1 point.
 4) The first team to score 15 points wins.

1) Draw a 10m circle and divide into an outer attacking team (5-6 players) and an inner defending team (3 players).
 2) Attackers pass the ball across the circle using their feet while defenders try to block it.
 3) Attackers earn 1 point for a completed pass, and defenders earn 1 point if they block or intercept the ball.
 4) The team that reaches 5 points first wins.

1) Form two teams of 6 players each and place goals at both ends of a rectangular court.
 2) When on offense, a player with the ball may pass or dribble to move, scoring 1 point by shooting into the opponent basket.
 3) If all teammates signal when ready and every player connects a pass before scoring, the team earns 2 points.
 4) Defenders must stay at least 1 meter away from the ball carrier and cannot block shots toward the goal; the team with the most points within the set time wins.

1) Divide into two teams of 7 players each and set up an offensive home and a defensive home.
 2) The offensive team kicks the ball rolled by the defensive team and circles the base to return to the offensive home.
 3) The defensive team catches the kicked ball and passes it among teammates toward the defensive home.
 4) If the defense passes the ball to the defensive home without dropping it before the runner steps on home plate, points are awarded equal to the number of passes made.

1) Mark the play area with cones, choose a tagger (monkey) wearing a colored vest, and all other students become bananas.
 2) When the monkey approaches, shout 'Banana' and raise both arms overhead to form a peel before getting tagged to be safe.
 3) A frozen banana can move again when other bananas come and simultaneously peel the arms down.
 4) If tagged before shouting 'Banana', switch vests and become the new monkey.

1) Make a small circle with a diameter of about 10 meters using cones; only the first runner steps outside the circle while others wait in line inside.
 2) When the signal sounds, the first runner starts, walks one lap, and returns to their team.
 3) The next runner steps outside the circle and stretches an arm back to receive the baton when signaled.
 4) Cooperate with teammates while walking relay style, and win by tagging an opponent teammate's back.

1) Warm up by stretching while mimicking fruit shapes like bananas, watermelons, or apples.
 2) Play a tag game following the freeze-tag format.
 3) Right before being tagged, shout a fruit name and freeze into that fruit's shape to avoid being caught.
 4) When a teammate touches you, you are unfrozen and can run again.
콘, 모둠 조끼, 배구공 또는 축구공

1) Set up cones 18 meters apart as turning points; team members stand in line with legs shoulder-width apart to form a tunnel, and the front runner holds the ball.
 2) On signal, roll the ball through the legs to the last player.
 3) The last player takes the ball, runs around both cones, returns to the front of the line, and rolls the ball through again.
 4) When all members finish running around the cones, the entire team sits down, and the first team seated wins.
Cones, team vests, volleyball or soccer ball
점수판, 모둠 조끼, 콘 또는 줄 긋는 기구

1) Mark the field using cones or lines and split into two groups: offense and defense (crocodiles).
 2) Defenders stand one per line while offensive runners gather at the starting point.
 3) On the signal, runners advance toward the finish line while defenders move along their assigned lines to tag them.
 4) The number of players reaching the finish safely becomes the team score; teams switch roles and the higher score wins.
Scoreboard, team vests, cones or line marker
던지고 달리기 야구형 게임 (공을 정확하게 던지고 받기)
Throw and Run Baseball Practice Game

1) Form 4 groups, wear baseball gloves, and line up at each corner of the diamond.
 2) Throw the ball to the player on the right, then run toward that position and join the back of the line.
 3) Practice throwing and catching at chest height.
 4) Practice overhead throws and ground ball rolling drills in rotation.
Team Cooperative Standing Long Jump Relay

1) The first runner from each group performs a standing long jump.
 2) Mark the landing heel position using spot markers or cones.
 3) The next runner jumps consecutively from that marked spot.
 4) The group that covers the greatest total distance after all runners finish wins.

1) Players freeze when the tagger calls out and turns around.
 2) Instead of just freezing, players must strike a monkey pose.
 3) If a player fails to freeze or make a monkey pose, they are caught and must hold hands with the tagger.
 4) The teacher starts as the tagger, then students take turns.

1) Form groups of three where the center student is "Namul" and outer partners hold hands as "Rice" around them.
 2) When "Namul" is called, center players run to find a new Rice shell.
 3) When "Rice" is called, outer partners separate to shelter a new Namul, and on "Bibimbap," everyone scrambles to form new trios.
 4) A tagger is added, and the student left without a spot becomes the next tagger.

1) The tagger calls out 'The frog flower has bloomed'.
 2) While the tagger chants, players leap high and far like frogs.
 3) Anyone who moves or fails to freeze in a frog pose when the tagger turns is caught and holds hands with the tagger.
 4) When a surviving player tags the tagger's back, all caught players run away.

1) Cut an A4 paper into 8 pieces, write your dream, hope, and name, and attach it to a disposable chopstick with double-sided tape to make a flag.
 2) Go out to the sandbox in the schoolyard and perform long jumps.
 3) Mark each student's landing heel position by sticking their flag along the edge of the sandbox.
 4) Check the flags of classmates and challenge your own record again.
Wooden chopsticks, A4 paper, double-sided tape

1) Divide into two teams and sit facing each other with a curtain (blanket) held between them.
 2) Each round, one player from each team steps forward to sit directly in front of the curtain.
 3) Everyone chants 'One, two, three, peekaboo!' as the curtain drops.
 4) The player who recognizes and shouts the opponent's name first wins the round for their team.

1) Set up a net in the center of a rectangular court and mark zones A and B.
 2) Form groups of two and prepare badminton rackets and shuttlecocks.
 3) Hit the shuttlecock from each zone to areas that are difficult for the opponent to return.
 4) Score 1 point if the shuttlecock lands in the opponent court or goes out, and the first to reach 21 points wins.

1) Divide into two teams, decide offense/defense by rock-paper-scissors, and set up 3 bases, a goal, a hoop, beanbags, and a dodgeball.
 2) Offense plays in pairs where one pitches and the other hits the ball with a hand.
 3) The pair runs together to a base, grabs a beanbag, and brings it back to the hoop (1 pt for 1st base, 2 pts for 2nd base, 3 pts for 3rd base).
 4) Fielders line up upon catching the ball to pass it backward and forward; the batter is out if the ball enters the goal before they finish or if a fly ball is caught directly.

1) Form pairs and stand facing each other at opposite starting lines.
 2) At the signal, the player on the left grabs a beanbag from the starting line and passes it to the partner running toward them.
 3) The receiving player turns around, runs back, and places the beanbag into the basket.
 4) Repeat the process until players can no longer run, and the pair that transfers the most beanbags wins.
모든 누 공 이어주기 티볼 게임

1) Divide into two teams for offense and defense; the batter hits the ball off the batting tee and runs around all bases to home.
 2) When the defense catches the ball, they throw it to the nearest base and relay it to every base in order.
 3) The batter is out if the defense relays the ball through all bases before the batter reaches home.
 4) The batter scores 1 point upon reaching home, and the team with more points after 3 innings wins.

1) Divide into two groups of 6, prepare 3 cups per group (6 total), and have the first 3 students hold a cup.
 2) The first runner places a cup past the finish line and returns using a U-turn touch around the team.
 3) The second student places a cup side by side, and the third student stacks one cup on top of the two.
 4) From the fourth student on, retrieve cups one by one, and the team whose members all sit down first wins.

1) Form a circle with chairs numbered one fewer than the participants.
 2) Assign fried rice ingredients such as eggs, kimchi, and green onions to players in order.
 3) When the tagger in the center calls an ingredient, the assigned players must stand up and move to a new seat, but cannot move to the immediately adjacent seat.
 4) When the tagger calls Fried Rice, everyone must switch seats, and the tagger may call one to three ingredients at once.
Chairs (one fewer than the number of players)
배팅 티, 공, 배트, 줄긋기 기구

1) Mark a tee-ball field on the ground with zones 1 and 2 and 1-, 2-, and 3-point lines, then set up a batting tee.
 2) The batter loudly calls out which of the two zones they will aim for and then hits the ball off the tee.
 3) Earn 1 to 3 points based on where the ball lands, and receive double points if it lands in the announced zone.
 4) Each player takes 3 swings, and the player with the highest total score wins.
Batting tee, ball, bat, line marker

1) One runner per team sprints to the marker cone.
 2) Jump left and right over the cone as one rep, completing a total of 5 reps.
 3) After jumping 5 times, run around the cone and sprint back to the starting line.
 4) Teammates run in relay format, and the first team whose runners all finish wins.
Side-to-Side Ball Pass and Relay Game

1) Set cones about 8 meters apart as turning points, line up team members in a single file, and have the first runner hold the ball.
 2) On the start signal, pass the ball alternately left and right starting from the left side.
 3) When the last runner receives the ball, sprint forward around both cones, and return to the front of the line.
 4) Continue the sequence until all runners finish circling the cones; the first team to sit down wins.

1) Form 4 to 5 lines using chairs as markers.
 2) Place 3 to 5 players in each line and designate 1 tagger.
 3) When the tagger touches a line, the players in that line must run and move.
 4) The last person to return becomes the next tagger, and becoming the tagger requires doing 5 squats.

1) Draw butterfly-shaped offensive and defensive zones and place a batting tee in the center.
 2) Form two teams of 4-5 players each, and the batter hits the ball off the tee.
 3) Once the ball is hit, all offensive teammates circle the bases in the opposite zone together and return home.
 4) The offense scores 1 point if they reach home before the defense fields and throws the ball through all 4 bases.

1) Form pairs, place two pizzas (flying discs) next to cones, and assign a runner and a receiver.
 2) On signal, the runner dashes to pick up a pizza, delivers it to the partner, and runs back for the next.
 3) Switch roles and repeat once both pizzas have been delivered.
 4) The team that delivers two pizzas the fastest wins; increase distance or pizza count to add challenge.

1) Prepare foam balls and split into two teams: one team outside and the other inside the donut zone.
 2) The outside team passes the ball to their captain standing in the center.
 3) Score 1 point when the captain successfully catches the ball.
 4) Switch offense and defense after a time limit of 2 or 3 minutes.
Foam ball (or soft volleyball), team vests

1) Line up in a single file holding the shoulders of the person in front to form a blindfolded train.
 2) Except for the lead guide at the front, all team members close their eyes or wear blindfolds.
 3) Following the guide's directions, navigate between crouching obstacle participants, chairs, and tables to reach the destination without colliding.
 4) Measure the time it takes for each team to reach the destination, and the team with the faster time wins.

1) Place a hoop in the center of the playing area, and form groups of three around the hoop.
 2) Two players hold hands to create a clam, and the remaining player stands inside to become the pearl.
 3) When the tagger inside the center hoop calls out 'Clam' or 'Pearl', players with that role must step into the hoop and find a new partner.
 4) The player left without a group becomes the new tagger.
풍선, 줄, 막대, 이름 적힌 붙임 쪽지, 조끼, 긴 줄
Grade 1 Movement Activities from People Textbook

1) Stretch back and forth holding a balloon, then tap the balloon to keep it airborne as long as possible.
 2) Play rock-paper-scissors where the winner flees to a safe zone and the loser chases to tag.
 3) Practice jumping high by tapping a suspended balloon or sticking a note high on a wall, and play jump tag where players leap on the tagger's cue.
 4) Perform long rope limbo, balance beam walking, dodging swinging ropes, figure-8 tag, and rock-paper-scissors step racing.
Balloons, Strings, Sticks, Sticky notes with names, Pinnies, Long jump ropes

1) Form two teams of 4 to 6 players based on court size, set up goals at both ends of a rectangular field with a 1-3m goal area marked by cones, and greet each other.
 2) Move the big ball toward the opponent goal by kicking or throwing it.
 3) Once holding the ball, players cannot travel but may pivot on one foot, passing from that spot while defenders stay at least 1m away.
 4) Scoring into the opponent goal earns 1 point, and entering the goal area is prohibited.

1) Form two teams of 9 players each, and set up a field with 15m base distances, tee-ball, and a batting tee.
 2) Begin offense with runners placed on assigned bases such as 1st, 2nd, or 3rd base.
 3) Batters are out if a fly ball is caught or if the ball reaches the base before the runner; each runner reaching home scores 1 point.
 4) Switch sides after 2 outs, play 3 innings each, and the team with the higher score wins.

1) All students stand in a circle.
 2) The space from one's left foot to the right friend's left foot serves as each player's goal and defense zone.
 3) When the ball comes, players kick it forward.
 4) A player is eliminated if the ball passes through their defense zone, and the last surviving players (around four) win.

1) Form pairs with two students.
 2) One student hangs on the horizontal bar to act like an animal, and the partner guesses it.
 3) Earn 1 point for every correct guess.
 4) Switch roles and continue; the pair with the highest score within the time limit wins.

1) Form two teams of 10 players each to play as offense and defense.
 2) The batter hits the ball and runs the bases; each runner reaching home scores 1 point.
 3) A runner is out if a fly ball is caught directly or if the defense throws to the base or home ahead of the runner.
 4) Teams switch sides after all batters finish their turn, playing 3 innings to decide the winner.
줄, 짐볼, 배드민턴 라켓, 셔틀콕, 공 2개

1) Single-leg stand with alternating hops: Partners face each other and hop switching feet on signal, balancing on one leg.
 2) Single-leg balance with a rope: Hook a rope around the ankle or foot and lift backward, or step on the rope with one foot while lifting the other foot and pulling the rope to the sides.
 3) Stability ball balance: Sit on a gym ball and maintain steady balance in proper posture without shaking.
 4) Coordination exercises: Bounce a shuttlecock on a badminton racket without dropping it, or bounce two balls simultaneously with both hands.
Rope, gym ball, badminton racket, shuttlecock, 2 balls

1) Four students form a group, choose one equipment per group, and stand in a circle to decide the order.
 2) The first member expresses a movement using the equipment.
 3) The second member mimics the first member's movement and adds a new movement, continuing in turn.
 4) Any member who fails to mimic or add a new movement sits down, and the game continues until one person remains.

1) Form a group of four players.
 2) Each player throws a beanbag five times using a chosen throwing method suited to their skill level.
 3) Earn points indicated on the basket when the beanbag lands inside.
 4) Sum the scores of all team members; the group with the highest total score wins.

1) Form groups of five and assign one member to place balls into the hoop.
 2) The first runner holds a ball with their feet and rolls backward like a roly-poly to drop it into the hoop above their head.
 3) The next member transfers a ball in the same manner; if a ball rolls out of the hoop, the assigned helper puts it back in.
 4) The group that transfers five balls first wins.
Basic Walking Techniques on the Balance Beam

1) Spread arms for balance and walk forward step by step, letting the toes graze the side of the beam.
 2) Spread arms for balance and walk backward step by step, feeling for foot placement with the toes without turning the head.
 3) Spread arms sideways and walk cross-stepping by crossing the right leg in front of the left leg and placing it next to the left foot.
빈 곳으로 움직이며 공 던지고 잡기
Moving to Open Space Pass and Catch Game

1) Form groups of six, and designate one player from each team as the goal.
 2) Move by passing and catching or dribbling the ball, and score a point by passing to the goal player.
 3) When moving three steps or more, you must dribble the ball by bouncing it.
 4) Possession switches upon fumbling or having the ball intercepted, and the team with the most points within the time limit wins.

1) Divide the class into 4 groups and set team positions, target beanbag colors, and running order.
 2) On the start signal, the first runner picks up a beanbag placed in the center of the play area.
 3) Navigate through the obstacle course and place the beanbag into the team hoop.
 4) Run back quickly to tag the next teammate's hand, and the team that collects the most beanbags within the time limit wins.

1) Approach smoothly, increasing speed with the final 3 steps being the fastest.
 2) Plant the take-off foot from the heel with strong, explosive force.
 3) Swing the lead leg over the bar followed immediately by lifting the trailing leg.
 4) Maintain balance and land one foot at a time while flexing knees safely on the mat.
High jump bar, stands, landing mat
태권도 공격 기본 기능(지르기 및 차기)

1) In a horse-riding stance, twist the punch palm-down to strike trunk, face, or low area.
 2) Bend and extend the knee to front kick with the ball of the foot, then recover quickly.
 3) Turn the body 90 degrees and kick sideways with the blade or heel of the foot.
 4) Turn the body 90 degrees and snap the foot in a wide arc using the instep to roundhouse kick.

1) Hold a basketball behind your head with both hands, bend your upper body forward, and bounce it forcefully forward.
 2) Set feet shoulder-width apart, bend knees, and explode upward while swinging both arms up for a standing vertical jump.
 3) Lower your stance, jump forcefully while spreading both legs sideways, touch your feet with your hands, and land softly.
 4) Jump rhythmically one foot at a time over several low hurdles set at regular intervals.

1) Divide the class into four teams at the corners, give rings equal to members, and pair up.
 2) On start, pairs hold hands, spin around as they move forward, and place a ring on the cone.
 3) Return by running straight without spinning and high-five the next pair.
 4) Teams earn 4, 3, 2, or 1 point based on finishing order, plus 2 bonus points for no falls; highest total points wins.

1) Nine players form a team, and two teams play the game.
 2) The kicker kicks the ball rolled by the pitcher, and scores 1 point if the kicker or runners circle all bases and return home.
 3) The kicker is out if the defense catches a fly ball or reaches the base with the ball before the runner.
 4) Teams switch after three outs, and the team with more points after five innings wins.

1) Serve the shuttlecock from below the waist level.
 2) The receiving side must not move before the opponent serves.
 3) Hit the shuttlecock without contacting it twice consecutively.
 4) Maintain the rally without touching the net with the racket or body.
반원기둥 모양 블록, 후프, 블록, 반원 모양 공, 콩주머니

1) Form a team of four students.
 2) At the starting signal, all team members run together and carry out the balance missions in order from zone 1 to zone 4.
 3) Hold balance for 10 seconds on semi-cylindrical blocks in zone 1, pass through hoops while balancing in zone 2, balance on one foot on a block for 10 seconds in zone 3, and balance with legs on a hemisphere ball for 10 seconds in zone 4.
 4) Earn one beanbag for each successful teammate in each zone, and the team with the most beanbags at the end wins.
Semi-cylindrical blocks, hoops, balance blocks, dome balance balls, beanbags

1) Start gradually, build speed until take-off, and slightly shorten the last stride.
 2) Take off strongly with a comfortable foot, placing full weight on the foot, and swing the other leg horizontally upwards.
 3) Arch the body like a bow at the peak, then extend arms and legs forward before landing.
 4) Land safely by bending the knees and leaning forward to avoid falling backward.
East West South North Rolling Relay

1) Divide the class into four groups, decide the rolling order within each group, and line up at the four starting points.
 2) On the start signal, the first runner departs, performs the assigned rolling task on each mat, and circles the play area.
 3) Upon returning to the start, tag hands with the next teammate, who then circles the area in the same manner.
 4) The group whose final runner returns first wins.

1) Divide the entire class into three teams and place hoops along with spot markers of varying point values (1, 2, 3 points) on the ground.
