Red Light Green Light Dribbling Game

1) Choose one tagger.
 2) While the tagger says "Red Light, Green Light," the other players dribble the ball toward the tagger.
 3) If a player moves when the tagger turns around, they are out and must move to the designated area to dribble until the game ends.
 4) The player who touches the tagger's back first without getting caught wins.

1) Place your foot on the starting block and sprint forward quickly at the starting signal.
 2) Gradually raise your upper body and widen your stride.
 3) Lift your knees high and swing your arms back and forth vigorously while running.
 4) Run through without reducing speed until the very end.

1) Form a group of six and choose one tagger.
 2) The tagger dribbles a ball to chase group members, while the others dribble away to escape.
 3) Players inside a safe zone cannot be tagged, but only one player can be inside at a time.
 4) If a player steps outside the boundary or is touched by the tagger, they become the new tagger.

1) Divide the class into two teams and pair students up within each team to set an order.
 2) On the starting signal, each pair moves forward while throwing and catching a ball around the turning point.
 3) The player holding the ball may take only one step, and if the ball is dropped, they must hold it for 3 seconds before throwing.
 4) The team whose final pair returns to the start line first wins.

1) Divide the entire class into two teams, hold hands within each team, and walk in a circle.
 2) For weaving, the first member of the team passes under the arms of the last and second-to-last members, repeating until everyone is interwoven.
 3) For unweaving, the first member reverses direction and passes under the arms of the second and subsequent members to untangle the line.
 4) The team that completes both weaving and unweaving first wins.

1) Four players form a group and determine the bowling order.
 2) Each player takes turns rolling the ball, choosing a distance of either 7m or 10m.
 3) Knocking down a pin from 7m scores 1 point each, and from 10m scores 2 points each.
 4) The scores of all group members are totaled, and the group with the highest score wins.

1) Divide the class into two groups and decide the rolling order.
 2) On the start signal, the first member rolls hugging a ball to the turning point and back.
 3) Hand over the ball with both hands to the next person without throwing.
 4) The group whose final member returns to the starting line first wins.
우리 반 육상 대회 기록 도전

1) Divide the class into four groups: two groups compete while the other two officiate.
 2) Switch roles once measurement is complete.
 3) All groups participate in the relay.
 4) Clear the bar using either scissors jump or flop style to challenge records.

1) For backhand grip, place the thumb on top, index finger around the rim, and remaining fingers supporting underneath.
 2) For backhand throw, stand shoulder-width apart facing the target with your shoulder line, extend arm back, shift weight forward, and throw with wrist snap.
 3) For forehand throw, grip with thumb on top and index/middle fingers underneath, extend arm back, straighten elbow, and throw with wrist snap.
 4) Catch chest-high discs by clapping hands together vertically, and catch discs flying toward your front by bringing both palms facing forward together.

1) Form groups of 6 and decide the dribbling order within each team.
 2) At the start signal, one player from each side dribbles the ball with a stick along the inner and outer paths.
 3) When encountering an opponent, play rock-paper-scissors; the winner keeps moving forward while the loser's team sends the next runner.
 4) The team that reaches the opponent's area first wins.

1) In groups of five, one student holds the number cards while the other four decide their rolling order and turn around.
 2) On the start signal, the first student performs a forward roll, reads, and memorizes the number on the card.
 3) All remaining group members take turns performing a forward roll.
 4) The group adds up all the numbers they saw and shouts the total; if incorrect, they restart from the beginning, and the first group to answer correctly wins.

1) Engage the core muscles that serve as the body's center to maintain balance.
 2) Start with simple balancing movements that you can comfortably perform.
 3) Gradually challenge yourself with more difficult balance postures.
 4) Practice advanced movements slowly following the demonstration.

1) Form two teams of 6 players each.
 2) Grab a ball from the central box with your hands and move quickly up to the restricted area in the opponent zone.
 3) Toss the ball into the basket located in the opponent zone without entering the restricted area.
 4) The team that puts the most balls into the opponent basket within the set time wins.
원 마커, 배드민턴 라켓, 셔틀콕, 네트

1) Two players form a team and two teams play across the net.
 2) Each player sets a spot marker for their defensive position, stands with one foot on it, hits the incoming shuttlecock, and returns to the spot marker.
 3) If a player hits the shuttlecock without returning to the spot marker, the opposing team scores 1 point.
 4) A team scores 1 point if the shuttlecock lands on the opponent's court floor or if the opponent hits it out of bounds, and the first team to reach 15 points wins.
Spot markers, badminton rackets, shuttlecock, net

1) Form groups of four and decide the rolling order within each group.
 2) On the start signal, the first runner lies down on the mat with the body straight and rolls.
 3) Upon reaching the finish, stand up and shout 'Arrived'.
 4) The next teammate starts upon hearing the call, and the group whose final runner finishes first wins.
Hit Over the Net Shuttlecock Game

1) Four players form a group, and two groups play against each other.
 2) Set the order within each group, and each player hits a shuttlecock over the net with a racket.
 3) Score the points designated to the area where the shuttlecock lands.
 4) Sum up all team members' scores, and the group with the highest score wins.

1) Three players form a team and two teams play using only half of a basketball court.
 2) Evade the opposing team by dribbling or passing to score: 2 points inside the 3-point line and 3 points outside.
 3) After stealing the ball or scoring, send the ball outside the 3-point line before starting the attack.
 4) The team that first reaches 20 points within the set time wins.

1) Two players sit shoulder-to-shoulder, wrapping the left hand around the leg satba from inside to outside and gripping the waist satba with the right hand.
 2) On the 'ready' signal, both players stand up while holding the satba.
 3) On the 'start' signal, use your strength and body weight to pull or push the satba to disrupt the opponent's center of gravity.
 4) The player who takes down the opponent first or forces them out of the mat wins.

1) Divide the entire class into three groups.
 2) Roll balls of various sizes into the circle.
 3) Earn 1 point for a large ball inside the circle and 2 points for a small ball; knock opponent balls out of the circle by rolling.
 4) The group with the highest score within the given time wins.

1) Form groups of four and decide the order of players.
 2) On the starting signal, the first player dribbles the ball with a stick, weaving through the obstacles.
 3) Turn around the final obstacle and dribble the ball back to the starting line.
 4) Pass the ball to the next teammate to continue, and the group whose final player returns to the starting line first wins.

1) Six players form a team and two teams play the game.
 2) Place two different colored cones at each end of each team's area.
 3) Hit the ball to strike the opposing team's cone to score 1 point.
 4) The team with the most points within the set time wins.

1) Six players form a team.
 2) Teammates pass and catch the ball to advance toward the opponent's goal area, moving up to a maximum of three steps while holding the ball.
 3) Defenders must stay more than 1 meter away from the offensive player holding the ball.
 4) Scoring 1 point occurs when a player enters the opponent's goal area with the ball, and the team with the most points within the set time limit wins.

1) Form groups of four and assign teams into offense and defense.
 2) The offense serves from the designated serve area.
 3) The defense receives the served ball and scores 1 point if they pass the ball to all team members.
 4) Switch offense and defense after all offensive players finish serving, and the team with more points wins.

1) Form two teams of 5 players each (Tigers and Lions) standing face to face across two starting lines.
 2) When the teacher calls Tigers, the Tigers chase the Lions; when Lions is called, the reverse takes place.
 3) The team that tags more opponents within the allotted time wins the game.
Kick and Run Around the Cone

1) Teams of six divide into offense and defense to play against each other.
 2) Offensive players take turns kicking the ball, rounding a cone, and returning to the home base.
 3) Defenders stop the kicked ball with their feet, pick it up with their hands, and send it to the defense home.
 4) If the runner arrives before the ball, the offense scores 1 point; teams switch roles and the higher score wins.

1) Divide the class into 4 groups and prepare 4 balls per group.
 2) On the start signal, go to an opponent's hoop and dribble back one ball at a time.
 3) Place the retrieved ball into your own group's hoop.
 4) The first group to collect 6 balls wins.
손짚고 옆돌기 단계별 연습(발박수, 다리 넘겨 착지, 옆돌기)
Progressive Cartwheel Practice (Foot Clap, Side Kick Landing, Full Cartwheel)

1) Crouch down, place both hands on the mat, kick legs up, and clap feet together.
 2) Place both hands on the mat with knees bent, kick both legs up strongly, and pass them sideways to land.
 3) Place hands one at a time and kick legs one at a time while bending knees to perform a cartwheel.
 4) Face forward, step one foot forward, place hands down while pushing off with the back foot, spread legs wide to support body, and push off the mat to stand up.
운동을 오래 할 수 있는 힘을 기르는 운동

1) Look forward and step up onto the step box one foot at a time, then step down in the same order.
 2) Place hands on waist, step on the box, and drive the opposite knee up toward the chest before stepping down.
 3) Run and walk without resting for a set duration or distance.
 4) Look forward, hold the jump rope, and jump with both feet together on each rope turn.
물과 친해지는 다양한 활동 및 뜨기

1) Lightly splash water, kick while sitting, hold breath underwater, and walk by holding shoulders or the pool wall in shallow water.
 2) Wet and immerse the face, hold breath underwater, pick up baduk stones, and play rock-paper-scissors underwater.
 3) Float in the water using methods like prone float, jellyfish float, tuck float, back float holding a kickboard, and jellyfish/starfish float.

1) Place spot markers at 12, 3, 6, and 9 o'clock directions centered around a middle spot marker.
 2) Represent the time called by the teacher while keeping one foot on the center marker.
 3) The fastest player to represent the time earns 1 point.
 4) Play 10 rounds, and the player with the highest score wins.
Kick the Ball and Hit the Cone Game

1) Form two teams of 7 players each, and place a cone inside a hula hoop to make a goal area that cannot be entered.
 2) The attacking team dribbles, passes, and traps the ball with their feet to hit the opponent's cone while evading defenders.
 3) The defending team defends the cone; possession switches if defenders steal the ball or if it goes out of bounds.
 4) The team that hits the opponent's cone first wins the game.

1) Bend alternately left and right within a comfortable range of motion without overstraining.
 2) Pull your left and right feet alternately.
 3) Practice reaching so that both hands and one foot touch alternately.
골프형 활동 기본 기능(채 잡기 및 공 보내기)
Basic Skills for Golf-Type Activities (Grip and Striking)

1) Grip the end of the club with the left hand like a handshake, and cover the left thumb with the right hand.
 2) Stand with feet shoulder-width apart forming a Y-shape with arms and club, swing like a clock pendulum, hit the ball, and extend arms toward the target.
 3) Stand with knees slightly bent, lift the club back while cocking the wrists, and shift body weight to the right leg.
 4) Keep eyes on the ball, shift weight to the left leg, swing down wrists and arms to hit the ball, and follow through forward.

1) Form a group of 4 players and divide into offense and defense groups.
 2) The offense group moves far while passing the ball.
 3) The defense group steals the ball from the offense group.
 4) When the defense steals the ball, they score points marked on that zone and switch offense and defense.

1) Two players stand on opposite sides of one kickboard facing each other and hold it firmly.
 2) At the start signal, kick hard to push the kickboard toward the opponent.
 3) The game ends after the set time, and the player who pushes the kickboard farther toward the opponent wins.

1) Form a team of 6 where one person rolls a die and the rest prepare in push-up positions.
 2) Everyone performs push-ups equal to the rolled number on the die.
 3) Rotate roles so all teammates take turns rolling the die and doing push-ups.
 4) After the activity, the team with the highest total push-up repetitions wins.

1) Divide the entire class into three groups and determine the rolling order within each group.
 2) At the start signal, the first runner rolls forward along a straight line toward the turning point, and rolls along a curved line when returning.
 3) When the first runner returns past the turning point, the next runner starts.
 4) The group whose final runner returns to the starting line first wins.

1) Divide the whole class into four groups and decide the running order for each group.
 2) At the start signal, fit a cone onto one foot in the team area.
 3) Move to the center game area on one foot and stand the cone upright; if the cone drops or both feet touch the ground, go to the back of the line.
 4) Return to tag the next runner's hand, and the group that stands the most cones within the time limit wins.

1) Form groups of five and play against each other.
 2) The batter kicks a stationary ball, picks up a beanbag at first base, and runs back home.
 3) When a fielder catches the ball, all fielders freeze in place and pass the ball to every teammate without dropping it.
 4) The fielding team scores 1 point if they finish passing before the runner reaches home; the batting team scores 1 point if the runner returns home first, and teams switch sides after all batters finish.

1) Form groups of four and decide the jumping order.
 2) Place the crossbar at knee height and take turns jumping over it.
 3) After clearing knee height, gradually raise the crossbar to hip height and navel height.
 4) Scoring is based on height cleared: knee height earns 1 point, hip height earns 2 points, and navel height earns 3 points; the team with the highest total score wins.
물속 호흡과 발차기 및 자유형 팔 돌리기
Swimming Breathing, Kicking, and Freestyle Arm Strokes

1) Hold the pool wall, straighten your body to float, and kick up and down with your entire legs while exhaling through the nose.
 2) Lift your head, exhale remaining air through your mouth, and inhale deeply.
 3) Hold a kickboard with relaxed ankles, bend your knees slightly, push the water down with your thighs, and lift your head to breathe when out of breath.
 4) Pull water with your hands, push one arm back, turn your head to the side to breathe, and alternate arm rotations towards your head.

1) Divide the class into three teams—Grape, Tomato, and Watermelon—and assign one spinning motion to each team.
 2) When the teacher calls out a fruit name, that entire team becomes taggers and chases members of the other teams.
 3) Taggers earn 1 point per tag; runners performing the designated spinning motion on a spot marker are safe.
 4) The tagger role shifts as different fruits are called, and the team with the most points after the designated time wins.

1) Two players stand facing each other with their feet placed heel-to-toe and play rock-paper-scissors.
 2) The winner moves backward by placing the front foot against the heel of the back foot.
 3) The loser slides the front foot forward to touch the tip of the winner's front foot.
 4) Repeat the rounds until a player can no longer spread their legs to determine the outcome.
Hit into the Empty Space Fist Baseball Game

1) Form groups of six students and play a game between two teams.
 2) The batter hits the ball with a fist and scores 1 point by rounding the 1-point cone to home, or 2 points by rounding the 2-point cone to home.
 3) The batter is out if the fielding team catches a fly ball directly or throws the ball home before the runner arrives.
 4) When all batters finish their turns, teams switch offense and defense, and the team with more points wins.

1) Divide the entire class into four groups, decide each group's running order, and stand next to your group's hoop.
 2) At the start signal, the first runner takes a beanbag from their hoop and carries it into the line marked in the center.
 3) Place the beanbag inside the line and shout "Transfer Complete" to signal the next runner to go.
 4) The group that moves all of their beanbags inside the line first wins.
Pass Game in the Scoring Area

1) Five players form a team and two teams prepare to play.
 2) Pass the ball with teammates to move into the scoring area.
 3) Score points equal to the number of passes completed inside the scoring area.
 4) Possession changes upon turnover, and the team with more points in the set time wins.
Jump Rope Techniques and Partner Jumping

1) Jump with feet together, then jump while spreading feet apart.
 2) Alternate left and right feet according to the rhythm of the turning rope.
 3) Lift one foot back to jump, swing it forward down to jump, and repeat with the other foot.
 4) Two people face the same direction or each other while one turns the rope, or stand side-by-side holding one handle each to turn and jump together.

1) Form a group of four and decide the jumping order.
 2) Place a sticker on the mat.
 3) Set the bar at waist height, take an approach run in turn, and jump over the bar.
 4) Tuck the chin and land on the back so that the sticker attaches to the back.

1) Divide the class into three groups and decide the rolling order within each group.
 2) The first runner sits touching the soles of their feet and holding their ankles, while the second runner rolls a die.
 3) Roll around the front cone if the die is odd, or the back cone if even.
 4) When the runner returns, the next player rolls the die and continues; the first team whose final runner finishes wins.

1) Form groups of four and decide the swimming order within each group.
 2) Each member swims 25m freestyle in order.
 3) Sum the time records of all four group members.
 4) Determine the final group rankings based on the combined total time.

1) Divide the entire class into two teams, form pairs of three within each team, and set the turn order.
 2) On the start signal, the first pair rolls a die and throws and catches the ball as many times as the number rolled.
 3) Upon completing the throws and catches, return to the start line and hand the ball to the next pair.
 4) The team whose final pair returns to the starting line first wins.

1) Arrange 12 stacking cups into three stacks of 3, 6, and 3.
 2) Perform up-stacking on the 3, 6, and 3 stacks in sequence from left or right depending on handedness.
 3) Perform down-stacking in the same direction starting from the side where up-stacking began.
 4) If a fumbling mistake occurs during up-stacking, return to the previous state to fix it immediately, and stop the timer with both hands.

1) Practice diagonal tosses 5 times each with the dominant and non-dominant hand using one ball.
 2) Hold two balls and practice tossing from the dominant hand to catch in front of the ball in the other hand.
 3) Hold 3 balls (2 in dominant hand, 1 in other) and perform continuous alternating diagonal tosses.
 4) Challenge for 8 rounds by performing the designated diagonal juggling routine for 1 minute per round.

1) Hold 2 balls in the dominant hand and 1 in the other, practicing diagonal tosses just above eye level.
 2) Toss all 3 balls consecutively in a steady half-beat rhythm across your body in right-left-right sequence.
 3) Practice catching ball 1 with the opposite hand at the exact moment the 3rd ball is tossed.
 4) Follow a 4-beat cadence to catch both the 1st and 2nd balls smoothly, training across 8 one-minute rounds.

1) Choose a push-up difficulty level suitable for your own fitness level.
 2) Complete a target of 50 push-ups as quickly as possible within a 4-minute time limit.
 3) Record the time taken to complete 50 reps, or record the number of reps completed if unfinished in 4 minutes.

1) Hold two balls in your right hand and one in your left.
 2) Toss a ball diagonally from the right hand on an off-beat rhythm.
 3) As the third ball is thrown, catch ball 1 with the left hand, ball 2 with the right hand on beat 4, and the remaining ball with the left hand on beat 5.
 4) Gradually increase the number of catches to complete continuous toss juggling with both hands.

1) Divide 12 cups into two stacks of 6 cups each.
 2) Pick up 3 cups in the right hand and 2 in the left, then stack a 6-cup pyramid on the left followed by the right to complete upstacking.
 3) Downstack the left pyramid into 3 cups in each hand, slide down the right pyramid, and collapse all cups into a single 12-cup stack.
 4) Divide the collapsed 12-cup stack back into two sets of 6 and repeat to minimize completion time.

1) Students on the left are Magpies and on the right are Crows, standing with adjacent feet touching while facing the teacher.
 2) When the teacher calls Magpie, Magpies chase Crows, and when the teacher calls Crow, Crows chase Magpies.
 3) Students who are tagged or fail to tag their opponent before the blue cone must do 5 jumping jacks.

1) Divide into four teams and choose one strong rock-paper-scissors player from each team to stand as a defender in front of the opposing team.
 2) Set cones about 15m apart and have each team line up in a single file behind the starting line.
 3) On the whistle, the first runner sprints forward to play rock-paper-scissors against the defender.
 4) If the runner wins, they move to the finish area and the next runner starts; if they lose, they return to the back of their team's line and the next runner goes.

1) A toss decides the initial serve and court; singles is played 1-on-1 and doubles 2-on-2.
 2) The side scoring 21 points first wins a game, and at 20-all, play continues until a 2-point lead is reached (at 29-all, the first to 30 wins).
 3) Serve from the right court on zero or even points, and from the left court on odd points diagonally.
 4) The entire shuttlecock must be below 1.15 meters from the court floor when hit, without stepping on the service line.
PAPS 측정 장비(20m 음원, 좌전굴 측정기, 악력계), 초시계
Student Physical Activity Promotion System (PAPS) Measurement and Procedures

1) In the 20m shuttle run, run between lines to the audio cues; the test ends when a student fails to cross with both feet before the beep twice.
 2) In the sit-and-reach test, remove shoes, place feet flat against the board, overlap hands, bend forward, and hold the position for at least 2 seconds.
 3) For grip strength, stand straight with feet shoulder-width apart, grip the dynamometer at a right angle with the second knuckle without touching the body, alternating twice per hand.
 4) In the 50m sprint, start from the sequence 'On your mark, Set, Go' and sprint across the finish line.
PAPS testing equipment (20m audio cue, sit-and-reach box, grip dynamometer), stopwatch

1) Two students face each other or turn around to get ready.
 2) On the whistle, race to grab the Jumbo Stacks placed in the middle.
 3) Play in a survival format to determine the final winner.
Balance and Stability Training for Fitness

1) Stand shoulder-width apart with hands on hips, lift one leg to shift weight, and lower it slowly (3 sets of 10 reps).
 2) Balance on one foot with the other foot placed on the inner knee while extending arms overhead.
 3) Hinge at the hip on one leg, extending the opposite leg back and arms to the side in a T-pose for 10 seconds.
가정에서 해보는 앉아서 윗몸 앞으로 굽히기 유연성 운동
Seated Forward Bend Flexibility Exercise at Home

1) Warm up first by rotating wrists and ankles and stretching joint areas.
 2) Sit upright on the floor or mat with legs fully extended without bending knees.
 3) Exhale slowly while bending the upper body forward, reaching hands as far forward as possible.
 4) Hold the lowest point for 2 to 3 seconds to measure flexibility, then maintain stretches for 10 seconds per posture.

1) Lightly warm up in place to prepare for the exercise.
 2) Perform full-body movements with full effort during the set work intervals following the audio cues.
 3) Take brief rests and move to the next exercise, repeating the cycle for 4 minutes.
양말과 공을 활용한 배드민턴 백스윙 연습
소프트 테니스공 2개, 양말, 부러진 라켓, 테이프, 라바콘 1개
Badminton Backswing Practice Using Socks and Balls

1) Make a practice tool by putting two soft tennis balls into a sock and taping it to a broken racket shaft.
 2) Swing the tool to practice wrist rotation and transitions between forehand and backhand grips.
 3) Place a cone on your head and practice dropping it by swinging the tool past the head.
 4) Begin the backswing preparation slowly and accelerate sharply as the tool passes behind your back into the forward swing.
Two soft tennis balls, sock, broken racket, tape, 1 cone

1) Stand with both feet on a spot marker, then step one foot out to maintain balance and movement.
 2) Right-handed players hold the paddle grip so that the printed graphic face is not visible.
 3) Hold the tip of the shuttlecock feathers with the non-dominant thumb and index finger, drop it, and gently tap it upward with the paddle.
 4) Once comfortable, alternate using both sides of the paddle or set target numbers of consecutive bounces.

1) Stand on the mat with hands placed close to the feet.
 2) Tuck the head to look toward the navel and lift the hips to round the body.
 3) Roll forward making sure the back of the head touches the mat first rather than the top of the head.
 4) Use the rolling momentum to grab the knees with both hands and stand up.

1) Hold the handler racket and place 2 students per half badminton court into their own designated zones.
 2) Practice bouncing a floorball ball using knee rebounds for balance, then switch to a shuttlecock.
 3) Keep hitting the shuttlecock upward without dropping it, utilizing both sides of the racket alternately.
 4) Players must not leave their designated area; those who drop the shuttlecock sit down to avoid interfering until the last survivor remains.

1) Teams of three play on a court marked with cone goal areas and mini goals.
 2) Players advance the ball through passing without physical contact.
 3) Shots are taken outside the goal crease starting with bounce shots in phase one and direct shots in phase two.
 4) Only the goalkeeper enters the goal crease and goals by girls award three points in coed games.

1) Kneel on the floor with hands held down at a right angle, then underhand pass when the ball arrives so that fingernails face the partner.
 2) Raise one knee and pass while keeping hands lowered at a right angle during ready stance.
 3) Stand slightly with bent knees and pass without fully straightening the knees upon rising.
 4) Keep hands free in a relaxed stance and only join hands when the ball comes, moving feet to anticipate the landing spot and lowering the center of gravity with legs spread before passing.

1) Acclimate to the mats, place hands close to the feet, tuck the chin so the back of the head touches the mat, and roll rounded.
 2) Tuck knees tightly toward the chest during the roll and use momentum to stand up immediately.
 3) Practice on an inclined mat to let gravity help carry the body smoothly forward into a stand.
 4) Place an obstacle such as a mini hurdle in front of the feet and reach hands forward to add forward momentum to the roll.

1) Start with a low height so students can experience success.
 2) Encourage students to place their hands as far forward as possible.
 3) Once comfortable, increase the height step by step.
 4) When proficient, remove extra obstacles, run up quickly, and vault over placing hands far ahead.
배드민턴 스텝 및 셔틀콕 치기 연습

1) Challenge hitting diagonal shuttlecocks consecutively twice.
 2) Step out smoothly using forehand or backhand footwork after hitting.
 3) Apply various footwork patterns such as quick steps, left-right sequences, or walking steps.
 4) Grip with the thumb positioned flat along the handle when hitting backhands.

1) The fielding team spreads out, bends their knees, and gets ready in a low stance to catch the ball.
 2) The kicking team kicks the ball and runs through 4 bases in order to score at home.
 3) On a ground ball, the fielding team lines up and passes the ball between their legs; the first fielder to touch the ball defends home plate, while the 9th fielder throws the ball home.
 4) A point is scored or prevented based on whether the runner or the ball reaches home plate first.
제자리 배드민턴 스윙 및 셔틀콕 던지기 연습
Badminton Stationary Swing and Shuttlecock Throwing Practice

1) Face forward and practice stationary swings using waist rotation.
 2) Raise the elbow and execute a complete follow-through.
 3) Stand sideways holding a shuttlecock instead of a racquet, throw upward like a pitcher for clear mechanics, and throw forward for smash mechanics.
 4) Coordinate connected body parts (waist, elbow, ankle, non-dominant arm) simultaneously when hitting.

1) Set up a net in the center of the court and divide into two teams.
 2) Serve by bouncing the ball on the floor from designated position 'T' and kicking it over.
 3) Each individual can touch the ball up to two consecutive times, and a direct volley counts as one touch.
 4) Pass among teammates and send the ball over the net within five touches.

1) Move 1: Jump by bringing feet together and opening them wide (Muk-Jji-Ppa step).
 2) Move 2: Bounce and jump alternately from side to side.
 3) Move 3: Jump while crossing feet forward and backward.
 4) Move 4: Jump crossing feet in an X-shape, then combine with arm motions (head-shoulders-cross-shoulders) to upbeat music.

1) Step forward and push the pass forward with backs of hands facing outward.
 2) Aim bounce passes at two-thirds of the floor distance toward the receiver's chest.
 3) Use quick, low underhand passes when playing against taller defenders.
 4) Execute hook passes swinging the arm in an arc over the shoulder.
셔틀콕 줍기 스텝 및 던지기 연습
Shuttlecock Pickup Step and Throwing Drill

1) Step forward with the right foot and right hand together to pick up the shuttlecock.
 2) Turn the body and recover backwards.
 3) Shift weight onto the left foot to balance and simulate a throwing motion.
 4) Repeat the sequence in rhythm with the footwork.
큰 공, 작은 공, 앵글볼 목표물 거치대, 팀조끼

1) Both teams line up at starting lines and run toward the center balls upon signal.
 2) The large ball is used to score by hitting down the target ball.
 3) Small balls are thrown at opponents like dodgeball; hit players must return to their starting line before rejoining.
 4) A player holding the large ball who gets hit by a small ball must drop it and back away at least 3 meters.
Large ball, small balls, target goal stand, team pinnies

1) Maintain a stance matching the width of the vaulting box in a ready position.
 2) Move the racket arm and leg simultaneously toward the incoming shuttlecock.
 3) Strike the shuttlecock with a forehand or backhand stroke as soon as the right foot touches the floor.
 4) Quickly return to the starting position and prepare for the next shot.
Badminton racket, shuttlecock, vaulting box, net

1) Draw a court and place spot markers along the outfield for each thrower.
 2) Each thrower stands on a spot marker and rolls or throws the gym ball to hit players inside.
 3) Throwers must keep at least one foot on their spot marker, and hit players are out.
 4) When time is up, count the surviving players to determine the winning team.

1) Place cones at the four room corners and set up chairs for the King in front.
 2) All students start at cone level 1 and play rock-paper-scissors with each other.
 3) Winners advance to the next corner cone, while losers remain or move back.
 4) Students who pass level 4 challenge the King, and winning replaces the King.

1) Teams of 3 to 5 players hold hands in a circle to form a protective shield.
 2) One team member wears a tail belt or team vest to become the protected target.
 3) The tagger outside the circle tries to touch the target player wearing the tail.
 4) Shield members rotate continuously to block the tagger without breaking their hand grip; if touched or if hands separate, roles swap.

1) 2-3 attackers hold dodgeballs at one end and defenders stand on the other side, while a giant die and cones numbered 2 to 6 are set outside the court.
 2) Defenders hit on the legs by thrown balls are out and line up at the waiting line outside the court.
 3) Eliminated players roll the die, run to touch the cone matching the rolled number, and revive back into the game (if 1 is rolled, move to the end of the line).
 4) Play for 3-5 minutes and count how many defenders survived.
Dodgeballs, Giant die, Numbered cones (2 to 6)

1) Divide into two teams, give each student a pom-pom ball, and line up behind the start lines at opposite ends.
 2) On the start signal, toss the pom-pom ball onto an empty spot marker.
 3) Once the ball lands on a spot marker, step onto that marker.
 4) If multiple students land on the same marker, play rock-paper-scissors; the winner takes the spot, and the loser returns to their previous spot to try again.

1) Students sit along opposite sides of the classroom, and a cone is placed as a turning point.
 2) The first runner taps the balloon continuously in the air with their hands toward the cone.
 3) After rounding the cone and returning to the start line, the next runner receives the balloon and takes off while the previous runner sits in the back.
 4) The team whose anchor returns first with the balloon wins.
Remove One Spot Marker Tag Game

1) Scatter spot markers on the gym floor fewer than the number of players and jog around freely.
 2) When the whistle blows, quickly locate an open spot marker and stand on it.
 3) If two players step on the same marker simultaneously, play Rock-Paper-Scissors to decide who stays.
 4) Players who fail to secure a marker assemble by the teacher, jog one lap around the boundary, and rejoin.
Badminton Deep Clear: Hitting Far to the Backcourt

1) Play a 1-on-1 match on a narrow court, greeting the opponent politely before and after the game.
 2) Point at the incoming shuttlecock with the non-racket hand while rotating the torso and drawing the racket back.
 3) Rotate the hips and swing the racket upward and through as if throwing it into the air to send the shuttlecock deep.
 4) When moving back for a deep shuttlecock, plant the rear foot, turn the torso, hit through the shot, and recover to center.

1) Use half of the court up to the center line and begin by bowing politely.
 2) Serve and hit the shuttlecock once over the net to land it on the opponent floor for 1 point.
 3) If the shuttlecock goes out of bounds or gets caught in the net, the opponent receives 1 point.
 4) The player who reaches the target score such as 3 points first wins the match.
배드민턴 거리 조절 서브 및 공 보내기

1) Learn backhand serve below waist level ensuring the shuttlecock crosses the opponent's service line.
 2) Practice short drop shots into the front hula hoop using gentle wrist snaps.
 3) Practice deep clears into the rear hula hoop using full body rotation to hit over the opponent's head.
 4) Apply distance control in a 1-on-1 match by aiming at open spaces in front or back.
수건 체조 (에이바 맥스 - 스윗 벗 사이코)

1) Hold a towel taut in front of the chest and lightly march in place, then lift it overhead while continuing to march.
 2) Hold the towel horizontally and rotate the torso sideways, then lift knees alternately while twisting.
 3) Hold the towel behind the body to perform jumping jacks, then bring it back in front to perform jumping jacks again.
 4) Kick feet forward and backward while holding the towel in front or overhead, and finish with side stretches and leg pulls.
Team Pinnies Focus and Agility Game

1) Face each other across a desk and place a team pinny in the center.
 2) Follow the teacher's commands (1 for head, 2 for shoulders, 3 for waist, 'turn' to spin around, 'hit' to slap the desk).
 3) When the teacher calls 'grab', quickly snatch the team pinny in the center.
 4) The player who grabs it and waves it overhead first wins.

1) Complete up-stacking and down-stacking of the 3-6-3 combination.
 2) Transition to the 6-6 stack, perform up-stacking and down-stacking to consolidate into a 12-cup column.
 3) Perform up-stacking of the 1-10-1 stack and slide down-stack diagonally to finish in the 3-6-3 layout.
플라잉디스크 백핸드 그립 및 짝과 주고받기
Flying Disc Backhand Grip and Catching Relay

1) Form a backhand grip with thumb on top and remaining fingers holding the disc.
 2) Turn slightly sideways and throw towards a partner using wrist snap from the belly area.
 3) Catch the disc using one of three methods: pancake (hamburger) catch, two-handed trap, or one-handed catch.
 4) Work with a partner to successfully throw and catch 10 times in a row.

1) The batter throws a flying disc, picks up spot markers in the field, and steps on home base to score.
 2) Fielders catch the disc and either step on home base first or pass it to get an out.
 3) Teams switch offense and defense after 3 outs.
Flying disc, spot markers, base, cones

1) Divide into a team wearing vests and a team without vests.
 2) The team scores 1 point by successfully making 5 consecutive passes to teammates.
 3) After scoring, possession goes to the opposing team.
 4) Players must pass within 3 seconds, and opponents can only intercept while the ball is passed.
 5) If intercepted, the pass count resets to zero.
 6) The team with more points at the end of 5 minutes wins.

1) Teams are assigned base colors and throw balls to hit opponents.
 2) When hitting an opponent, take a required color from them.
 3) Teammates can share colors and pass the ball to each other.
 4) The team that collects all 6 colors first wins.

1) The runner straps the parachute around their waist behind the cone while a teammate may hold the parachute.
 2) On start signal, run forward around the turning point and return.
 3) Runners must keep the parachute buckled at the waist and never carry it with their hands.
 4) Hand off the parachute after a high-five tag, and finished runners sit down to the side to avoid collisions.
미니 허들, 라바콘, 링 배턴, 천막(터널), 평균대 매트, 스텝래더

1) The first runner starts and jumps over consecutive mini hurdles.
 2) Weave through the cones in a zigzag pattern.
 3) Crawl through the cloth tunnel and balance across the balance beam.
 4) Step through the agility ladder one rung at a time and pass the baton or place the ring on the cone.
Mini hurdles, cones, ring batons, cloth tunnel, balance beam, agility ladder

1) The fielding team takes positions in the infield while the batting team prepares to kick and run.
 2) The kicker kicks the ball and runs toward first base, while baserunners advance according to the play.
 3) Fielders record an out by catching the ball in the air or touching a base for a force out or tag out.
 4) Three fouls result in an out, and teams switch sides after three outs.
Classroom Desk Mini Table Tennis Doubles

1) Form pairs of two players on each side of joined desks for a doubles match.
 2) Serve diagonally from right to right, alternating turns after every two serves.
 3) The player who serves or hits the ball must immediately switch positions with their partner.
 4) A player cannot hit the ball twice consecutively, and the game is played up to 11 points (a two-point lead is required at deuce).
Padminton rackets, table tennis ball, classroom desks
Foot Flying Disc Target Knockout Game

1) Mark a boundary line with cones and place flying discs inside the area.
 2) Play rock-paper-scissors to determine who kicks first.
 3) Use feet instead of hands to kick the disc toward the opponent's disc.
 4) The player who knocks the opponent's disc completely outside the designated boundary line wins.

1) Both teams wait against their respective walls and rush to the center to grab team vests upon the start signal.
 2) Players throw the captured team vests to hit opponent players.
 3) If a thrown team vest hits the floor, the thrower or hit player is out and must move to a spot marker outside.
 4) If a teammate catches a flying team vest directly, an eliminated teammate can be revived and return to play.

1) Instead of batting, the thrower tosses the ball by hand to practice defense.
 2) The ball is thrown as a grounder, fly ball, or on one bounce to simulate real game situations.
 3) The runner sprints toward the bases immediately after throwing.
 4) Fielders catch the ball and throw it to the nearest base to make an out.
원 둘레 달리기와 농구 패스 대결
Circle Run vs Basketball Pass Race

1) Students form a circle while one runner holding a ball starts outside the circle.
 2) On the signal, the outside runner sprints around the perimeter of the circle.
 3) While the runner is sprinting, students in the circle quickly pass the ball to the adjacent teammate around the circle.
 4) Check whether the runner returns to the start first or the ball completes the circle first.

1) Mark a 15-meter running distance and pair students into runners and counters.
 2) Run from the start line to the opposite line in time with the beep audio cues.
 3) Reach the line before the next beep sounds and turn back to run again.
 4) Stop when failing to reach the line twice within the signal, and record the final count.
경사 매트 활용 뒤구르기 단계별 연습
Backward Roll Practice Using an Inclined Mat

1) Practice placing hands on the mat while keeping the chest close to the thighs and raising the heels.
 2) Fold the mat in half to create an incline and stand at the top of the slope.
 3) Roll backward like a ball without straightening the legs and push the mat with both hands to land.
Desk and Chair Cup Basketball Game

1) Place chairs closely behind desks to set up target areas.
 2) Practice bouncing the ball with a one-bounce shot into the target.
 3) Modify the game to throw directly into the target without bouncing.
 4) Team members take turns shooting and quickly retrieving the ball.

1) The first runner circles the first spot in a straight line and tags the next teammate.
 2) The second, third, and fourth runners run around their designated spots in order.
 3) The last runner races to hook or hang the marker first, and the team that hangs it first wins.

1) Divide into a vest team and a non-vest team.
 2) The team that successfully makes 5 consecutive passes scores 1 point.
 3) After scoring or on a turnover/missed pass, possession goes to the opposing team.
 4) Players must not hold the ball for more than 3 seconds and cannot stand up.
계란판 탁구공 원바운드 넣기 및 빙고 놀이
Egg Carton Table Tennis Ball One-Bounce Bingo

1) Place an egg carton in the center of the desk and bounce table tennis balls with one bounce into it.
 2) Decide turns with rock-paper-scissors or throw alternately using one bounce.
 3) The first player to complete a 3-in-a-row bingo horizontally, vertically, or diagonally wins.
 4) If all 5 balls are placed without making bingo, remove one ball at a time and throw again.
Badminton Short and Long Serve Practice

1) Hold the racket with a backhand grip, placing your thumb along the grip.
 2) Pinch the shuttlecock feathers with thumb and index finger, placing it near the racket face.
 3) Practice alternating between short serves and deep long serves using consistent form.
 4) Pull the racket head back to create shoulder space before hitting.
스태킹 컵 엘리베이터 및 탑 쌓기 놀이
Cup Stacking Elevator and Pyramid Challenge

1) Pick up cups with both hands, form a semi-circle, and gather them toward the body.
 2) Play the elevator game by moving the star-marked cup from bottom to top one by one.
 3) Stack cups by placing 6 at the bottom and 5 in the center.

1) Each team positions players across the court, such as two in front and three in the back.
 2) The server starts play by throwing the ball over the net from behind the service line.
 3) The receiving team passes the ball within the team up to three times before throwing it back.
 4) The player holding the ball cannot run, and the ball must be thrown upwards rather than spiked downward.
 5) Dropping a pass or committing a fault awards a point to the opposing team.
셔틀콕 공 멀리 던지기 기본 기능 익히기

1) Step right foot forward, raise elbow above the ear, and throw forward extending the elbow as if clearing a high net.
 2) Step right foot back and practice throwing utilizing waist rotation, shoulder, elbow, and wrist.
 3) Step right foot back, lift left foot, and step forward to throw using weight transfer from back to front.
 4) Step further back behind yellow and white lines to hit target wall and increase distance.

1) Place hands on body parts called out (1 Head, 2 Shoulders, 3 Waist, 4 Hips, 5 Knees).
 2) On the cue 'Catch', run quickly and pull the flying disc using feet.
 3) Players who miss also return to their spot, and discs must be returned to center using only feet.

1) Assign runners progressively longer distances corresponding to court lines 1, 2, 3, 4, and the far wall.
 2) On the start signal, runners sprint sequentially to their designated line or wall, touch it, and run back to hand off the ring baton.
 3) The final runner sprints to touch the far wall, runs back, and loops the ring baton over the cone to win.
 4) Runners who have finished must immediately sit down quietly at the back of their team's line.

1) Both teams stand in a 3-3-3 zigzag formation and determine the serve order.
 2) Catch the served ball using a scoop, pass it to teammates, and throw it over to the opponent court.
 3) The player holding the ball cannot move and must pass or throw from that spot.
 4) A point is scored when the opposing team fails to catch the ball, and the scoring team continues serving.

1) Divide the class into four teams (A, B, C, D) and assign each to a designated corner area.
 2) Throw balls to eliminate players from other teams while avoiding getting hit.
 3) Eliminated players must step outside their team zone and attempt to hit players from opposing teams.
 4) The team with the most surviving players within the time limit wins.

1) Alternate right and left hands to build pyramid stacks using three cups (upstack).
 2) Collapse the cups back down from right to left using alternating hands (downstack).
 3) Complete and pack down the 3-3-3 formation quickly upon signal.

1) Divide into teams wearing vests and teams without vests.
 2) Hit opponents inside the court with the ball within the time limit.
 3) Hit players move to the designated area behind the opposing team.
 4) When an eliminated player is present, inside players get out if they step outside to retrieve balls.

1) Defending players step on inside bases while offensive runners step on outside bases, and bolus stays on the opposite side.
 2) The game proceeds with an all-batter format instead of a three-out system.
 3) Remember the position of runners left on base before switching sides and resume from there on the next offensive turn.
 4) Throwing the bat results in an out.

1) Each student places a spot marker (pizza) flat on their hand as a delivery worker.
 2) Move around the play area and try to knock down other players' markers.
 3) Players are out if they touch someone's body, drop their own marker, or step out of bounds.
 4) The last player remaining with their pizza wins.
교실 책상 사이 자유투 농구 게임
Classroom Desk Free Throw Basketball Game

1) Students sit on the floor in teams waiting in order from person number one.
 2) On their turn players throw a ball from a seated position into the space between desks.
 3) The thrower retrieves the ball and passes it to the next teammate in line.
 4) The team that makes the most shots wins and players place hands on heads when finished.

1) Players space out using spot markers, and player 1 passes the ball to player 2.
 2) Alternate between short and long passes, moving dynamically according to the ball trajectory.
 3) If a pass is dropped, repeat until successfully completed.
 4) After finishing a round, player 1 rotates to the back of the line to change leaders.

1) Hold the ball steady with the left hand like a tee without tossing it.
 2) Form a fist and make contact with the fleshy part of the hand.
 3) Swing the right arm back moderately and follow through forward.
 4) Practice serving facing a partner.

1) Both taggers and runners are allowed to move only a single step simultaneously when the tagger shouts "One step!".
 2) Any player who moves out of sync or takes two steps instead of one is immediately called out and leaves the field.
 3) Stepping outside the designated boundary line or being touched by a tagger results in elimination.
 4) Two taggers herd the runners like sheep to tag them until only the final two survivors remain.

1) Sit in a circle and roll a gymball toward the player in the center.
 2) If tagged by the ball, the player is out and replaced by the next player.
 3) In the second round, expand the circle and throw the ball to hit the center player.
 4) If the center player catches the thrown ball, the thrower must turn around to be hit on the back or legs.

1) Determine serve order by rock-paper-scissors; each player serves twice alternately, bouncing the ball once on their table then onto the opponent's.
 2) Catch the served ball using the cup.
 3) During rallies, hit the ball directly onto the opponent's desk without touching your own desk.
 4) If a player fails to return the ball properly or catch it with the cup, the opponent scores a point.

1) Taggers chase and touch fleeing players using foam sticks.
 2) Players directly caught by taggers go outside the court boundary to serve as referees.
 3) When about to be tagged, players clasp hands overhead shouting banana to freeze, and lower one hand when a teammate taps them.
 4) When another teammate taps them again, they are fully rescued to run, and taggers win if they catch everyone within 5 minutes.
농구 시간 내 최다 슛 성공 실기평가

1) Students choose their own shooting position and distance.
 2) Choose any shooting technique among jump shot, set shot, or layup shot.
 3) Shoot the ball within the given time limit.
 4) The score is evaluated based on the number of successful baskets made within the time limit.
줄넘기 응용 스텝 (앞뒤 흔들어 뛰기, 무릎 올려 뛰기, 360도 돌기)
Advanced Jump Rope Steps (Swing, High Knees, 360 Turn)

1) In swing step, alternate feet by kicking one back on count 1 and forward on count 2.
 2) In high knees step, lift each knee until the thigh forms a 90-degree angle.
 3) Complete one high knee repetition after 4 rope turns.
 4) For the 360-degree turn, divide the rotation into small angles and turn gradually.
PAPS 대비 윗몸 말아 올리기 기초 동작
Curl-Up Technique for Physical Fitness Testing

1) Lie down with knees bent at approximately 90 degrees and arms extended forward.
 2) Engage the abdominal muscles and curl the upper body upward reaching toward the knees.
 3) If struggling independently, have a partner hold the feet or brace feet under a sturdy base.
벽, 허리 높이 받침대, 무릎 높이 받침대

1) Set the basic plank posture keeping the body in a straight line from head to heels (or knees).
 2) Step 1: Stand and push against a wall.
 3) Step 2: Perform push-ups with hands placed at waist height.
 4) Step 3: Perform push-ups with hands at knee height; Step 4: Perform push-ups on the floor (with knees on the ground if needed).
Noiseless Lower Body Power Training at Home

1) Stand facing a wall and perform calf raises rapidly without your heels touching the floor roughly.
 2) Set feet 5–15 degrees apart and perform seated squats on a chair or quick-tempo tension squats at knee level.
 3) Place one foot on a chair or sofa and perform split squats alternately on both legs.
 4) Rest shoulders on a sofa with toes raised, lowering and explosively lifting your hips for hip thrusts.

1) Select and arrange 7 different jump rope footwork skills into a personalized continuous routine.
 2) Start with foundational steps such as 15 basic jumps and 10 alternate-foot steps.
 3) Transition smoothly without stopping into side straddle cross jumps, forward-backward swings, and 360-degree turning jumps.
 4) Complete advanced skills such as criss-cross jumps (5-10 reps) and double unders (10-20 reps) continuously to clear all 7 levels.

1) Interlock fingers and stretch arms upward and backward.
 2) Lean the torso slowly to the left and right while keeping fingers interlocked.
 3) Extend one arm across the chest and pull it close using the opposite elbow.
 4) Raise one arm behind the head and gently pull the elbow down with the opposite hand.

1) Set up a badminton net on a badminton court with 6 players per team (or adjusted numbers).
 2) Serve underhand without stepping on the service line; play continues even if the serve hits the net.
 3) Pass or return the ball to the opponent court in 1 to 5 touches, and using feet is allowed during play.
 4) The team that wins 2 out of 3 sets wins the match, while touching an out ball or returning a serve directly with an overhand results in a lost point.

1) Set up the badminton court and net, with two players on each side for a doubles match.
 2) Start the rally using a short or long serve diagonally into the opponent's service court.
 3) Continue the rally by executing various strokes such as high clears, drops, smashes, pushes, and drives.
 4) A point is scored when the shuttlecock lands on the court floor or out of bounds.

1) From attention stance, squat down and place hands on the floor shoulder-width apart.
 2) Jump both feet back into a plank position with the body in a straight line.
 3) Jump feet back in toward hands into the squat position.
 4) Use momentum to jump straight up into the air to complete one repetition.

1) For the forehand serve, place the racket-side foot back, hold the shuttlecock between waist and chest, drop it without tossing, and hit it high and far.
 2) For the backhand serve, put the racket-side foot forward, position the shuttlecock below 115cm, draw the racket back, and push gently.
 3) The shuttlecock must be struck below 115cm from the floor (around the chest).
관절 부상 없는 안전한 줄넘기 기본자세 및 모아뛰기 500회 도전
Safe Basic Jump Rope Posture and 500-Bounce Challenge

1) Fold the rope in half, step on the center with one foot, and adjust the handles to chest/pit-of-stomach height.
 2) Stand straight, slightly raise the heels, and bend the knees to absorb landing impacts.
 3) Keep arms close to the torso and turn the rope lightly using only wrists while bouncing gently.
 4) Challenge yourself to complete 500 consecutive basic jumps at a pace of 100 jumps per minute.
체력 향상 줄넘기(1회선 2도약, 모아뛰기, 외발뛰기, 번갈아뛰기)

1) Divide the skills into groups A through G and write down the order of your choice on the evaluation sheet.
 2) In Group A, perform 10 repetitions of two-bounce jumping and 10 repetitions of basic bounce jumping.
 3) In Group B, perform single-foot jump (5 each), alternate-foot jump (5 times), and alternate double-bounce jump (3 each).
 4) Practice the assigned jump rope movements to build physical fitness.

1) Divide into two teams, stack jumbo stacks in two rows in front of each team, and set up a model target pattern behind a screen partition.
 2) On signal, one runner from each team runs behind the partition to observe the colors and arrangement of the target stack.
 3) Return to the team and place one matching jumbo stack, with each player allowed to move only one cup per turn (or fix one misplaced cup).
 4) High-five the next runner before they can start, and the team that perfectly matches the target stack first wins.

1) All players gather and stand in a circular formation.
 2) One player in the center spins a water bottle on the floor.
 3) The player pointed to by the tip of the bottle when it stops becomes the runner.
 4) The chosen runner immediately flees while everyone else chases them within 10 seconds.

1) Divide players into 2 teams; the first runner of each team holds a handball and starts on the signal.
 2) Upon reaching the goal area line, shoot into the handball goal.
 3) After one shot attempt, quickly run back and hand the ball to the next runner to continue the relay.
 4) Goals scored into an already completed target hole do not count; the team that fills all target holes first wins.
Badminton Doubles Court Rules and Service

1) Decide the initial service order by a toss before the match starts.
 2) The server serves diagonally from the right court when the score is zero or even, and from the left court when odd.
 3) Deliver the service hit below a height of 1.15 meters from the floor.
 4) Score a point when the shuttlecock lands within the opponent's boundary, and concede a point if it goes out or hits the net.

1) Determine the first server by a toss and serve diagonally from the right court at 0-0
 2) Serve diagonally from the right court when the serving side's score is even (including 0) and from the left court when odd
 3) Only when the serving team wins a rally and scores consecutively do partners switch service courts and the same player serves again
 4) When winning the serve back from the opponent, players do not switch sides; the player standing in the court corresponding to their score serves

 2) Practice opening the feet shoulder-width apart and closing them across four beats.
 3) Jump lightly just as the rope approaches right in front of your feet.
 4) Turn the rope to the rhythm and continuously perform the open-and-close jumps.

1) Stretch the right thigh, then stretch the other leg.
 2) Hold ankles and repeat sitting down and standing up.
 3) Tap toes while extending arms, raise elbows, and tap up and down.
 4) Stretch legs while seated, then stand up and interlock fingers to stretch upward.

1) Push the chair back to make room between the desk and chair, and gently warm up the neck and shoulders.
 2) Keep feet on the floor, bring knees together, hold the lower chair back, open the chest, and hold Camel Pose for 10 seconds.
 3) Round the spine inward looking at the belly button and hold Cat Pose for 10 seconds.
 4) Perform Chair Pose hovering slightly off the seat, Crescent Pose bending to each side, knee-to-chest pulls, and finish with Child's Pose.

1) Sit properly on a chair in front of the desk and wait for the music.
 2) Follow the rhythmic upper-body choreography to the song 'Balloons'.
 3) Float or wave balloons with both hands during the chorus or ending part to express freely.
Namsaeng Play Traditional Rhythm and Movement

1) Partners face each other holding hands and step in rhythm to Jajinmori jangdan while singing the traditional song 'Play Namsaeng'.
 2) Change the lyrics to movement words such as jumping, wiggling, fluttering, or moving slowly.
 3) Create and perform corresponding body movements along with the new descriptive words in time with the rhythm.

1) Perform reverse lunges alternating right and left legs.
 2) Do jumping jacks and forward crawl walkouts from standing.
 3) Perform burpees and starfish crunches touching alternating hands and feet while lying down.
 4) Complete superman holds, skate jumps, no-hands sit-ups, and punch-kick combinations.

1) Perform jumping jacks in place.
 2) Perform high-knee running by lifting knees up toward the waist.
 3) Perform cross-jumping by opening and crossing arms and legs.
 4) Continue with butt kicks, jump squats, and lunges.
배드민턴 라켓 2개, 셔틀콕, 팀 조끼, 목표 기록 표

1) Divide the class into 2 teams and put on team vests.
 2) Write down the names of team members and each member's target number of shuttlecock hits on a score sheet.
 3) Players take turns stepping forward to hit the shuttlecock without dropping it until their target number is reached before passing the racket to the next player.

 4) Resume jogging once arriving at the next green sign and continue around the loop.
